title.zh: 卷二十八 魏書二十八 王毌丘諸葛鄧鍾傳
title.en: Volume 28: Book of Wei 28 - Biographies of Wang, Guanqiu, Zhuge, Deng and Zhong
title.raw: 卷二十八 魏書二十八 王毌丘諸葛鄧鍾傳 Volume 28: Book of Wei 28 - Biographies of Wang, Guanqiu, Zhuge, Deng and Zhong

sentences.zh: 王凌 毌丘儉 諸葛誕 鄧艾 鍾會

translations.literal: Wang Ling, Guanqiu Jian, Zhuge Dan, Deng Ai, Zhong Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling, Guanqiu Jian, Zhuge Dan, Deng Ai, and Zhong Hui.

sentences.zh: 王凌字彥雲，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Ling, courtesy name Yan Yun, was a man of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling, styled Yan Yun, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 叔父允，為漢司徒，誅董卓。

translations.literal: His uncle Wang Yun served as Minister of Education of Han and killed Dong Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Wang Yun served the Han as Minister over the Masses and executed Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓將李傕、郭汜等為卓報仇，入長安，殺允，盡害其家。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo's generals Li Jue, Guo Si, and others avenged Zhuo, entered Chang'an, killed Wang Yun, and massacred his entire household.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's officers Li Jue and Guo Si, among others, avenged their master: they entered Chang'an, put Wang Yun to death, and slaughtered his whole family.

sentences.zh: 凌及兄晨，時年皆少，逾城得脫，亡命歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Ling and his elder brother Chen, both young at the time, climbed over the city wall and escaped, fleeing for their lives back to their native place.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling and his older brother Wang Chen were still boys; they scaled the wall and escaped, then fled incognito to their home district.

sentences.zh: 凌舉孝廉，為發干長，

translations.literal: Ling was recommended as filial and incorrupt and became magistrate of Fagan,
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling was nominated as filial and incorrupt and appointed magistrate of Fagan county,

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：凌為長，遇事，髡刑五歲，當道掃除。

translations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei says: When Ling was magistrate, he became involved in an affair and was sentenced to shaved-head punishment for five years, sweeping the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei relates that while he was county magistrate he ran afoul of the law and was sentenced to five years of shaved-head penal labor sweeping the streets.

sentences.zh: 時太祖車過，問此何徒，左右以狀對。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Progenitor's carriage passed by; he asked what sort of men these were, and his attendants explained the situation.
translations.idiomatic: As Cao Cao's carriage passed, he asked who these laborers were, and his attendants explained what had happened.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「此子師兄子也，所坐亦公耳。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "This youth is my teacher's nephew; what he was punished for was also for the public good."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "This young man is my mentor's nephew; his offense was committed in the state's interest."

sentences.zh: 」於是主者選為驍騎主簿。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon the responsible official selected him as secretary of the Swift Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities thereupon appointed him secretary of the Swift Cavalry corps.

sentences.zh: 稍遷至中山太守，所在有治，太祖辟為丞相掾屬。

translations.literal: Gradually promoted to governor of Zhongshan, wherever he served there was good order; the Grand Progenitor summoned him as an aide in the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to governor of Zhongshan, earning a reputation for capable administration until Cao Cao recruited him as an aide in the Chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 文帝踐阼，拜散騎常侍，出為兗州刺史，與張遼等至廣陵討孫權。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, [Wang Ling] was appointed irregular cavalry attendant-in-ordinary, went out as Inspector of Yan Province, and with Zhang Liao and others went to Guangling to campaign against Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen took the throne, Wang Ling was named attendant at irregular cavalry, then posted out as inspector of Yan Province; he joined Zhang Liao and others at Guangling for the expedition against Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 臨江，夜大風，吳將呂範等船漂至北岸。

translations.literal: They drew near the river; at night a great wind blew, and the ships of Wu generals such as Lü Fan drifted to the north bank.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the Yangzi, a gale blew up that night and drove the vessels of Wu officers including Lü Fan onto the northern shore.

sentences.zh: 凌與諸將逆擊，捕斬首虜，獲舟船，有功，封宜城亭侯，加建武將軍，轉在青州。

translations.literal: Ling with the various generals attacked them head-on, capturing and beheading enemy heads and prisoners, seizing boats and ships; for merit he was enfeoffed as marquis of Yicheng village, promoted general who establishes martial prowess, and transferred to Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling and the Wei commanders counterattacked: they took heads and prisoners, seized enemy craft, and Wang Ling was rewarded with the village marquisate of Yicheng, the title general who establishes martial prowess, and a transfer to Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 是時海濱乘喪亂之後，法度未整。

translations.literal: At this time along the coast, riding on the aftermath of turmoil and bereavement, regulations were not yet put in order.
translations.idiomatic: The coastal regions had yet to recover their laws and institutions after the chaos of war.

sentences.zh: 凌布政施教，賞善罰惡，甚有綱紀，百姓稱之，不容於口。

translations.literal: Ling spread policy and taught; he rewarded good and punished evil, and had very good discipline; the common people praised him without restraint from their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling governed with clear rewards and punishments and firm standards of conduct; the people praised him ceaselessly.

sentences.zh: 後從曹休征吳，與賊遇於夾石，休軍失利，凌力戰決圍，休得免難。

translations.literal: Later he followed Cao Xiu in campaigning against Wu; they met the enemy at Jiashi; Xiu's army suffered defeat; Ling fought hard and broke the encirclement, and Xiu was able to escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He later accompanied Cao Xiu against Wu; at Jiashi Cao Xiu's army was routed, but Wang Ling fought his way through the encirclement and saved Cao Xiu from disaster.

sentences.zh: 仍徙為揚、豫州刺史，咸得軍民之歡心。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was transferred to be Inspector of Yang and Yu Provinces; in both he won the hearts of soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: He was then moved to successive postings as inspector of Yang and of Yu, winning the goodwill of soldiers and civilians in each.

sentences.zh: 始至豫州，旌先賢之後，求未顯之士，各有條教，意義甚美。

translations.literal: When he first arrived in Yu Province, he honored the descendants of former worthies and sought out scholars not yet distinguished; each had regulations and teachings, and the intent and meaning were very fine.
translations.idiomatic: On first reaching Yu he singled out the heirs of noted men of old, sought obscure talent, and issued well-crafted directives—policy that was as admirable in spirit as in letter.

sentences.zh: 初，凌與司馬朗、賈逵友善，及臨兗、豫，繼其名跡。

translations.literal: Earlier Ling had been friendly with Sima Lang and Jia Kui; when he came to Yan and Yu, he continued their reputations and traces.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling had long been on good terms with Sima Lang and Jia Kui; once he governed Yan and Yu, he was seen as walking in their footsteps.

sentences.zh: 正始初，為征東將軍，假節都督揚州諸軍事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhengshi era he became general who conquers the east, was given the credential insignia, and superintended military affairs of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengshi period he was named general who conquers the east, invested with the jie staff as commander-in-chief of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 二年，吳大將全琮數万眾寇芍陂，凌率諸軍逆討，與賊爭塘，力戰連日，賊退走。

translations.literal: In the second year, Wu general Quan Zong with several tens of thousands raided Shaopi; Ling led the various armies to oppose and attack them, contended with the bandits over the embankment, fought hard for successive days, and the bandits withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the era, Quan Zong of Wu led tens of thousands against the Shaopi reservoir; Wang Ling took the field, contested the dikes day after day, and drove the enemy back.

sentences.zh: 進封南鄉侯，邑千三百五十戶，遷車騎將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was advanced in enfeoffment to marquis of Nanxiang, with a fief of one thousand three hundred fifty households; he was promoted to chariot-and-cavalry general, with ceremonial parity of the three offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to marquis of Nanxiang with a fief of 1,350 households, then promoted to chariot-and-cavalry general with honors matching the three senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 令狐愚

translations.literal: Linghu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Yu.

sentences.zh: 宣王遂至壽春。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xuan then arrived at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi, Prince of Xuan, marched into Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 張式等皆自首，乃窮治其事。

translations.literal: Zhang Shi and others all surrendered themselves; thereupon the matter was thoroughly prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi and others turned themselves in, and the entire conspiracy was investigated to the end.

sentences.zh: 彪賜死，諸相連者悉夷三族。

translations.literal: Biao was granted death; all connected persons were exterminated to the third degree.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Biao was compelled to take his own life, and everyone implicated was executed along with three generations of kin.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》載：山陽單固，字恭夏，為人有器實。

translations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei records: Shan Gu of Shanyang, courtesy name Gongxia, as a man had substance and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei introduces Shan Gu of Shanyang, styled Gongxia, as a man of solid ability.

sentences.zh: 正始中，兗州刺史令狐愚與固父伯龍善，辟固​​，欲以為別駕。

translations.literal: In Zhengshi, Inspector of Yan Province Linghu Yu was on good terms with Gu's father Bolong; he summoned Gu, wishing to appoint him provincial aide.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengshi, Linghu Yu, inspector of Yan Province, was close to Gu's father Bolong; he recruited Shan Gu and meant to install him as provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 固不樂為州吏，辭以疾。

translations.literal: Gu was not pleased to serve as a provincial clerk and declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Gu had no wish to serve on the provincial staff and pleaded illness to refuse.

sentences.zh: 愚禮意愈厚，固不欲應。

translations.literal: Yu grew ever more earnest in courtesy; Gu still did not wish to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Yu pressed him with ever greater courtesy, yet Shan Gu would not yield.

sentences.zh: 固母夏侯氏謂固曰：「使君與汝父久善，故命汝不止，汝亦故當仕進，自可往耳。

translations.literal: Gu's mother, née Xiahou, said to Gu: "The inspector has long been on good terms with your father; therefore he summons you without cease; you likewise ought to advance in office—you may simply go."
translations.idiomatic: His mother, of the Xiahou clan, told him: "The inspector and your father have been friends for years—that is why he keeps calling for you. You ought to take office in any case; go."

sentences.zh: 」固不獲已，遂往，與兼治中從事楊康並為愚腹心。

translations.literal: Gu could not refuse further; he went, and together with Yang Kang, concurrently clerk of the bureau of administration, both became Yu's trusted intimates.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refuse further, he went and, alongside Yang Kang of the provincial bureau staff, became one of Linghu Yu's inner circle.

sentences.zh: 後愚與王凌通謀，康、固皆知其計。

translations.literal: Later Yu plotted with Wang Ling; Kang and Gu both knew the plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Linghu Yu later conspired with Wang Ling, Yang Kang and Shan Gu were both privy to the plot.

sentences.zh: 會愚病，康應司徒召詣洛陽，固亦以疾解祿。

translations.literal: When Yu fell ill, Kang responded to the Minister of Education's summons and went to Luoyang; Gu also resigned his stipend on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Yu then fell ill; Yang Kang obeyed the minister of education's summons to Luoyang, while Shan Gu resigned his post, again citing sickness.

sentences.zh: 康在京師露其事，太傅乃東取王凌。

translations.literal: In the capital Kang exposed the affair; the Grand Tutor then moved east to seize Wang Ling.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital Yang Kang revealed what he knew, whereupon the grand tutor marched east against Wang Ling.

sentences.zh: 到壽春，固見太傅，太傅問曰：「卿知其事為邪？

translations.literal: Arriving at Shouchun, Gu met the Grand Tutor; the Grand Tutor asked: "Do you know this affair to be true?"
translations.idiomatic: At Shouchun, Shan Gu was brought before the grand tutor, who asked: "Were you aware that this plot was real?"

sentences.zh: 」固對不知。

translations.literal: Gu replied that he did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Gu said he had not known.

sentences.zh: 太傅曰：「且置近事。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor said: "For the moment set aside recent matters.
translations.idiomatic: The grand tutor said, "Set aside what just happened for now.

sentences.zh: 問卿，令狐反乎？

translations.literal: I ask you: did Linghu rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Tell me—did Linghu Yu rebel?"

sentences.zh: 」固又曰無。

translations.literal: Gu again said no.
translations.idiomatic: Again Shan Gu denied it.

sentences.zh: 而楊康白，事事與固連。

translations.literal: But Yang Kang informed [against him]; each matter connected Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kang then informed, linking Shan Gu to every detail.

sentences.zh: 遂收捕固及家屬，皆係廷尉，考實數十，固故云無有。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gu and his family members were seized and arrested, all bound over to the Minister of Justice; they interrogated and verified dozens of times, yet Gu insisted there was nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Gu and his kin were taken into custody and handed to the minister of justice; though questioned repeatedly, he still insisted he knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 太傅錄楊康，與固對相詰。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor brought in Yang Kang to confront Gu with mutual questioning.
translations.idiomatic: The grand tutor had Yang Kang brought in to confront Shan Gu face to face.

sentences.zh: 固辭窮，乃罵康曰：「老庸既負使君，又滅我族，顧汝當活邪！

translations.literal: Gu's words failed; then he cursed Kang: "Old mediocrity—you have betrayed the inspector and also destroyed my clan—do you expect to live?"
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Shan Gu turned on Yang Kang: "You worthless old fool—you betrayed your lord and wiped out my family—do you think you will survive?"

sentences.zh: 」辭定，事上，須報廷尉，以舊皆聽得與其母妻子相見。

translations.literal: When the testimony was settled, the matter went up; awaiting reply from the Minister of Justice, according to precedent all were permitted to see their mothers, wives, and children.
translations.idiomatic: Once his confession was recorded and sent up, they awaited the minister of justice's ruling; by old practice prisoners could still visit mother, wife, and children.

sentences.zh: 固見其母，不仰視，其母知其慚也，字謂之曰：「恭夏，汝本自不欲應州郡也，我強故耳。

translations.literal: When Gu saw his mother, he did not look up; his mother knew his shame and by his courtesy name said to him: "Gongxia, you originally yourself did not wish to answer the provincial summons—it was I who forced you.
translations.idiomatic: When he faced his mother he could not lift his eyes; she knew his shame and called him by his style: "Gongxia, you never wanted that provincial appointment—I pushed you into it."

sentences.zh: 汝為人吏，自當爾耳。

translations.literal: You became another man's clerk—it should be thus.
translations.idiomatic: You chose to serve as an official—what happened follows from that."

sentences.zh: 此自門戶衰，我無恨也。

translations.literal: This is our household's decline—I have no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: If our house falls, I bear no grudge.

sentences.zh: 汝本意與我語。

translations.literal: Your original intent was to speak with me.
translations.idiomatic: You meant to speak with me before the end."

sentences.zh: 」固終不仰，又不語，以至於死。

translations.literal: Gu to the end did not look up, nor speak, until death.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Gu never raised his eyes nor uttered another word—so he went to his death.

sentences.zh: 初，楊康自以白其事，冀得封拜，後以辭頗參錯，亦並斬。

translations.literal: Earlier Yang Kang thought by exposing the affair he would obtain enfeoffment and appointment; afterward because his testimony was somewhat inconsistent, he too was beheaded with the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kang had hoped his confession would win him honors; when his story proved inconsistent, he was executed alongside the others.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，俱出獄，固又罵康曰：「老奴，汝死自分耳。

translations.literal: Facing execution, both came out of prison; Gu again cursed Kang: "Old slave—your death is your own portion.
translations.idiomatic: On the way to execution both men were led from jail; Shan Gu cursed Yang Kang again: "Slave—you chose your own death.

sentences.zh: 若令死者有知，汝何面目以行地下也。」〉

translations.literal: If the dead have awareness, with what face would you walk under the earth?"
translations.idiomatic: If the dead have any knowledge, what face would you have in the underworld?"

sentences.zh: 朝議咸以為春秋之義，齊崔杼、鄭歸生皆加追戮，陳屍斫棺，載在方策。

translations.literal: Court deliberation all held that by the meaning of the Spring and Autumn, Qi Cui Zhu and Zheng Guisheng both received posthumous punishment: corpses displayed and coffins hacked—recorded on tablets and bamboo slips.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that Spring and Autumn precedent justified posthumous punishment Cui Zhu of Qi and Guisheng of Zheng had suffered—exposing the corpse and splintering the coffin, as the classics record.

sentences.zh: 凌、愚罪宜如舊典。

translations.literal: The crimes of Ling and Yu ought to follow the old norms.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling and Linghu Yu deserved the same ancient penalties.

sentences.zh: 乃發凌、愚塚，剖棺，暴屍於所近市三日，燒其印綬、朝服，親土埋之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they opened the tombs of Ling and Yu, split the coffins, exposed the corpses in the nearest market for three days, burned their seals and ribbons and court robes, and buried them with earth by hand.
translations.idiomatic: Their graves were opened, the coffins broken open, and the bodies displayed three days in the nearest town; seals, court dress, and ribbons were burned, and what remained was covered with bare earth.

sentences.zh: 〈干寶《晉紀》曰：兗州武吏東平馬隆，託為愚家客，以私財更殯葬，行服三年，種植松柏。

translations.literal: Gan Bao's Annals of Jin says: Ma Long of Dongping, a military clerk of Yan Province, posed as a retainer of Yu's household, used private wealth again to bury them, observed mourning three years, and planted pines and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao records that Ma Long, a Yan Province clerk from Dongping, passed himself off as Linghu Yu's retainer, paid for a second burial from his own purse, mourned three years, and planted pine and cypress at the grave.

sentences.zh: 一州之士愧之。〉

translations.literal: The gentlemen of the whole province were shamed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of learning across the province were put to shame by his integrity.

sentences.zh: 進弘、華爵為鄉侯。

translations.literal: Hong and Hua were advanced in rank to village marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong and Wang Hua were promoted to village marquises.

sentences.zh: 廣有志尚學行，死時年四十餘。

translations.literal: Guang had aspirations and scholarly conduct; at death his age was over forty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guang was a man of ambition and learning; he was a little over forty when he died.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：廣字公淵。

translations.literal: The Annals of the House of Wei says: Guang's courtesy name was Gong Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei chronicle gives Wang Guang's style as Gong Yuan.

sentences.zh: 弟飛梟、金虎，並才武過人。

translations.literal: Younger brothers Feixiao and Jinhu both had martial talent surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Wang Feixiao and Wang Jinhu were both formidable fighters.

sentences.zh: 太傅嘗從容問蔣濟，濟曰：「凌文武俱贍，當今無雙。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor once casually asked Jiang Ji; Ji said: "Ling in civil and military is both ample—in the present age without peer.
translations.idiomatic: The grand tutor once asked Jiang Ji for his opinion. Jiang said, "Wang Ling's abilities in civil and military affairs are unrivaled in our time;

sentences.zh: 廣等志力，有美於父耳。

translations.literal: Guang and the others in aspiration and strength—there is excellence compared to the father only.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guang and his brothers almost equal their father in resolve."

sentences.zh: 」退而悔之，告所親曰：「吾此言，滅人門宗矣。

translations.literal: Having withdrawn, he regretted it and told those close: "These words of mine will destroy people's gates and clans.
translations.idiomatic: When he had stepped aside, he regretted what he had said and told his confidants, "That compliment could wipe out whole families."

sentences.zh: 」《魏末傳》曰：凌少子字明山，最知名，善書，多技藝，人得其書，皆以為法。

translations.literal: " The Wei Final Traditions says: Ling's youngest son had courtesy name Mingshan; he was most renowned, skilled at writing, with many arts—people who obtained his writing all took it as model.
translations.idiomatic: The Traditions of Late Wei adds that Wang Ling's youngest son, styled Mingshan, was the best known of the brothers: he wrote a fine hand and possessed many talents, and others copied his brushwork as a standard.

sentences.zh: 走向太原，追軍及之，時有飛鳥集桑樹，隨枝低卬，舉弓射之即倒，追人乃止不復進。

translations.literal: He fled toward Taiyuan; pursuing troops overtook him; at that time a flying bird perched on a mulberry tree, lowering with the branches; he raised his bow and shot it and it fell at once; the pursuers then stopped and came no further.
translations.idiomatic: He ran toward Taiyuan until the pursuit caught up; a bird settled in a mulberry and dipped with the branch—he shot it down at once, and the chase halted.

sentences.zh: 明山投親家食，親家告吏，乃就執之。〉

translations.literal: Mingshan went to a relative by marriage to eat; the relative by marriage informed the officials, and thereupon he was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Mingshan sought food with in-laws, who denounced him to the authorities, and he was taken.

sentences.zh: 毌丘儉

translations.literal: Guanqiu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian.

sentences.zh: 青龍中，帝圖討遼東，以儉有幹策，徙為幽州刺史，加度遼將軍，使持節，護烏丸校尉。

translations.literal: In the Qinglong era the emperor planned to campaign against Liaodong; because Jian had expedients and strategies, he was transferred to be Inspector of You Province, promoted general who crosses the Liao, invested with the credential insignia, and protector-general of the Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: During Qinglong the emperor prepared an expedition against Liaodong; trusting Guanqiu Jian's judgment, he transferred him to You Province as inspector, named him general who crosses the Liao with jie authority, and put him in charge of the Wuhuan colonelcy.

sentences.zh: 率幽州諸軍至襄平，屯遼隧。

translations.literal: He led the various armies of You Province to Xiangping and encamped at Liaosui.
translations.idiomatic: He brought the You armies to Xiangping and camped at Liaosui.

sentences.zh: 右北平烏丸單于寇婁敦、遼西烏丸都督率眾王護留等，昔隨袁尚奔遼東者，率眾五千餘人降。

translations.literal: The Wuhuan chanyu Kou Loudun of Youbeiping, and Huliu of Liaoxi Wuhuan commissioner leading-the-host king who commands the masses, and others—those who formerly followed Yuan Shang in fleeing to Liaodong—led more than five thousand people and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Loudun, chanyu of the Youbeiping Wuhuan, and Huliu, the Liaoxi Wuhuan chief styled king who leads the host—men who had followed Yuan Shang into Liaodong—came in with more than five thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 寇婁敦遣弟阿羅槃等詣闕朝貢，封其渠率二十餘人為侯、王，賜輿馬繒採各有差。

translations.literal: Kou Loudun sent younger brother Aluo Pan and others to the court to pay tribute; more than twenty of their chieftains were enfeoffed as marquises and kings; carriages, horses, silk, and fabric were granted according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Loudun sent his brother Aluo Pan and others to court with tribute; over twenty Wuhuan leaders received marquisates or royal titles, with graded gifts of vehicles, horses, and silk.

sentences.zh: 公孫淵逆與儉戰，不利，引還。

translations.literal: Gongsun Yuan opposed Jian in battle, did not prevail, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yuan offered battle but lost and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝遣太尉司馬宣王統中軍及儉等眾數万討淵，定遼東。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor sent Grand Commandant Sima Yi to command the central army and Jian and others' hosts of several tens of thousands to campaign against Yuan and pacify Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor ordered Sima Yi, as grand commandant, to lead the central army and tens of thousands under Guanqiu Jian against Gongsun Yuan and secure Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 儉以功進封安邑侯，食邑三千九百戶。

translations.literal: Jian for merit was advanced in enfeoffment to marquis of Anyi, with a fief of three thousand nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in the victory Guanqiu Jian was ennobled as marquis of Anyi with a fief of 3,900 households.

sentences.zh: 正始中，儉以高句驪數侵叛，督諸軍步騎萬人出玄菟，從諸道討之。

translations.literal: In Zhengshi, because Gaogouli repeatedly invaded and rebelled, Jian superintended various armies of infantry and cavalry ten thousand strong out of Xuantu, campaigning against them by various routes.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengshi, Gaogouli having raided and rebelled repeatedly, Guanqiu Jian led ten thousand horse and foot out of Xuantu commandery along several routes.

sentences.zh: 句驪王宮將步騎二萬人，進軍沸流水上，大戰梁口，

translations.literal: The Gouli king Gong led infantry and cavalry twenty thousand strong, advanced the army on the Fei flowing water, and fought a great battle at Liang mouth,
translations.idiomatic: King Gong of Gaogouli brought twenty thousand men to the Feisui River and fought a major engagement at Liangkou.

sentences.zh: 〈梁音渴。〉

translations.literal: Liang is pronounced ke.
translations.idiomatic: The note reads liang with the same vowel as ke ("thirst").

sentences.zh: 宮連破走。

translations.literal: Gong was repeatedly defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was routed again and again and fled.

sentences.zh: 儉遂束馬縣車，以登丸都，屠句驪所都，斬獲首虜以千數。

translations.literal: Jian thereupon bound horses and suspended wagons to ascend Wandu, slaughtered Gouli's capital, and beheaded and captured heads and prisoners by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian then climbed the tortuous road to Wandu, sacked the Gaogouli capital, and took thousands of heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 句驪沛者名得來，數諫宮，

translations.literal: Gouli's peizhe was named Delai; he repeatedly remonstrated with Gong,
translations.idiomatic: A Gaogouli official titled peizhe named Delai repeatedly urged King Gong to reconsider.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之按東夷傳：沛者，句驪國之官名。〉

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi checks the Traditions of the Eastern Barbarians: peizhe is an official title of the Gouli state.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi cites the Eastern Yi treatise: peizhe is a Gaogouli office title.

sentences.zh: 宮不從其言。

translations.literal: Gong did not follow his words.
translations.idiomatic: The king ignored him.

sentences.zh: 得來歎曰：「立見此地將生蓬蒿。

translations.literal: Delai sighed and said: "Standing here I see this place about to grow wormwood.
translations.idiomatic: Delai sighed, "Before long this soil will be overgrown with weeds."

sentences.zh: 」遂不食而死，舉國賢之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he refused food and died; the whole state deemed him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: He starved himself to death, and the entire kingdom honored him as a worthy.

sentences.zh: 儉令諸軍不壞其墓，不伐其樹，得其妻子，皆放遣之。

translations.literal: Jian ordered the various armies not to destroy his tomb, not to cut his trees; those who captured his wife and children all released them.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian forbade his troops to disturb Delai's grave or fell his trees; anyone who seized his family let them go.

sentences.zh: 宮單將妻子逃竄。

translations.literal: Gong alone led wife and children and fled in hiding.
translations.idiomatic: King Gong fled with only his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 儉引軍還。

translations.literal: Jian led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 六年，复征之，宮遂奔買溝。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, again campaigning against him, Gong then fled to Maigou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year another expedition drove Gong as far as Maigou.

sentences.zh: 儉遣玄菟太守王頎追之，

translations.literal: Jian sent Governor of Xuantu Wang Qi to pursue him,
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian sent Wang Qi, governor of Xuantu, in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：頎字孔碩，東萊人，晉永嘉中大賊王彌，頎之孫。〉

translations.literal: The Sayings of the Age says: Qi's courtesy name was Kongshuo; he was a man of Donglai; in Jin's Yongjia era the great bandit Wang Mi was Qi's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Shishuo yinyu records Wang Qi, styled Kongshuo, from Donglai—his grandson was the notorious bandit Wang Mi of Western Jin.

sentences.zh: 過沃沮千有餘里，至肅慎氏南界，刻石紀功，刊丸都之山，銘不耐之城。

translations.literal: Passing Woju more than a thousand li, reaching the southern border of the Sushen clan, they carved stone to record merit, inscribed Mount Wandu, and inscribed the city of Naibu.
translations.idiomatic: They marched over a thousand li past Woju to the southern edge of Sushen territory, carved victory stelae on Mount Wandu and at Naibu city.

sentences.zh: 諸所誅納八千餘口，論功受賞，侯者百餘人。

translations.literal: In various places those executed and submitted numbered more than eight thousand persons; by merit discussion those receiving reward—marquises—were more than one hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: They killed or accepted the surrender of over eight thousand people; more than a hundred merited noble titles.

sentences.zh: 穿山溉灌，民賴其利。

translations.literal: They bored through mountains for irrigation; the people relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: They cut channels through hills for irrigation, to the people's lasting benefit.

sentences.zh: 遷左將軍，假節監豫州諸軍事，領豫州刺史，轉為鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted general of the left, given the credential insignia to supervise military affairs of Yu Province, concurrently Inspector of Yu Province, transferred to general who guards the south.
translations.idiomatic: He became general of the left with jie authority over Yu forces, served as inspector of Yu, then rotated to general who guards the south.

sentences.zh: 諸葛誕戰於東關，不利，乃令誕、儉對換。

translations.literal: Zhuge Dan fought at Dong Pass and did not prevail; thereupon Dan and Jian were ordered mutually exchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Dan's setback at Dong Pass, the court swapped his post with Guanqiu Jian's.

sentences.zh: 誕為鎮南，都督豫州。

translations.literal: Dan became general who guards the south, superintending Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan became general who guards the south and commanded Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 儉為鎮東，都督楊州。

translations.literal: Jian became general who guards the east, superintending Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian took the post of general who guards the east over Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 吳太傅諸葛恪圍合肥新城，儉與文欽御之，太尉司馬孚督中軍東解圍，恪退還。

translations.literal: Wu Grand Tutor Zhuge Ke besieged the new city of Hefei; Jian with Wen Qin resisted him; Grand Commandant Sima Fu superintended the central army eastward to lift the siege; Ke withdrew and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu's grand tutor Zhuge Ke invested Hefei's new fortress, Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin held him off until Grand Commandant Sima Fu led the central army east to break the siege and Zhuge Ke withdrew.

sentences.zh: 大將軍統中外軍討之，別使諸葛誕督豫州諸軍從安風津擬壽春，征東將軍胡遵督青、徐諸軍出於譙、宋之間，絕其歸路。

translations.literal: The Grand General commanded inner and outer armies to campaign against them; separately he ordered Zhuge Dan to superintend the Yu armies from Anfeng Ford toward Shouchun; general who conquers the east Hu Zun superintended Qing and Xu armies out between Qiao and Song, cutting off their return route.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general took command of all forces against the rebels: Zhuge Dan was to bring the Yu columns from Anfeng toward Shouchun, while Hu Zun, general who conquers the east, struck between Qiao and Song to sever their retreat.

sentences.zh: 大將軍屯汝陽，使監軍王基督前鋒諸軍據南頓以待之。

translations.literal: The Grand General encamped at Ruyang; he ordered army supervisor Wang Ji to command the vanguard armies to occupy Nandun and await them.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general camped at Ruyang and ordered Wang Ji to hold Nandun with the van and wait.

sentences.zh: 今諸軍皆堅壁勿與戰。

translations.literal: Now the various armies all fortify walls and do not engage in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Every column was ordered to stand on the defensive and refuse battle.

sentences.zh: 儉、欽進不得鬥，退恐壽春見襲，不得歸，計窮不知所為。

translations.literal: Jian and Qin advancing could not fight; retreating they feared Shouchun would be attacked; they could not return; stratagems exhausted, they knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin could neither advance to battle nor fall back without risking an attack on Shouchun; cut off from home, they were at their wits' end.

sentences.zh: 淮南將士，家皆在北，眾心沮散，降者相屬，惟淮南新附農民為之用。

translations.literal: The Huainan officers and soldiers—all their families were in the north; the host's hearts were dispirited and scattered; surrenderers followed one another; only Huainan's newly attached peasants served them.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan troops had kin north of the Huai; morale collapsed and men surrendered in chains—only recent settlers would still fight for them.

sentences.zh: 大將軍遣兗州刺史鄧艾督泰山諸軍萬餘人至樂嘉，示弱以誘之，大將軍尋自洙至。

translations.literal: The Grand General sent Inspector of Yan Province Deng Ai to superintend the Taishan armies, more than ten thousand persons, to Lejia, showing weakness to entice them; shortly the Grand General himself arrived from Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general sent Deng Ai with over ten thousand Taishan troops to Lejia as bait; Sima Shi himself followed hard behind from Zhu.

sentences.zh: 欽不知，果夜來欲襲艾等，會明，見大軍兵馬盛，乃引還。

translations.literal: Qin did not know; indeed he came by night wishing to raid Ai and others; when it grew light, he saw the great army's soldiers and horses abundant; thereupon he led back.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin took the bait and attacked by night, but at dawn he saw the main host's strength and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：欽中子俶，小名鴦。

translations.literal: The Annals of the House of Wei says: Qin's middle son Shu, childhood name Wild Goose.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei chronicle names Wen Qin's second son Shu, nicknamed Wild Goose.

sentences.zh: 年尚幼，勇力絕人，謂欽曰：「及其未定，擊之可破也。

translations.literal: His years were still young; courage and strength surpassed others; he said to Qin: "While they are not yet settled, striking them can break them.
translations.idiomatic: Though still a boy, he was extraordinarily strong and told his father, "Strike before they form up—we can shatter them."

sentences.zh: 」於是分為二隊，夜夾攻軍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they divided into two teams and by night attacked the army from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: They split into two wings for a night attack on both flanks.

sentences.zh: 俶率壯士先至，大呼大將軍，軍中震擾。

translations.literal: Shu led stalwarts and arrived first, loudly shouting Grand General; within the army there was shock and disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Shu led picked men in first, roaring for the grand general until the camp erupted in confusion.

sentences.zh: 欽後期不應。

translations.literal: Qin was late and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin failed to arrive on time.

sentences.zh: 會明，俶退，欽亦引還。

translations.literal: When it grew light, Shu withdrew; Qin also led back.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Shu broke off, and Wen Qin retreated as well.

sentences.zh: 魏末傳曰：殿中人姓尹，字大目，小為曹氏家奴，常侍在帝側，大將軍將俱行。

translations.literal: Wei Final Traditions says: A palace insider surnamed Yin, courtesy name Damu, in youth was a domestic slave of the Cao clan, constantly attending at the emperor's side; the Grand General orders him to go together.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Final Traditions tells of Yin Damu, once a Cao household slave who attended the emperor; he now accompanied the grand general.

sentences.zh: 大目知大將軍一目已突出，啟云：「文欽本是明公腹心，但為人所誤耳，又天子鄉里。

translations.literal: Damu knew the Grand General's one eye had already bulged out; he reported saying: "Wen Qin originally was your trusted intimate, only was misled by others; moreover he is of the Son of Heaven's native place.
translations.idiomatic: Yin knew Sima Shi's eye had been injured; he urged, "Wen Qin was once your man—only others misled him—and he hails from your sovereign's home district."

sentences.zh: 大目昔為文欽所信，乞得追解語之，令還與公复好。

translations.literal: Damu formerly was trusted by Wen Qin; I beg to pursue, explain, and speak to him, ordering him to return and restore good relations with you.
translations.idiomatic: Qin once trusted me—let me ride after him, explain your mercy, and bring him back to your service."

sentences.zh: 」大將軍聽遣大目單身往，乘大馬，被鎧甲，追文欽，遙相與語。

translations.literal: " The Grand General listened and sent Damu alone to go, riding a great horse, draped in armor, pursuing Wen Qin; from afar they mutually spoke.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general agreed: Yin Damu rode out alone in armor, overtook Wen Qin, and hailed him from a distance.

sentences.zh: 大目心實欲曹氏安，謬言：「君侯何苦若不可復忍數日中也！

translations.literal: Damu's heart truly wished the House of Cao to be secure; he falsely said: "Lord, why bitterly as if unable again to endure within several days!
translations.idiomatic: Yin hoped still to save the Caos but spoke softly: "Sir, surely you can endure a few days longer!"

sentences.zh: 」欲使欽解其旨。

translations.literal: " He wished to make Qin understand his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He meant Wen Qin to read this as a hint of pardon.

sentences.zh: 欽殊不悟，乃更厲聲罵大目：「汝先帝家人，不念報恩，而反與司馬師作逆；

translations.literal: Qin utterly did not understand; then he even more harshly cursed Damu: "You former emperor's household person, do not think of repaying grace, but on the contrary join Sima Shi in rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin missed the point entirely and screamed at Yin: "You served the late emperor—how can you side with Sima Shi's treason?"

sentences.zh: 不顧上天，天不祐汝！

translations.literal: You disregard High Heaven; Heaven does not protect you!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sees you—Heaven will not shield you!"

sentences.zh: 」乃張弓傅矢欲射大目，大目涕泣曰：「世事敗矣，善自努力也。」〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon he drew the bow and fitted an arrow wishing to shoot Damu; Damu wept tears and said: "World affairs are defeated; well, strive on yourself."
translations.idiomatic: He strung an arrow to shoot Yin, who wept, "All is lost—do what you can."

sentences.zh: 大將軍縱驍騎追擊，大破之，欽遁走。

translations.literal: The Grand General unleashed swift cavalry to pursue and strike; greatly defeated them; Qin fled and ran.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general sent swift horse in pursuit, shattered Wen Qin's force, and Wen Qin bolted.

sentences.zh: 是日，儉聞欽戰敗，恐懼夜走，眾潰。

translations.literal: That day Jian heard Qin was defeated in battle; in fear he fled by night; the host dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Guanqiu Jian heard of Wen Qin's defeat, fled in panic by night, and his army melted away.

sentences.zh: 比至慎縣，左右人兵稍棄儉去，儉獨與小弟秀及孫重藏水邊草中。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Shen county, attendants and soldiers gradually abandoned Jian and left; Jian alone with younger brother Xiu and Sun Chong hid among riverside grass.
translations.idiomatic: By Shen county his escort had melted away; Guanqiu Jian hid in riverside grass with his youngest brother Xiu and Sun Chong.

sentences.zh: 安風津都尉部民張屬就射殺儉，傳首京都。

translations.literal: Anfeng Ford commandant's department commoner Zhang Shu thereupon shot and killed Jian; his head was forwarded to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shu, a local under the Anfeng ford captain, shot Guanqiu Jian down and sent his head to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 屬封侯。

translations.literal: Shu was enfeoffed marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shu received a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 秀、重走入吳。

translations.literal: Xiu and Chong fled into Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu and Sun Chong escaped into Wu.

sentences.zh: 將士諸為儉、欽所迫脅者，悉歸降。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers various who had been coerced by Jian and Qin all returned and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Every soldier Wen Qin and Guanqiu Jian had pressed into rebellion submitted.

sentences.zh: 〈欽與郭淮書曰：「大將軍昭伯與太傅

translations.literal: Qin's letter to Guo Huai says: "The Grand General Zhabo and the Grand Tutor
translations.idiomatic: In Wen Qin's letter to Guo Huai he wrote: "General-in-chief Zhabo and the grand tutor

translations.literal: (Bo)
translations.idiomatic: (text gloss 'Bo')

sentences.zh: 俱受顧命，登床把臂，託付天下，此遠近所知。

translations.literal: together received the testamentary charge; mounted the bed and grasped arms; entrusted the realm—this near and far knew.
translations.idiomatic: together received the imperial testament: they mounted the couch, clasped arms, and were charged with the empire—the whole realm knows it."

sentences.zh: 後以勢利，乃絕其祀，及其親黨，皆一時之俊，可為痛心，奈何奈何！

translations.literal: Later because of power and profit, then cut off his sacrifices, and his kin and partisans—all were outstanding men of the age—it may be called heartbreaking—alas alas!
translations.idiomatic: Later Sima Yi crushed him for ambition's sake and wiped out his kin—every one of them among the finest men of the hour; it breaks the heart.

sentences.zh: 公侯恃與大司馬公恩親分著，義貫金石，當此之時，想益毒痛，有不可堪也。

translations.literal: Your lordship relied on Grand Marshal's grace—kinship ties manifest, righteousness piercing metal and stone—at this time I imagine increased poisonous pain, there is what cannot be endured.
translations.idiomatic: You who share Grand Marshal Cao Shuang's blood must feel the wound cut deeper than words can bear.

sentences.zh: 王太尉嫌其專朝，潛欲舉兵，事竟不捷，复受誅夷，害及楚王，想甚追恨。

translations.literal: Director Wang abhorred his monopolizing court; secretly wished to raise troops; the affair ultimately did not succeed; again suffered execution and extermination; harm reached Prince Chu—I imagine great retrospective bitterness.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Wang Ling could not abide his monopoly at court and secretly plotted arms—the coup failed, his clan fell, and even Prince Chu died for it; one imagines your bitterness runs deep.

sentences.zh: 太傅既亡，然其子師繼承父業，肆其虐暴，日月滋甚，放主弒後，殘戮忠良，包藏禍心，遂至篡弒。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor having died, yet his son Shi inherited father's enterprise; wantoned in cruelty and violence; sun and moon daily grew worse; dismissed ruler murdered empress; butchered the loyal and good; harbored calamitous intent; finally reached usurpation and regicide.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Yi died, Sima Shi inherited his ambition and grew crueller by the day—deposing sovereigns, killing empresses, slaughtering loyal ministers, all prelude to usurpation.

sentences.zh: 此可忍也，孰不可忍？

translations.literal: If this can be endured, what cannot be endured?
translations.idiomatic: If we tolerate this, what outrage could we not swallow?

sentences.zh: 欽以名義大故，事君有節，忠憤內發，忘寢與食，無所吝顧也。

translations.literal: Qin because righteousness is great, serving lord has restraint, loyal wrath inward bursts forth, forgot sleeping and eating—there is nothing stinted or looked back on.
translations.idiomatic: Bound by duty to ruler and state, I burned with loyal rage—I forgot sleep and food and hesitated at nothing.

sentences.zh: 會毌丘子邦自與父書，騰說公侯，盡事主之義，欲奮白髮，同符太公，惟須東問，影響相應，聞問之日，能不慷慨！

translations.literal: Meeting Guanqiu son Bang himself writing father letter, soaring explaining your lordship, exhausting serving lord's righteousness; wishing to rouse white hair, match tally Taigong; only must east inquire—echo responding—on day of hearing news—how can one not be stirred!
translations.idiomatic: When Guanqiu Dian's son Bang wrote urging all honors you owed your sovereign—like Lü Wang rallying in old age—calling for word from the east, how could loyal hearts not thrill?

sentences.zh: 是以不顧妻孥之痛，即與毌丘鎮東舉義兵三萬餘人，西趨京師，欲扶持王室，掃除奸逆，企踵西望，不得聲問，魯望高子，不足喻急。

translations.literal: Therefore not caring wife and children's pain; immediately with Guanqiu general who guards east raised righteous troops more than thirty thousand persons; west hurried toward capital; wishing to support royal house; sweep away traitorous rebels; standing on tiptoe west gazed; obtained no news sound; Lu looking toward Gaozi—not sufficient to illustrate urgency.
translations.idiomatic: So I left wife and children behind and marched thirty thousand west beside Guanqiu Jian to rescue the throne—yet westward we heard nothing; Confucius longing for Gao Chai scarcely matches our desperation.

sentences.zh: 夫當仁不讓，況救君之難，度道遠艱，故不果期要耳。

translations.literal: Now facing benevolence one does not yield—moreover rescuing lord's difficulty—measuring road far hard—therefore did not realize agreed rendezvous only.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous men do not yield precedence—and saving one's sovereign matters more than punctuality; the distance defeated our timetable.

sentences.zh: 然同舟共濟，安危勢同，禍痛已連，非言飾所解，自公侯所明也。

translations.literal: Yet same boat together crosses—safety danger situation same—calamity pain already linked—not speech ornament can explain—naturally your lordship understands.
translations.idiomatic: We share one boat—your peril is mine; no rhetoric can mend it—you know this well.

sentences.zh: 共事曹氏，積信魏朝，行道之人，皆所知見。

translations.literal: Together served House of Cao; accumulated trust Wei court—travelers on the road—all know and see.
translations.idiomatic: We both served the Caos and enjoyed Wei's trust—the whole road knows it.

sentences.zh: 然在朝之士，冒利偷生，烈士所恥，公侯所賤，賈豎所不忍為也，況當塗之士邪？

translations.literal: Yet those at court—risk profit steal life—martyr scholars shame—your lordship despises—market boys cannot bear to do—moreover those who tread the road?
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers cling to profit—heroes despise them, as do you; peddlers would blush—how much less men who hold power?

sentences.zh: 軍屯住項，小人以閏月十六日別進兵，就於樂嘉城討師，師之徒眾，尋時崩潰，其所斬截，不復訾原，但當長驅徑至京師，而流言先至，毌丘不復詳之，更謂小人為誤，諸軍便爾瓦解。

translations.literal: The army encamped and stayed at Xiang; the petty man on intercalary month sixteenth day separately advanced troops, approached at Lecia city to campaign against Shi; Shi's followers, in a short time collapsed; those he cut down, no longer count origin—but ought long drive straight reach capital; but flying words arrived first; Guanqiu no longer examined them, further said the petty man was wrong; the various armies then so dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Our host lay at Xiang: on the sixteenth of the intercalary month I struck toward Lejia to hit Sima Shi; his line broke at once, his dead beyond counting—you should have driven straight on Luoyang, but rumor arrived first, Guanqiu Jian took me for a liar, and the armies fell apart.

sentences.zh: 毌丘還走，追尋釋解，無所及。

translations.literal: Guanqiu returned and ran; pursue seek explain release—reached nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian retreated before I could reach him to explain.

sentences.zh: 小人還項，复遇王基等十二軍，追尋毌丘，進兵討之，即時克破，所向全勝，要那後無繼何？

translations.literal: The petty man returned to Xiang; again met Wang Ji and others twelve armies; pursue seek Guanqiu; advance troops campaign against him; immediately conquered and broke—where directed wholly victorious—essential what afterward no successor—how?
translations.idiomatic: Back at Xiang I collided with Wang Ji's twelve armies chasing Guanqiu Jian—we shattered him utterly—yet where were reserves when we needed them?

sentences.zh: 孤軍梁昌，進退失所，還據壽春，壽春复走，狼狽躓閡，無復他計，惟當歸命大吳，借兵乞食，繼踵伍員耳。

translations.literal: Isolated army Liangchang—advance retreat lose place—return occupy Shouchun—Shouchun again fled—wretched stumble obstruct—no further other plan—only ought submit destiny Great Wu—borrow troops beg food—follow heel Wu Yuan ear.
translations.idiomatic: Stranded at Liangchang with nowhere to turn, I fell back on Shouchun, lost it again, and had no choice but to cast myself on Wu for troops and rations—another Wu Zixu.

sentences.zh: 不若僕隸，如何快心，复君之仇，永使曹氏少享血食，此亦大國之所祐念也。

translations.literal: Not equal servants-slaves—how express joyful heart—restore lord's revenge—forever cause House of Cao little enjoy blood sacrifice—this also great state's place blesses and remembers.
translations.idiomatic: We are lower than slaves—yet nothing would satisfy me like avenging our sovereign and denying the Simas even one offering—surely Great Wu wishes the same.

sentences.zh: 想公侯不使程嬰、臼擅名於前代，而使大魏獨無鷹揚之士與？

translations.literal: Imagine your lordship does not cause Cheng Ying and Bo alone grasp fame in former ages, yet causes Great Wei alone lack soaring-hawk scholars?
translations.idiomatic: Would you leave Cheng Ying and Gongsun Jiuyi the only names remembered while Wei has no champion left?

sentences.zh: 今大吳敦崇大義，深見愍悼。

translations.literal: Now Great Wu earnestly honors great righteousness; deeply shows pity and grief.
translations.idiomatic: Wu honors righteousness and has shown me deep compassion.

sentences.zh: 然僕於國大分連接，遠同一勢，日欲俱舉，瓜分中國，不原偏取以為己有。

translations.literal: Yet your servant toward state's great division connects—far same one situation—daily wishes together raise—melon-split Middle Kingdom—not wish partial take to regard as own possession.
translations.idiomatic: Wu shares our frontier and could divide the realm with us—I ask no selfish carve-out.

sentences.zh: 公侯必欲共忍帥胸懷，宜廣大勢，恐秦川之卒不可孤舉。

translations.literal: Your lordship must wish together endure command chest bosom—ought enlarge great situation—I fear Qinchuan's soldiers cannot alone raise.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to join hearts with us, widen the front—I doubt Qinchuan can rise alone.

sentences.zh: 今者之計，宜屈己伸人，託命歸漢，東西俱舉爾，乃可克定師黨耳。

translations.literal: Present plan—ought bend self extend others—entrust life submit Han—east west together raise only—then can overcome settle faction.
translations.idiomatic: Yield your pride, pledge allegiance to Shu Han, strike east and west together—only so can we crush Sima Shi's clique.

sentences.zh: 深思鄙言，若愚計可從，宜使漢軍克制期要，使六合校考，與周、召同封，以託付兒孫。

translations.literal: Deeply ponder my base words; if my foolish plan may be followed—ought make Han army restrain agreed rendezvous—make six directions examine and verify—with Zhou and Shao same enfeoffment—to entrust sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Think it through: if my scheme wins you over, coordinate with Han's army, let the realm see you enfeoffed like the Dukes of Zhou and Shao, and hand that legacy to your heirs.

sentences.zh: 此亦非小事也，大丈夫寧處其落落，是以遠呈忠心，時望嘉應。

translations.literal: This also is not a small matter; the great man rather dwells in his lonely neglect—therefore from afar presents loyal heart—momentarily hopes favorable response.
translations.idiomatic: This is no trifle—a gentleman may stand alone, yet I lay my loyalty before you and await your noble answer.

sentences.zh: 」時郭淮已卒，欽未知，故有此書。

translations.literal: " At that time Guo Huai had already died; Qin did not know; therefore had this letter.
translations.idiomatic: " By then Guo Huai was dead—Wen Qin did not know it, which explains this letter.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：毌丘儉之誅，黨與七百餘人，傳侍御史杜友治獄，惟舉首事十人，餘皆奏散。

translations.literal: The Sayings of the Age says: At Guanqiu Jian's execution, partisans were more than seven hundred persons; attendant censor Du You was transmitted to manage the prison; only raised first actors ten persons; the rest all memorialized scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Shishuo yinyu records that when Guanqiu Jian died over seven hundred associates were implicated; Du You as attendant censor handled the case and indicted only ten ringleaders while dismissing the rest.

sentences.zh: 友字季子，東郡人，仕晉冀州刺史、河南尹。

translations.literal: You's courtesy name was Jizi; he was a man of Dong commandery; served Jin as Inspector of Ji Province and governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Du You, styled Jizi, from Dong commandery, later served Western Jin as inspector of Ji and governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 子默，字世玄，歷吏部郎，衛尉。〉

translations.literal: Son Mo, courtesy name Shixuan; passed through ministry of personnel gentleman; commandant of guards.
translations.idiomatic: His son Du Mo, styled Shixuan, rose to director of the ministry of personnel and commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 儉子甸為治書侍御史，先時知儉謀將發，私出將家屬逃走新安靈山上。

translations.literal: Jian's son Dian served as secretary at the imperial secretariat-attendant censor; beforehand knowing Jian's plot would erupt; privately went out leading family members fleeing to ascend Xin'an Ling mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Dian held a palace secretary post; foreseeing his father's rising, he slipped away with his kin to Mount Ling in Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 別攻下之，夷儉三族。

translations.literal: Separately attacked and took them; exterminated Jian's three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Another column stormed the mountain and extirpated Guanqiu Jian's three degrees of kin.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：甸字子邦，有名京邑。

translations.literal: The Sayings of the Age says: Dian's courtesy name was Zibang; had fame in the capital district.
translations.idiomatic: Shishuo yinyu gives Dian's style as Zibang and calls him celebrated in the capital.

sentences.zh: 齊王之廢也，甸謂儉曰：「大人居方獄重任，國傾覆而晏然自守，將受四海之責。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi was deposed, Dian said to Jian: "Father occupies regional prison heavy responsibility; state overturns yet calmly self-guards—will receive four seas' blame.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince of Qi fell, Dian told his father, "You hold a frontier command while the state founders—history will blame you if you sit idle."

sentences.zh: 」儉然之。

translations.literal: " Jian approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian agreed.

sentences.zh: 大將軍惡其為人也。

translations.literal: The Grand General abhorred his person.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi detested his character.

sentences.zh: 及儉起兵，問屈𩑺所在，云不來無能為也。

translations.literal: When Jian raised troops, he asked where Qu 𩑺 was; it was said if he does not come there is nothing to be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the revolt began, Jian asked after Qu 𩑺 and was told the plan was hopeless without him.

sentences.zh: 儉初起兵，遣子宗四人入吳。

translations.literal: When Jian first raised troops, he sent four sons Zong into Wu.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Guanqiu Jian sent four sons named Zong to Wu.

sentences.zh: 太康中，吳平，宗兄弟皆還中國。

translations.literal: In Taikang, Wu was pacified; Zong and brothers all returned to the central states.
translations.idiomatic: After Taikang, when Wu fell, the Zong brothers came back to the north.

sentences.zh: 宗字子仁，有儉風，至零陵太守。

translations.literal: Zong's courtesy name was Ziren; had Jian's style; reached governor of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Zong, styled Ziren, resembled his father and rose to governor of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 宗子奧，巴東監軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: Zong's son Ao, East Ba army supervisor, Inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's son Ao became East Ba area commander and inspector of Yi.

sentences.zh: 習鑿齒曰：毌丘儉感明帝之顧命，故為此役。

translations.literal: Xi Chao says: Guanqiu Jian was moved by Mingdi's testamentary charge; therefore made this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zhaozhi writes that Guanqiu Jian rose to honor Emperor Ming's deathbed charge.

sentences.zh: 君子謂毌丘儉事雖不成，可謂忠臣矣。

translations.literal: The noble man says Guanqiu Jian's affair though not successful, can be called a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemanly opinion calls him a loyal subject though he failed.

sentences.zh: 夫竭節而赴義者我也，成之與敗者時也，我苟無時，成何可必乎？

translations.literal: Now exhausting integrity and rushing to righteousness is I; success and failure is the times; I if without timely opportunity—how can success be certain?
translations.idiomatic: One gives all for duty; fortune decides the outcome—without Heaven's hour, who can promise victory?

sentences.zh: 忘我而不自必，乃所以為忠也。

translations.literal: Forgetting self yet not insisting on certainty oneself—this is therefore because of loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: To forget yourself without demanding success—that is loyalty.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：「死者復生，生者不愧。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: "If the dead could live again, the living would not be ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "Should the dead return to life, the living could face them without shame."

sentences.zh: 」若毌丘儉可謂不愧也。〉

translations.literal: " Thus Guanqiu Jian may be called not ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: By that measure Guanqiu Jian had nothing to regret.

sentences.zh: 欽亡入吳，吳以欽為都護、假節、鎮北大將軍、幽州牧、譙侯。

translations.literal: Qin fled into Wu; Wu made Qin protector-general, credential insignia, general who guards the north, Governor of You Province, marquis of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin fled to Wu, which named him protector-general with jie authority, general who guards the north, governor of You, and marquis of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 〈欽

translations.literal: Qin
translations.idiomatic: (Memorial of Wen) Qin—

sentences.zh: 〈降吳表〉

translations.literal: Memorial Submitting to Wu
translations.idiomatic: Memorial of Surrender to Wu

sentences.zh: 曰：「禀命不幸，常隸魏國，兩絕於天。

translations.literal: It says: "Receiving mandate unlucky; constantly subordinated to Wei state; doubly cut off from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: It reads: "Ill fortune placed me under Wei and twice cut me off from Heaven's favor."

sentences.zh: 雖側伏隅都，自知無路。

translations.literal: Though crouch hiding corner capital—self-know no road.
translations.idiomatic: Though I have skulked in a corner, I know there is no refuge.

sentences.zh: 司馬師滔天作逆，廢害二主，辛、癸、高、莽，惡不足喻。

translations.literal: Sima Shi floods heaven committing rebellion; deposed and harmed two lords; Xin, Gui, Gao, Mang—evil not sufficient to compare.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi's treason overflows heaven—he cast down two sovereigns; Jie, Zhou, Wang Mang pale beside him.

sentences.zh: 欽累世受魏恩，烏鳥之情，竊懷憤踴，在三之義，期於弊僕。

translations.literal: Qin successive generations received Wei grace; crow-bird feeling—privately cherishes indignant leap—the thrice obligation—expects unto exhausted servant.
translations.idiomatic: My house owes Wei generations of kindness—the filial urge of the nesting crow burns in me; bound thrice to ruler, father, and teacher, I mean to serve unto death.

sentences.zh: 前與毌丘儉、郭淮等俱舉義兵，當共討師，掃除凶孽，誠臣慺慺愚管所執。

translations.literal: Earlier together with Guanqiu Jian, Guo Huai and others jointly raised righteous troops; ought together campaign against Shi; sweep away fierce offspring—sincere minister earnest ignorant tube holds.
translations.idiomatic: I marched with Guanqiu Jian and Guo Huai to destroy Sima Shi and scour his faction—that humble longing still grips me.

sentences.zh: 智慮淺薄，微節不騁，進無所依，悲痛切心。

translations.literal: Wisdom and consideration shallow thin—fine restraint not galloping—advance nowhere to rely—grief pain cuts heart.
translations.idiomatic: My plans proved shallow, my moment never came, my advance had no foothold—grief cuts to the bone.

sentences.zh: 退惟不能扶翼本朝，抱愧俯仰，靡所自厝。

translations.literal: Retiring only cannot support wing this court—embrace shame looking up and down—nowhere self to place.
translations.idiomatic: I could not save my dynasty; shame bows me at every turn—I have nowhere to stand.

sentences.zh: 冒緣古義，固有所歸，庶假天威，得展萬一，僵仆之日，亦所不恨。

translations.literal: Risking climb ancient righteousness—solidly has place to return—perhaps borrow Heaven's might—obtain extend one ten-thousandth—stiff-fallen day—also not regret.
translations.idiomatic: I invoke ancient duty and seek your shelter; if Heaven lends me one chance in ten thousand, I will fall content.

sentences.zh: 輒相率將，歸命聖化，慚偷苟生，非辭所陳。

translations.literal: Then mutually lead generals; submit destiny to sagely transformation; ashamed stealing surviving—not speech can declare.
translations.idiomatic: I lead my officers to your enlightened rule; ashamed I lived so long by stealth—words fail me.

sentences.zh: 謹上還所受魏使持節、前將軍、山桑侯印綬。

translations.literal: Respectfully upward return received Wei credential bearing insignia, former general, Shansang marquis seals and ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: I return my Wei seals—credential insignia, former general, and marquis of Shansang.

sentences.zh: 臨表惶惑，伏須罪誅。

translations.literal: Facing memorial confused; prostrate await crime execution.
translations.idiomatic: I lay this memorial in terror and await your judgment.

sentences.zh: 」《魏書》曰：欽字仲若，譙郡人。

translations.literal: " The Book of Wei says: Qin's courtesy name was Zhongruo; a man of Qiao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " The Wei shu gives Wen Qin, styled Zhongruo, from Qiao commandery.

sentences.zh: 父稷，建安中為騎將，有勇力。

translations.literal: Father Ji; in Jian'an era was cavalry general; had courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wen Ji was a cavalry officer under the Jian'an reign, famed for courage.

sentences.zh: 欽少以名將子，材武見稱。

translations.literal: Qin in youth by famous general's son—talent and martial—was praised.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was known as a famous general's son of martial talent.

sentences.zh: 魏諷反，欽坐與諷辭語相連，及下獄，掠笞數百，當死，太祖以稷故赦之。

translations.literal: When Wei Feng rebelled, Qin sat because with Feng's phrasing language connected; when down to prison, flogged and whipped several hundred; ought to die; the Grand Progenitor because of Ji pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Feng rebelled, Wen Qin was implicated by something he had said; he was jailed, beaten hundreds of strokes, and sentenced to death until Cao Cao spared him for Wen Ji's sake.

sentences.zh: 太和中，為五營校督，出為牙門將。

translations.literal: In Taihe era, became colonel supervisor of the five camps; went out as gate general.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taihe he supervised the five camps, then became a camp general.

sentences.zh: 欽性剛暴無禮，所在倨傲陵上，不奉官法，輒見奏遣，明帝抑之。

translations.literal: Qin's nature was harsh violent without propriety; wherever arrogant proud overawe superiors; did not obey official law; then saw memorialized dismissed; Mingdi restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin was brutish and insolent—everywhere he bullied his superiors and flouted orders until impeachment drove him from post after post and Emperor Ming checked him.

sentences.zh: 後復以為淮南牙門將，轉為廬江太守、鷹揚將軍。

translations.literal: Later again made Huainan gate general; transferred to governor of Lujiang, general who soars like a hawk.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored as Huainan's camp general, then governor of Lujiang and general who soars like a hawk.

sentences.zh: 王凌奏欽貪殘，不宜撫邊，求免官治罪，由是徵欽還。

translations.literal: Wang Ling memorialized Qin greedy and cruel, not appropriate to pacify border; sought dismiss office punish crime; thereupon summoned Qin back.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling impeached him for corruption and cruelty—unfit to guard the frontier—and demanded his dismissal, so the court recalled him.

sentences.zh: 曹爽以欽鄉里，厚養待之，不治欽事。

translations.literal: Cao Shuang, because Qin was his townsman, richly supported and favored him and did not discipline Qin's misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wen Qin hailed from the same district as Cao Shuang, Shuang showered him with favors and looked the other way when he broke the rules.

sentences.zh: 復遣還廬江，加冠軍將軍，貴寵逾前。

translations.literal: He was again posted back to Lujiang, promoted general of the vanguard, and honored more lavishly than before.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Lujiang as general of the vanguard and enjoyed greater favor than ever.

sentences.zh: 欽以故益驕，好自矜伐，以壯勇高人，頗得虛名於三軍。

translations.literal: Qin therefore grew more arrogant, fond of boasting of himself, looking down on others through brute courage, and gained a hollow reputation in the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Flush with favor, he swaggered, trumpeted his valor, and lorded it over his fellows—earning empty prestige in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 曹爽誅後，進欽為前將軍以安其心，後代諸葛誕為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: After Cao Shuang's execution, Qin was promoted to former general to reassure him; later he succeeded Zhuge Dan as Inspector of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuang fell he was elevated to former general to buy his loyalty, then replaced Zhuge Dan as inspector of Yang.

sentences.zh: 自曹爽之誅，欽常內懼，與諸葛誕相惡，無所與謀。

translations.literal: From the day Shuang died, Qin lived in constant fear; he detested Zhuge Dan and shared no counsel with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Shuang's death Wen Qin had lived in dread and feuded with Zhuge Dan—they never plotted together.

sentences.zh: 會誕去兵，毌丘儉往，乃陰共結謀。

translations.literal: When Dan yielded command of the army and Guanqiu Jian arrived, they secretly allied.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhuge Dan stepped down and Guanqiu Jian took his place, the two secretly joined forces.

sentences.zh: 戰敗走，晝夜間行，追者不及，遂得入吳，孫峻厚待之。

translations.literal: Defeated, he fled day and night between watches; his pursuers could not catch him, so he reached Wu, where Sun Jun treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: He ran night and day until the chase slackened, found sanctuary in Wu, and Sun Jun welcomed him handsomely.

sentences.zh: 欽雖在他國，不能屈節下人，自呂據、朱異等諸大將皆憎疾之，惟峻常左右之。〉

translations.literal: Though Qin lived among foreigners, he refused to humble himself; generals such as Lü Ju and Zhu Yi all despised him—only Jun constantly shielded him.
translations.idiomatic: Even in exile Wen Qin would not defer to anyone—Lü Ju, Zhu Yi, and other senior commanders loathed him; only Sun Jun stood by him.

sentences.zh: 諸葛誕

translations.literal: Zhuge Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan.

sentences.zh: 諸葛誕字公休，琅邪陽都人，諸葛豐後也。

translations.literal: Zhuge Dan, courtesy name Gongxiu, was a native of Yangdu in Langya and a descendant of Zhuge Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan, styled Gongxiu, came from Yangdu in Langya and traced his line to Zhuge Feng.

sentences.zh: 初以尚書郎為滎陽令，

translations.literal: He first served as magistrate of Xingyang while holding the post of gentleman of the palace secretariat,
translations.idiomatic: His first appointment was as magistrate of Xingyang while attached to the palace secretariat,

sentences.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：誕為郎，與僕射杜畿試船陶河，遭風覆沒，誕亦俱溺。

translations.literal: The Annals of the House of Wei relates that when Dan was a gentleman of the secretariat, he and Deputy Director Du Ji tested a boat on the Tao River; they met a squall, capsized, and sank together.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei chronicle tells how Dan and Deputy Director Du Ji capsized during a trial run on the Tao River.

sentences.zh: 虎賁浮河救誕，誕曰：「先救杜侯。

translations.literal: Tiger guards swam the river to rescue Dan; Dan said, "Save Marquis Du first."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial guards swam out to save him, but he cried, "Marquis Du first!"

sentences.zh: 」誕飄於岸，絕而復蘇。〉

translations.literal: Dan washed ashore, stopped breathing, and revived.
translations.idiomatic: He was washed ashore, apparently drowned, yet revived.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as gentleman of the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as gentleman of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 人有所屬託，輒顯其言而承用之，後有當否，則公議其得失以為褒貶，自是群僚莫不慎其所舉。

translations.literal: Whenever someone pressed a private suit, Dan publicly quoted the request and acted on it; afterward he convened open discussion of whether it had been right or wrong and praised or blamed accordingly—after which no official was careless about whom he recommended.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone brought him a private plea, he aired it openly before acting, then let colleagues debate the outcome—so every nomination was weighed with care.

sentences.zh: 累遷御史中丞尚書，與夏侯玄、鄧颺等相善，收名朝廷，京都翕然。

translations.literal: He rose to palace aide to the censor-in-chief and secretary; he was close to Xiahou Xuan, Deng Yang, and others, won fame at court, and the capital sang his praises.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to palace aide and secretary, he befriended Xiahou Xuan and Deng Yang, built a reputation at court, and became the toast of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 言事者以誕、颺等脩浮華，合虛譽，漸不可長。

translations.literal: Critics charged Dan, Yang, and their circle with cultivating flashy ostentation and trading empty praise—a trend that could not be allowed to spread.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists accused Dan, Deng Yang, and company of empty glitter and mutual puffery—a fashion that had to be stopped.

sentences.zh: 明帝惡之，免誕官。

translations.literal: Mingdi detested them and removed Dan from office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming drove Dan from office in disgust.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：是時，當世俊士散騎常侍夏侯玄、尚書諸葛誕、鄧颺之徒，共相題表，以玄、疇四人為四聰，誕、備八人為八達，中書監劉放子熙、孫資子密、吏部尚書衛臻子烈三人，咸不及比，以父居勢位，容之為三豫，凡十五人。

translations.literal: The Sayings of the Age relates that the luminaries of the day—irregular cavalry attendant Xiahou Xuan, secretary Zhuge Dan, Deng Yang, and the rest—labelled one another: Xuan, Chou, and two others were the Four Clever; Dan, Bei, and seven others were the Eight Freethinkers; three sons of powerful fathers—Liu Xi son of palace supervisor Liu Fang, Sun Mi son of Sun Zi, and Wei Lie son of minister of personnel Wei Zhen—could not match them and were grudgingly dubbed the Three Hesitant, fifteen men in all.
translations.idiomatic: Shishuo yinyu lists the Zhengshi partisans: Xiahou Xuan and three others as the "Four Clever," Zhuge Dan and seven others as the "Eight Freethinkers," with three well-connected also-rans mocked as the "Three Hesitant"—fifteen names in all.

sentences.zh: 帝以構長浮華，皆免官廢錮。〉

translations.literal: The emperor held that they were fostering vain fashion and dismissed them all and barred them from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed them for spreading hollow manners and cashiered the whole set.

sentences.zh: 會帝崩，正始初，玄等並在職。

translations.literal: When the emperor died and the Zhengshi era opened, Xuan and the others were back in harness.
translations.idiomatic: By the start of Zhengshi, after Mingdi's death, Xuan and company held posts again.

sentences.zh: 復以誕為御史中丞尚書，出為揚州刺史，加昭武將軍。

translations.literal: Dan was again named palace aide and secretary, then posted out as Inspector of Yang Province with the added title general who displays martial illumination.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as palace aide and secretary, then became inspector of Yang with the title general who displays martial illumination.

sentences.zh: 王凌之陰謀也，太傅司馬宣王潛軍東伐，以誕為鎮東將軍、假節都督揚州諸軍事，封山陽亭侯。

translations.literal: When Wang Ling plotted in secret, Grand Tutor Sima Yi marched east with concealed forces and appointed Dan general who guards the east, invested him with the jie staff over Yang Province, and enfeoffed him as village marquis of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Ling's conspiracy Sima Yi gave Zhuge Dan command of the east with jie authority over Yang and the village marquisate of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 諸葛恪興東關，遣誕督諸軍討之，與戰，不利。

translations.literal: Zhuge Ke opened operations at Dong Pass; the court ordered Dan to lead the armies against him; they fought and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Ke struck Dong Pass, Zhuge Dan took the field and lost the engagement.

sentences.zh: 還，徙為鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: On returning he was transferred to general who guards the south.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he rotated to general who guards the south.

sentences.zh: 後毌丘儉、文欽反，遣使詣誕，招呼豫州士民。

translations.literal: Later, when Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin rebelled, they sent envoys to Dan summoning the officials and commoners of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin rose, they dispatched envoys to Zhuge Dan urging Yu Province to join them.

sentences.zh: 誕斬其使，露布天下，令知儉、欽凶逆。

translations.literal: Dan executed their envoys, issued a manifesto across the realm, and proclaimed Jian and Qin's treason.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan beheaded the messengers and published an edict branding the rebels traitors.

sentences.zh: 大將軍司馬景王東征，使誕督豫州諸軍，渡安風津向壽春。

translations.literal: Grand General Sima Jingwang campaigned east and ordered Dan to command the Yu armies across Anfeng Ford toward Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi marched east and told Zhuge Dan to bring the Yu forces toward Shouchun via Anfeng Ford.

sentences.zh: 儉、欽之破也，誕先至壽春。

translations.literal: When Jian and Qin were crushed, Dan reached Shouchun first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan arrived at Shouchun before Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin were routed.

sentences.zh: 壽春中十餘萬口，聞儉、欽敗，恐誅，悉破城門出，流迸山澤，或散走入吳。

translations.literal: More than a hundred thousand people were inside Shouchun; hearing of Jian and Qin's defeat, they feared execution, smashed the gates, and fled into hills and marshes or scattered into Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the rebels' defeat reached Shouchun's hundred thousand souls, panic swept the city; people tore open the gates and fled into the wilds or east into Wu.

sentences.zh: 以誕久在淮南，乃復以為鎮東大將軍、儀同三司、都督揚州。

translations.literal: Because Dan had long served in Huainan, he was again named grand general who guards the east with ceremonial parity of the three offices and command of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting his long experience in Huainan, the court restored him as grand general who guards the east with honors matching the three senior ministers over Yang.

sentences.zh: 吳大將孫峻、呂據、留贊等聞淮南亂，會文欽往，乃帥眾將欽徑至壽春；

translations.literal: Wu generals Sun Jun, Lü Ju, and Liu Zan, hearing of the turmoil in Huainan and Wen Qin's approach, led their troops escorting Qin straight to Shouchun;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun, Lü Ju, Liu Zan, and other Wu commanders, hearing of the revolt and Wen Qin's flight, marched him toward Shouchun—

sentences.zh: 時誕諸軍已至，城不可攻，乃走。

translations.literal: but Dan's army had already arrived; the city could not be taken, so they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: but Zhuge Dan's men were already there; finding the city untakable, they retired.

sentences.zh: 誕遣將軍蔣班追擊之，斬贊，傳首，收其印節。

translations.literal: Dan sent General Jiang Ban in pursuit; Ban killed Liu Zan, sent his head to headquarters, and seized his seals of office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan ordered Jiang Ban to chase them down—Liu Zan fell, his head and insignia taken.

sentences.zh: 進封高平侯，邑三千五百戶，轉為征東大將軍。

translations.literal: Dan was advanced to marquis of Gaoping with a fief of 3,500 households and promoted to grand general who conquers the east.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to marquis of Gaoping with 3,500 households and promoted to grand general who conquers the east.

sentences.zh: 六月，車駕東征，至項。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the imperial train campaigned east to Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor's host reached Xiang.

sentences.zh: 大將軍司馬文王督中外諸軍二十六萬眾，臨淮討之。

translations.literal: Grand General Sima Wenwang superintended 260,000 inner and outer troops and advanced on the Huai to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao led 260,000 men of the inner and outer armies to the Huai to besiege the rebels.

sentences.zh: 大將軍屯丘頭。

translations.literal: The Grand General encamped at Qiutou.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general pitched camp at Qiutou.

sentences.zh: 使基及安東將軍陳騫等四面合圍，表裡再重，塹壘甚峻。

translations.literal: He ordered Ji and general who pacifies the east Chen Qian and others to surround them on four sides—inner and outer double rings—with ditches and ramparts exceptionally steep.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji and Chen Qian ringed the city in two belts of trench and palisade.

sentences.zh: 又使監軍石苞、兗州刺史州泰等，簡銳卒為遊軍，備外寇。

translations.literal: He also ordered army supervisor Shi Bao, Inspector of Yan Province Zhou Tai, and others to pick crack troops as flying columns against outside raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao, Zhou Tai of Yan, and others led picked mobile troops to ward off relief forces.

sentences.zh: 欽等數出犯圍，逆擊走之。

translations.literal: Qin and company repeatedly sallied against the lines and were beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin sortied again and again and was driven in each time.

sentences.zh: 吳將朱異再以大眾來迎誕等，渡黎漿水，泰等逆與戰，每摧其鋒。

translations.literal: Wu general Zhu Yi twice brought a great host to rescue Dan and company; crossing the Lijiang slurry, Tai and others opposed them in battle and each time blunted their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi of Wu twice tried to relieve the siege at Lijiang; Zhou Tai and company turned him aside.

sentences.zh: 孫綝以異戰不進，怒而殺之。

translations.literal: Sun Chen, furious that Yi would not advance, executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chen killed Zhu Yi for failing to press the attack.

sentences.zh: 城中食轉少，外救不至，眾無所恃。

translations.literal: Food inside the city dwindled; outside relief never arrived; the host had nothing to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions ran low, no help came, and the defenders lost heart.

sentences.zh: 將軍蔣班、焦彝，皆誕爪牙計事者也，棄誕，逾城自歸大將軍。

translations.literal: Generals Jiang Ban and Jiao Yi—Dan's claws and fangs for planning—abandoned Dan, climbed the wall, and surrendered to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ban and Jiao Yi, Zhuge Dan's chief counselors, slipped over the wall to Sima Zhao.

sentences.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：蔣班、焦彝言於諸葛誕曰：「朱異等以大眾來而不能進，孫綝殺異而歸江東，外以發兵為名，而內實坐須成敗，其歸可見矣。

translations.literal: The Han-Jin Spring and Autumn relates that Jiang Ban and Jiao Yi said to Zhuge Dan: "Zhu Yi came with a great army yet could not advance; Sun Chen killed Yi and returned east—the outward plea was sending troops, yet inwardly they sit watching success or failure; their withdrawal is plain.
translations.idiomatic: Ban and Yi warned Dan: Wu sent Zhu Yi but called him back after executing him—Sun Chen only waited on events east of the river.

sentences.zh: 今宜及眾心尚固，士卒思用，並力決死，攻其一面，雖不能盡克，猶可有全者。

translations.literal: Now we ought while hearts are still firm and soldiers eager to stake everything on one desperate assault along one face—even if we cannot win outright, some may yet survive.
translations.idiomatic: Strike now while morale holds—throw everything at one sector; even total victory may not come, yet some might escape alive."

sentences.zh: 」文欽曰：「江東乘戰勝之威久矣，未有難北方者也。

translations.literal: Wen Qin said: "East of the river has ridden victory's prestige long—nobody there has ever feared the north.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin replied: "The south has swaggered on victory too long to fear us."

sentences.zh: 況公今舉十餘萬之眾內附，而欽與全端等皆同居死地，父子兄弟盡在江表，就孫綝不欲，主上及其親戚豈肯聽乎？

translations.literal: Moreover you now bring more than a hundred thousand within our walls to surrender; Qin and Quan Duan and the rest share this dead-end ground—fathers, sons, and brothers all remain south of the river—suppose Sun Chen is unwilling; would their sovereign and kin consent?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, your hundred thousand newcomers are trapped like Qin and Quan Duan—every family still lies east of the Yangzi—would Sun Chen or their kinsmen truly march to save us?"

sentences.zh: 且中國無歲無事，軍民並疲，今守我一年，勢力已因，異圖生心，變故將起，以往準今，可計日而望也。

translations.literal: Moreover the central plain knows no year without crisis—soldiers and civilians alike are weary; keep us bottled one more year and strength fails; other plots will stir—reckon by past cases and deliverance is only days away.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland never rests—another year's siege would exhaust everyone; history shows relief follows soon."
