sentences.zh: 」班、彝固勸之，欽怒，而誕欲殺班。

translations.literal: Ban and Yi urged hard; Qin grew angry, and Dan wished to kill Ban.
translations.idiomatic: Ban and Yi pressed their case until Wen Qin flared and Dan nearly executed Ban.

sentences.zh: 二人懼，且知誕之必敗也，十一月，乃相攜而降。〉

translations.literal: The pair grew fearful and knew Dan must fall; in the eleventh month they slipped away together and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Dan's doom, they defected together in the eleventh month."

sentences.zh: 大將軍乃使反間，以奇變說全懌等，懌等率眾數千人開門來出。

translations.literal: The Grand General then employed stratagem and whispered strange tales to Quan Yi and company; Yi led several thousand men out through an opened gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao spread distrust among Quan Yi and company until Yi opened the gates with thousands of followers.

sentences.zh: 城中震懼，不知所為。

translations.literal: The city shook with terror and knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Panic seized the garrison.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，誕、欽、咨等大為攻具，晝夜五六日攻南圍，欲決圍而出。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Dan, Qin, Zi, and others built great siege engines and assaulted the southern perimeter five or six days and nights running, seeking to burst the cordon.
translations.idiomatic: First month, year three: Dan, Qin, and Tang Zi hurled engines against the south wall for days, trying to break out.

sentences.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：文欽曰：「蔣班、焦彝謂我不能出而走，全端、全懌又率眾逆降，此敵無備之時也，可以戰矣。

translations.literal: The Han-Jin Spring and Autumn records Wen Qin saying: "Jiang Ban and Jiao Yi claimed we could not break out and fled; Quan Duan and Quan Yi even led their men to surrender—the enemy is off guard; we can fight."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin argued that defections meant the Wei lines were slack.

sentences.zh: 」誕及唐咨等皆以為然，遂共悉眾出攻。〉

translations.literal: Dan and Tang Zi and others all agreed; then together they launched the whole force against the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan and Tang Zi agreed and threw every man into the assault."

sentences.zh: 圍上諸軍，臨高以發石車火箭逆燒破其攻具，弩矢及石雨下，死傷者蔽地，血流盈塹。

translations.literal: The troops on the berm rained catapult stones and rocket fire from the heights, burning the siege gear; crossbow bolts and stones fell like rain—the dead carpeted the ground and blood filled the ditches.
translations.idiomatic: Defenders on the earthworks smashed the rams with traction trebuchets and rockets; missiles fell like rain until corpses choked the trenches.

sentences.zh: 復還入城，城內食轉竭，降出者數万口。

translations.literal: They fell back inside; provisions inside were exhausted further, and tens of thousands came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew; starvation drove tens of thousands to yield.

sentences.zh: 欽欲盡出北方人，省食，與吳人堅守，誕不聽，由是爭恨。

translations.literal: Qin wished to expel every northerner to save grain and let Wu men hold out alone—Dan refused, and they nursed mutual hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin wanted to drive out northern troops to stretch rations while Wu soldiers held the walls—Dan refused, and they turned on each other.

sentences.zh: 欽素與誕有隙，徒以計合，事急愈相疑。

translations.literal: Qin had long been at odds with Dan; only expediency held them together—when crisis peaked, suspicion grew.
translations.idiomatic: Old enemies forced into alliance, they trusted each other less as danger mounted.

sentences.zh: 欽見誕計事，誕遂殺欽。

translations.literal: When Qin came to consult Dan, Dan killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Qin came to council, Zhuge Dan slew him.

sentences.zh: 欽子鴦及虎將兵在小城中，聞欽死，勒兵馳赴之，眾不為用。

translations.literal: Qin's sons Yang and Hu commanded troops in the lesser citadel; hearing of Qin's death, they rushed there—yet the men would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Yang and Hu held the inner ward; hearing of their father's murder they galloped to revenge but their troops refused orders.

sentences.zh: 鴦、虎單走，逾城出，自歸大將軍。

translations.literal: Yang and Hu fled alone, climbed out, and surrendered to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers scaled the wall alone and defected to Sima Zhao.

sentences.zh: 軍吏請誅之，大將軍令曰：「欽之罪不容誅，其子固應當戮，然鴦、虎以窮歸命，且城未拔，殺之是堅其心也。

translations.literal: Staff officers asked to execute them; the Grand General ordered: "Qin's guilt deserved death—his sons normally should die too—yet Yang and Hu surrender at extremity; while the city stands, killing them would steel enemy hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao spared them: Wen Qin's crimes deserved death, but executing his sons mid-siege would harden resistance.

sentences.zh: 」乃赦鴦、虎，使將兵數百騎馳巡城，呼語城內云：「文欽之子猶不見殺，其餘何懼？

translations.literal: " Thereupon he pardoned Yang and Hu, gave them several hundred riders to circle the walls, and shouted to the city: "Even Wen Qin's sons live—what have you to fear?
translations.idiomatic: He freed them and sent them riding the circuit crying that Wen Qin's heirs lived—so why fear?"

sentences.zh: 」表鴦、虎為將軍，各賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: " He memorialized Yang and Hu as generals and granted each noble rank within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He named them generals with noble rank within the passes.

sentences.zh: 城內喜且擾，又日飢困，誕、咨等智力窮。

translations.literal: Inside there was joy yet turmoil; hunger worsened daily; Dan and Zi had run out of stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison wavered between hope and panic as hunger gnawed and Dan's counsel failed.

sentences.zh: 大將軍乃自臨圍，四面進兵，同時鼓譟登城，城內無敢動者。

translations.literal: The Grand General then personally approached the lines; troops advanced on every side, drums thundered as they scaled the walls—none inside dared move.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao rode to the siege line; assault parties escaladed on four fronts while garrison troops froze.

sentences.zh: 誕窘急，單乘馬，將其麾下突小城門出。

translations.literal: Dan, desperate, rode alone with his household troops and burst through a small gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan bolted through a postern with his household guard.

sentences.zh: 大將軍司馬胡奮部兵逆擊，斬誕，傳首，夷三族。

translations.literal: Major Hu Fen's contingent struck head-on, slew Dan, forwarded his head, and exterminated three degrees of kin.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fen cut him down; his head went to Luoyang and his clan perished.

sentences.zh: 誕麾下數百人，坐不降見斬，皆曰：「為諸葛公死，不恨。

translations.literal: Several hundred of Dan's followers who refused surrender were executed in ranks; each said, "We die for Lord Zhuge without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds who would not yield died shouting devotion to Zhuge Dan.

sentences.zh: 」其得人心如此。

translations.literal: Thus did he win men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his hold on loyalty.

sentences.zh: 〈干寶《晉紀》曰：數百人拱手為列，每斬一人，輒降之，竟不變，至盡，時人比之田橫。

translations.literal: Gan Bao's Annals of Jin says: Several hundred stood with folded hands in ranks; each time one was beheaded they refused to kneel—unchanged to the last—men compared them to Tian Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao describes hundreds standing like Tian Heng's retainers, undaunted to the blade.

sentences.zh: 吳將於詮曰：「大丈夫受命其主，以兵救人，既不能克，又束手於敵，吾弗取也。

translations.literal: Wu general Yu Quan said: "A great man takes his lord's charge and leads troops to save others—if he cannot conquer and folds his hands to the enemy, I will not abide it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu officer Yu Quan declared he would not surrender tamely while failing his mission.

sentences.zh: 」乃免冑冒陳而死。〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon he doffed his helmet and charged the formation to his death.
translations.idiomatic: He threw away his helm and died charging the Wei lines."

sentences.zh: 唐咨、王祚及諸裨將皆面縛降，吳兵萬眾，器仗軍實山積。

translations.literal: Tang Zi, Wang Zuo, and other colonels bound themselves and yielded; ten thousand Wu soldiers with weapons and baggage piled like hills.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zi, Wang Zuo, and staff tied themselves and came out; ten thousand Wu troops stacked arms in heaps.

sentences.zh: 初圍壽春，議者多欲急攻之，大將軍以為：「城固而眾多，攻之必力屈，若有外寇，表裡受敵，此危道也。

translations.literal: When the siege of Shouchun began, many advisers urged a swift assault; the Grand General judged: "The walls are strong and the multitude large—a storm would exhaust us; if outside enemies struck we would face foes front and rear—that is perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Early debate favored storming Shouchun; Sima Zhao argued the walls were thick and relief possible—a rush attack courted disaster.

sentences.zh: 今三叛相聚於孤城之中，天其或者將使同就戮，吾當以全策縻之，可坐而制也。

translations.literal: Now three rebels mass in a lone city—Heaven perhaps intends them to perish together; I shall bind them with full strategy and sit to subdue.
translations.idiomatic: Three traitors trapped in one town—Heaven may mean to destroy them together; I will starve them into submission.

sentences.zh: 」誕以二年五月反，三年二月破滅。

translations.literal: " Dan rebelled in the fifth month of the second year and was destroyed in the second month of the third.
translations.idiomatic: Dan rose second year fifth month and fell third year second month.

sentences.zh: 六軍按甲，深溝高壘，而誕自困，竟不煩攻而克。

translations.literal: The six armies rested their armor behind deep ditches and high ramparts while Dan trapped himself—never troubled by storming yet conquered.
translations.idiomatic: Wei troops stood idle behind fortifications until Dan collapsed without a major assault.

sentences.zh: 〈干寶《晉紀》曰：初，壽春每歲雨潦，淮水溢，常淹城邑。

translations.literal: Gan Bao's Annals of Jin relates that Shouchun flooded yearly—Huai waters rose and often drowned the district.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao notes chronic floods around Shouchun when the Huai spilled.

sentences.zh: 故文王之築圍也，誕笑之曰：「是固不攻而自敗也。

translations.literal: Thus when Wenwang built the siege lines Dan laughed: "This fort needs no attack—it will defeat itself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan mocked Sima Zhao's siege: floods would finish them.

sentences.zh: 」及大軍之攻，亢旱逾年。

translations.literal: When the main army attacked, severe drought lasted more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: Yet during the siege a year-long drought struck.

sentences.zh: 城既陷，是日大雨，圍壘皆毀。

translations.literal: When the city fell that day a great rain fell and washed away the berms.
translations.idiomatic: The day it fell a cloudburst swept the earthworks away.

sentences.zh: 誕子靚，字仲思，吳平還晉。

translations.literal: Dan's son Jing, courtesy name Zhongsi, returned to Jin after Wu fell.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhuge Jing, styled Zhongsi, came back under Jin after Wu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 靚子恢，字道明，位至尚書令，追贈左光祿大夫開府。〉

translations.literal: Jing's son Hui, courtesy name Daoming, rose to secretary-in-chief and was posthumously honored minister of the left with full cabinet privileges.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's son Hui, styled Daoming, reached secretary-in-chief and received posthumous honors."

sentences.zh: 及破壽春，議者又以為淮南仍為叛逆，吳兵室家在江南，不可縱，宜悉坑之。

translations.literal: After Shouchun fell some argued Huainan remained rebellious and Wu soldiers' families lay south of the Yangzi—best bury them all alive.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged slaughtering captured Wu troops lest Huainan rebel again.

sentences.zh: 大將軍以為古之用兵，全國為上，戮其元惡而已。

translations.literal: The Grand General held that in ancient warfare sparing the whole state ranked highest—execute only the chief evil.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao cited the maxim: spare the state when possible—punish ringleaders alone.

sentences.zh: 吳兵就得亡還，適可以示中國之弘耳。

translations.literal: Let Wu soldiers escape home—it demonstrates central state's magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Letting survivors return advertises the north's mercy.

sentences.zh: 一無所殺，分佈三河近郡以安處之。

translations.literal: Not one was killed; they were quartered among the three He commanderies nearby for resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: None were executed; they were settled among commanderies near the three He rivers.

sentences.zh: 唐咨本利城人。

translations.literal: Tang Zi was originally a man of Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zi came from Licheng.

sentences.zh: 黃初中，利城郡反，殺太守徐箕，推咨為主。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu era Licheng commandery rebelled, slew prefect Xu Ji, and elevated Zi as leader.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangchu Licheng rose, killed prefect Xu Ji, and made Tang Zi chief.

sentences.zh: 文帝遣諸軍討破之，咨走入海，遂亡至吳，官至左將軍，封侯、持節。

translations.literal: Wendi dispatched armies that crushed them; Zi fled to the sea and escaped to Wu, rising to general of the left with marquis rank and jie authority.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen crushed the revolt; Tang Zi fled overseas to Wu and climbed to general of the left with a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 誕、欽屠戮，咨亦生禽，三叛皆獲，天下快焉。

translations.literal: Dan and Qin were slaughtered; Zi was taken alive—all three rebels captured—the realm rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Dan and Qin died; Tang Zi was captured—the three rebels gone at last.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：宋建椎牛禱賽，終自焚滅。

translations.literal: The Fuzi says: Song Jian slaughtered oxen for sacrifice yet burned to destruction at last.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan compares Song Jian's vain sacrifices to doom.

sentences.zh: 文欽日祠祭事天，斬於人手。

translations.literal: Wen Qin worshipped heaven daily yet died by another's blade.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin's daily prayers did not spare him from the sword.

sentences.zh: 諸葛誕夫婦聚會神巫，淫祀求福，伏尸淮南，舉族誅夷。

translations.literal: Zhuge Dan and his wife summoned spirit mediums with licentious rites seeking blessing—corpses littered Huainan and their clan was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan and his wife fed shamans—corpses filled Huainan and extirpation followed.

sentences.zh: 此天下所共見，足為明鑑也。〉

translations.literal: All under Heaven witnessed it—enough for a bright mirror.
translations.idiomatic: The realm saw—clear warning for posterity."

sentences.zh: 拜咨安遠將軍，其餘裨將咸假號位，吳眾悅服。

translations.literal: Zi was appointed general who pacifies the far regions; the remaining colonels were all granted interim titles; the Wu troops were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zi became general who pacifies the far regions; subordinates received brevet ranks and Wu surrendered willingly.

sentences.zh: 江東感之，皆不誅其家。

translations.literal: East of the river was moved by this—they executed none of their families.
translations.idiomatic: Wu so respected Wei mercy that no captive kin suffered reprisal.

sentences.zh: 其淮南將吏士民諸為誕所脅略者，惟誅其首逆，餘皆赦之。

translations.literal: As for Huainan officers, clerks, soldiers, and commoners whom Dan had coerced and led astray, only the chief rebels were executed; all others were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan folk pressed into rebellion faced punishment only for ringleaders; the rest went free.

sentences.zh: 聽鴦、虎收斂欽喪，給其車牛，致葬舊墓。

translations.literal: Yang and Hu were permitted to gather Qin's remains for burial; carts and oxen were supplied to convey him to his ancestral tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yang and Wen Hu buried their father with imperial carts and oxen at his old grave.

sentences.zh: 〈習鑿齒曰：自是天下畏威懷德矣。

translations.literal: Xi Chao says: From this the realm both feared might and embraced virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zhaozhi writes that the empire thereafter feared Wei arms yet treasured its grace.

sentences.zh: 君子謂司馬大將軍於是役也，可謂能以德攻矣。

translations.literal: The gentleman judged Grand General Sima in this campaign able to be called attacking through virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Moralists called Sima Zhao's campaign a conquest won by clemency.

sentences.zh: 夫建業者異矣，各有所尚，而不能兼併也。

translations.literal: Those who build enterprise differ: each has what it esteems, and cannot combine them all.
translations.idiomatic: Founders differ in what they prize—no one path holds every virtue.

sentences.zh: 故窮武之雄斃於不仁，存義之國喪於懦退，今一征而禽三叛，大虜吳眾，席捲淮浦，俘馘十萬，可謂壯矣。

translations.literal: Therefore the hero of ultimate martial prowess perishes from want of benevolence; the state that preserves righteousness may perish from timid retreat. Now one expedition seized three rebels, took the great host of Wu, swept the Huai shore, and captured a hundred thousand—truly a mighty feat.
translations.idiomatic: Brute force without humanity fails; soft virtue without steel fails. One campaign netted three traitors, broke Wu's army on the Huai, and took a hundred thousand heads—magnificent.

sentences.zh: 而未及安坐，喪王基之功，種惠吳人，結異類之情，寵鴦葬欽，忘疇昔之隙，不咎誕眾，使揚士懷愧，功高而人樂其成，業廣而敵懷其德，武昭既敷，文算又洽，推此道也，天下其孰能當之哉？

translations.literal: Before he could sit in peace, he lost Wang Ji's service; he sowed favor among Wu people, bound the feelings of foreign kinds, honored Yang and buried Qin, forgot old grudges, did not blame Dan's host, and made Yangzi gentry feel shame; merit was high yet people rejoiced in the completion, enterprise was broad yet enemies cherished his virtue; martial glory was spread and civil planning was thorough—pursue this way, and who under Heaven could withstand it?
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao lost Wang Ji yet won Wu hearts, forgave enemies, left Yang gentry abashed, and balanced force with policy—none could have stood against such a course.

sentences.zh: 喪王基，語在《基傳》。

translations.literal: The loss of Wang Ji is discussed in the "Biography of Ji."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji's death is related in his own chapter.

sentences.zh: ◎鴦一名俶。

translations.literal: Yang was also called Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yang was also known as Shu.

sentences.zh: 《晉諸公贊》曰，俶後為將軍，破涼州虜，名聞天下。

translations.literal: The Praise of Jin Lords says Shu later became a general, smashed Liangzhou raiders, and his fame reached the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Praise records Shu as general who crushed Liangzhou barbarians and became famous.

sentences.zh: 太康中為東夷校尉、假節。

translations.literal: In Taikang he served as colonel of the eastern barbarians with credential insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taikang he was eastern Yi colonel with jie authority.

sentences.zh: 當之職，入辭武帝，帝見而惡之，託以他事免俶官。

translations.literal: When about to take office he entered to bid Emperor Wu farewell; the emperor saw him and detested him and dismissed him from office on another pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave of Emperor Wu before his posting, he earned the emperor's disgust and lost his post on a trumped-up excuse.

sentences.zh: 東安公繇，諸葛誕外孫，欲殺俶，因誅楊駿，誣俶謀逆，遂夷三族。〉

translations.literal: Duke Dong'an Sima You, maternal grandson of Zhuge Dan, wished to kill Shu; exploiting the execution of Yang Jun he falsely accused Shu of rebellion and exterminated three degrees of kin.
translations.idiomatic: Sima You, Zhuge Dan's grandson, framed Shu during Yang Jun's purge and wiped out his clan.

sentences.zh: 鄧艾字士載，義陽棘陽人也。

translations.literal: Deng Ai, courtesy name Shizai, was a native of Jiyang in Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai, styled Shizai, came from Jiyang in Yiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 少孤，太祖破荊州，徙汝南，為農民養犢。

translations.literal: He lost his father young; when Taizu took Jingzhou he was moved to Runan and raised calves for a farmer.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, after Cao Cao conquered Jingzhou his family was relocated to Runan, where he herd calves for peasants.

sentences.zh: 年十二，隨母至潁川，讀故太丘長陳寔碑文，言「文為世範，行為士則」，艾遂自名範，字士則。

translations.literal: At twelve he followed his mother to Yingchuan and read the inscription on former magistrate of Taiqiu Chen Shi's stele, which said "Literature is the age's model; conduct is the gentleman's standard"; Ai thereupon named himself Fan and styled Shize.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve, reading Chen Shi's epitaph in Yingchuan—"his prose modeled the age, his deeds modeled gentlemen"—he took the names Fan and Shize.

sentences.zh: 後宗族有與同者，故改焉。

translations.literal: Later someone of his lineage bore the same names, so he changed them.
translations.idiomatic: A clansman later claimed the same courtesy names, so he changed them.

sentences.zh: 為都尉學士，以口吃，不得作幹佐。

translations.literal: As academician to the commandant, because he stuttered he could not serve as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Named to the commandant's school, his stammer barred him from staff work.

sentences.zh: 為稻田守叢草吏。

translations.literal: He became a thicket-warden of the paddy fields.
translations.idiomatic: He served as keeper of the irrigation ditches.

sentences.zh: 同郡吏父憐其家貧，資給甚厚，艾初不稱謝。

translations.literal: A clerk from his commandery pitied his family's poverty and subsidized him richly; Ai never thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: A colleague's father subsidized the poor boy generously; Deng Ai offered no thanks.

sentences.zh: 每見高山大澤，輒規度指畫軍營處所，時人多笑焉。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw high mountains and broad marshes he would trace plans for campsites; people of the age often laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: He traced imaginary camps on every ridge and marsh—others mocked the dreaming cowherd.

sentences.zh: 後為典農綱紀，上計吏，因使見太尉司馬宣王。

translations.literal: Later he became bookkeeper of the military-agriculture colony, accounts clerk for population registers, and through an errand met Grand Commandant Sima Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted through agribusiness posts to clerk, he eventually audience with Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 宣王奇之，辟之為掾，

translations.literal: Yi marveled at him and summoned him as an aide,
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi was impressed and recruited him as an aide,

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：鄧艾少為襄城典農部民，與石苞皆年十二三。

translations.literal: The Sayings of the Age relates that Deng Ai in youth was a tenant farmer under Xiangcheng military-agriculture, together with Shi Bao—both twelve or thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: Shishuo yinyu tells how Deng Ai and Shi Bao, tweens in Xiangcheng agribusiness,

sentences.zh: 謁者陽翟郭玄信，武帝監軍郭誕元奕之子。

translations.literal: The usher Guo Xuanxin of Yangdi was son of Emperor Wu's army supervisor Guo Dan, courtesy name Yuanyi.
translations.idiomatic: met usher Guo Xuanxin of Yangdi—son of military inspector Guo Dan.

sentences.zh: 建安中，少府吉本起兵許都，玄信坐被刑在家，從典農司馬求人禦，以艾、苞與禦，行十餘里，與語，悅之，謂二人皆當遠至為佐相。

translations.literal: In Jian'an era Junior Minister Ji Ben raised troops at Xuchang; Xuanxin was implicated and punished and stayed home; he asked the military-agriculture major for drivers—Ai and Bao were given him; after riding ten li he talked with them, delighted, and said both would rise to minister rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Ben's coup left Guo Xuanxin under sentence at home; borrowing Deng Ai and Shi Bao as drivers for ten li, he predicted ministerial careers for both.

sentences.zh: 艾後為典農功曹，奉使詣宣王，由此見知，遂被拔擢。〉

translations.literal: Ai later became merit officer of military-agriculture; sent on mission to Sima Yi he came to notice and was promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai rose to merit evaluator, impressed Sima Yi on embassy, and climbed the ladder."

sentences.zh: 遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted gentleman of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred to gentleman of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時欲廣田畜谷，為滅賊資，使艾行陳、項已東至壽春。

translations.literal: At that time they wished to broaden fields and hoard grain to supply the destruction of bandits; they sent Ai from Chen and Xiang east as far as Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: The court meant to farm Huainan for the Wu campaign and sent Deng Ai to survey from Chen-Xiang east to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 艾以為「田良水少，不足以盡地利，宜開河渠，可以引水澆溉，大積軍糧，又通運漕之道。

translations.literal: Ai judged that "the soil is good but water scarce—not enough to exhaust the land's advantage; ought to open canals to draw irrigation, pile up army grain in bulk, and open water transport."
translations.idiomatic: He reported fertile land but scarce water—dig canals for irrigation, grain stockpiles, and canal traffic.

sentences.zh: 」乃著濟河論以喻其指。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed the Discourse on the Ji River to explain his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted the Discourse on the Ji River to spell it out.

sentences.zh: 又以為「昔破黃巾，因為屯田，積穀於許都以制四方。

translations.literal: He also judged that "when the Yellow Scarves were crushed we instituted garrison farms and stored grain at Xuchang to bind the four quarters."
translations.idiomatic: He recalled how garrison farming after the Yellow Scarves filled Xuchang to hold the realm.

sentences.zh: 今三隅已定，事在淮南，每大軍征舉，運兵過半，功費巨億，以為大役。

translations.literal: Now the three corners are pacified; the issue is Huainan—every great expedition spends over half its effort moving supplies; costs reach billions—this is the great labor.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan alone remained costly—every campaign wasted half its strength on transport.

sentences.zh: 陳、蔡之間，土下田良，可省許昌左右諸稻田，並水東下。

translations.literal: Between Chen and Cai the ground slopes yet soil is good; we may retire several paddy colonies west of Xuchang and shift water east.
translations.idiomatic: Chen-Cai land is prime—divert water east from Xuchang farms.

sentences.zh: 令淮北屯二萬人，淮南三萬人，十二分休，常有四萬人，且田且守。

translations.literal: Order 20,000 colonists north of the Huai and 30,000 south, rotating in twelve shifts—always 40,000 men farming and guarding together.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand tillers north of the Huai, thirty thousand south, rotating twelve ways—forty thousand always under arms and plow.

sentences.zh: 水豐常收三倍於西，計除眾費，歲完五百萬斛以為軍資。

translations.literal: With abundant water harvests triple those west of the mountains; deducting expenses, yearly five million hu remain for the army.
translations.idiomatic: Well-watered fields yield triple interior harvests—five million hu yearly after costs.

sentences.zh: 六七年間，可積三千萬斛於淮上，此則十萬之眾五年食也。

translations.literal: In six or seven years thirty million hu may accumulate on the Huai—this feeds a host of 100,000 for five years.
translations.idiomatic: Six or seven years yields thirty million hu on the Huai—five years' food for a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 以此乘吳，無往而不克矣。

translations.literal: With this to strike Wu there is nowhere you would not conquer.
translations.idiomatic: Such stores guarantee victory against Wu.

sentences.zh: 」宣王善之，事皆施行。

translations.literal: Yi approved; all measures were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi endorsed every proposal.

sentences.zh: 正始二年，乃開廣漕渠，每東南有事，大軍興眾，汎舟而下，達於江、淮，資食有儲而無水害，艾所建也。

translations.literal: In Zhengshi second year they opened the Broad Canal; whenever the southeast stirred, great armies embarked downstream to the Jiang and Huai—provisions were stocked without flood damage; this was Ai's creation.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi 2 they dug the Broad Canal so fleets could supply Jiang-Huai campaigns—Deng Ai's legacy.

sentences.zh: 出參征西軍事，遷南安太守。

translations.literal: He went out as aide on the west expedition staff and was promoted governor of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the western headquarters as aide and became governor of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 嘉平元年，與征西將軍郭淮拒蜀偏將軍姜維。

translations.literal: In Jiaping first year he joined general who conquers the west Guo Huai against Shu lieutenant-general Jiang Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaping 1: he fought Jiang Wei beside Guo Huai.

sentences.zh: 維退，淮因西擊羌。

translations.literal: Wei withdrew; Huai therefore struck west against the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Wei retired, Guo Huai turned west against Qiang tribes.

sentences.zh: 艾曰：「賊去未遠，或能復還，宜分諸軍以備不虞。

translations.literal: Ai said: "The enemy has not gone far—they may return; divide the armies against surprises."
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai warned Jiang Wei might double back—split forces.

sentences.zh: 」於是留艾屯白水北。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ai was left to encamp north of the White Water.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed north of the Bailong River.

sentences.zh: 三日，維遣廖化自白水南向艾結營。

translations.literal: On the third day Jiang Wei sent Liao Hua from south of the Bailong to tie Ai with camps.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Liao Hua appeared south of the Bailong facing Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 艾謂諸將曰：「維今卒還，吾軍人少，法當來渡而不作橋。

translations.literal: Ai told the generals: "Wei returned abruptly—we are few—by rule they should ford yet build no bridge."
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai saw Jiang Wei's rapid return and thin Wei ranks—a feint; no bridge meant no real crossing.

sentences.zh: 此維使化持吾，令不得還。

translations.literal: This is Wei using Hua to hold us so we cannot return.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Hua pins us while Jiang Wei strikes elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 維必自東襲取洮城。

translations.literal: Wei must himself raid Taocheng from the east.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei aims east at Taocheng.

sentences.zh: 」洮城在水北，去艾屯六十里。

translations.literal: Taocheng lies north of the river, sixty li from Ai's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Taocheng sits sixty li north across the water.

sentences.zh: 艾即夜潛軍徑到，維果來渡，而艾先至據城，得以不敗。

translations.literal: Ai immediately marched by night straight there—Wei indeed tried to ford but Ai seized the town first and escaped defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai marched overnight, seized Taocheng before Jiang Wei, and averted disaster.

sentences.zh: 賜爵關內侯，加討寇將軍，後遷城陽太守。

translations.literal: He was granted noble rank within the passes and promoted general who smashes bandits; later promoted governor of Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded with noble rank within the passes and general who smashes bandits, then governor of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 是時并州右賢王劉豹並為一部，艾上言曰：

translations.literal: At this time Bingzhou Right Worthy King Liu Bao merged into one tribe; Ai memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: When Bingzhou's Liu Bao unified his tribe, Deng Ai submitted:

sentences.zh: 戎狄獸心，不以義親，強則侵暴，弱則內附，故周宣有玁狁之寇，漢祖有平城之圍。

translations.literal: "Barbarians have beasts' hearts—they cleave not to righteousness by kinship; strong they raid, weak they attach inward—thus King Xuan suffered Xianyun raids and Gaozu endured Pingcheng's siege."
translations.idiomatic: Nomads are faithless—strong they raid, weak they submit—like Zhou against Xianyun or Han at Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 每匈奴一盛，為前代重患。

translations.literal: Whenever the Xiongnu flourished they became grave trouble for former dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Every Xiongnu revival imperiled China.

sentences.zh: 自單于在外，莫能牽制長卑。

translations.literal: Since the Chanyu stayed abroad none could rein him from afar.
translations.idiomatic: With the Chanyu beyond reach court control grew slack.

sentences.zh: 誘而致之，使來入侍。

translations.literal: They were enticed to enter court service.
translations.idiomatic: The court baited him into attendance.

sentences.zh: 由是羌夷失統，合散無主。

translations.literal: Thus Qiang and Yi lost cohesion—gathered or scattered they had no lord.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier tribes lost unified leadership.

sentences.zh: 以單于在內，萬里順軌。

translations.literal: With the Chanyu inside, ten thousand li obeyed the track.
translations.idiomatic: While the Chanyu stayed at court the steppes obeyed.

sentences.zh: 今單于之尊日疏，外土之威浸重，則胡虜不可不深備也。

translations.literal: Now the Chanyu's dignity daily ebbs while outer tribes' power swells—Hu raiders must be guarded closely.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Chanyu fades while border bands rise—prepare for nomads.

sentences.zh: 聞劉豹部有叛胡，可因叛割為二國，以分其勢。

translations.literal: I hear Liu Bao's band harbors rebel Hu—use the split to carve two states and divide their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Split Liu Bao's rebel Hu into two polities.

sentences.zh: 去卑功顯前朝，而子不繼業，宜加其子顯號，使居雁門。

translations.literal: Qubei earned merit under the former dynasty yet his son inherits nothing—grant the son a lofty title and station him at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Honor Qubei's heir at Yanmen for past service.

sentences.zh: 離國弱寇，追錄舊勳，此禦邊長計也。

translations.literal: Splitting states weakens raiders and records old merit—this is the long plan for the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Divide and weaken—sound border policy."

sentences.zh: 又陳：“羌胡與民同處者，宜以漸出之，使居民表崇廉恥之教，塞姦宄之路。

translations.literal: He also stated: "Where Qiang and Hu dwell among commoners, gradually move them out so citizens learn shame and block villainy."
translations.idiomatic: He urged relocating mixed barbarian settlements to teach Chinese propriety.

sentences.zh: ”大將軍司馬景王新輔政，多納用焉。

translations.literal: Grand General Sima Jingwang had newly assumed government and adopted much of this.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi newly in power adopted many proposals.

sentences.zh: 遷汝南太守，至則尋求昔所厚己吏父，久已死，遣吏祭之，重遺其母，舉其子與計吏。

translations.literal: Promoted governor of Runan, on arrival he sought the clerk's father who had favored him—long dead—sent officers to sacrifice, gave generously to the mother, and raised the son to accounts clerk.
translations.idiomatic: As Runan governor he honored his poor patron's memory—sacrificed at his grave, enriched his widow, promoted his son.

sentences.zh: 艾所在，荒野開闢，軍民並豐。

translations.literal: Wherever Ai went, wild lands opened and soldiers and civilians alike prospered.
translations.idiomatic: His postings turned wasteland fertile for army and people.

sentences.zh: 諸葛恪圍合肥新城，不克，退歸。

translations.literal: Zhuge Ke besieged Hefei's new fortress without success and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke failed at Hefei new town and retreated.

sentences.zh: 艾言景王曰：「孫權已沒，大臣未附，吳名宗大族，皆有部曲，阻兵仗勢，足以建命。

translations.literal: Ai told Jingwang: "Sun Quan is gone; great ministers are not yet loyal; Wu's powerful clans each command private troops and could dictate orders."
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai told Sima Shi that Wu's great houses each ran private armies.

sentences.zh: 恪新秉國政，而內無其主，不念撫恤上下以立根基，競於外事，虐用其民，悉國之眾，頓於堅城，死者萬數，載禍而歸，此恪獲罪之日也。

translations.literal: Ke newly holds state power yet lacks an inner sovereign—he does not soothe superiors and inferiors to plant roots but races after foreign ventures, cruelly exploits the people, throws the whole nation's host against a stubborn wall—dead count in myriads—and bears calamity home—this is the day Ke earns guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke seized power without consolidating within—he battered his army on Hefei's walls and marched ruin home.

sentences.zh: 昔子胥、吳起、商鞅、樂毅皆見任時君，主沒而敗。

translations.literal: Formerly Wu Zi, Wu Qi, Shang Yang, and Yue Yi each enjoyed their sovereign's trust yet fell when the lord died.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zi, Wu Qi, Shang Yang, and Yue Yi fell once their patrons died.

sentences.zh: 況恪才非四賢，而不慮大患，其亡可待也。

translations.literal: Moreover Ke's talent falls short of those four sages yet he ignores great peril—his ruin awaits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke is less able yet blind to danger—doom nears.

sentences.zh: 」恪歸，果見誅。

translations.literal: Ke returned and indeed was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke died on his return.

sentences.zh: 遷兗州刺史，加振威將軍。

translations.literal: Promoted Inspector of Yan Province with added title general who shakes might.
translations.idiomatic: He became inspector of Yan with general who shakes might.

sentences.zh: 上言曰：「國之所急，惟農與戰，國富則兵強，兵強則戰勝。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "What the state urgently needs is farming and war—wealth makes armies strong; strong armies win."
translations.idiomatic: He urged agriculture as foundation of military strength.

sentences.zh: 然農者，勝之本也。

translations.literal: Yet farming is victory's root.
translations.idiomatic: Farming underpins victory.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰『足食足兵』，食在兵前也。

translations.literal: Confucius said 'ample food, ample arms'—food comes before arms.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius listed food before arms.

sentences.zh: 上無設爵之勸，則下無財畜之功。

translations.literal: Without noble ranks to encourage above there is no urge to accumulate wealth below.
translations.idiomatic: Without incentives none hoard grain.

sentences.zh: 今使考績之賞，在於積粟富民，則交遊之路絕，浮華之原塞矣。」

translations.literal: Now let merit reviews reward grain-rich households—then factional networking ends and flashy ostentation dries up."
translations.idiomatic: Reward harvests in performance reviews—cut patronage and glitter."

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公即尊位，進封方城亭侯。

translations.literal: When Duke Gaoguixiang assumed the throne Ai was advanced to village marquis of Fangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoguixiang's accession brought village marquis of Fangcheng.

sentences.zh: 毌丘儉作亂，遣健步齎書，欲疑惑大眾，艾斬之，兼道進軍，先趣樂嘉城，作浮橋。

translations.literal: When Guanqiu Jian rebelled he sent runners with letters to confuse the host—Ai executed them and marched by forced march to seize Lecia first and build floating bridges.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian's propaganda runners died on Deng Ai's sword; he raced to Lecia and threw pontoon bridges.

sentences.zh: 司馬景王至，遂據之。

translations.literal: When Sima Jingwang arrived, they occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi arrived and held Lecia.

sentences.zh: 文欽以後大軍破敗於城下，艾追之至丘頭。

translations.literal: After Wen Qin's army was crushed beneath the walls Ai pursued as far as Qiutou.
translations.idiomatic: After Wen Qin's rout Deng Ai chased him to Qiutou.

sentences.zh: 欽奔吳。

translations.literal: Qin fled to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin escaped to Wu.

sentences.zh: 吳大將軍孫峻等號十萬眾，將渡江，鎮東將軍諸葛誕遣艾據肥陽，艾以與賊勢相遠，非要害之地，輒移屯附亭，遣泰山太守諸葛緒等於黎漿拒戰，遂走之。

translations.literal: Wu grand general Sun Jun and others claimed 100,000 men intent on crossing the Yangzi; general who guards the east Zhuge Dan ordered Ai to hold Feiyang—Ai judged it far from the enemy and not vital, shifted camp to Futing, sent Taishan governor Zhuge Xu and others to fight at Lijiang, and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun threatened to cross with 100,000 men; Zhuge Dan posted Deng Ai at Feiyang—Ai relocated to Futing and routed Wu at Lijiang via Zhuge Xu.

sentences.zh: 其年徵拜長水校尉。

translations.literal: That year he was summoned as colonel of the everlasting troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as colonel of the everlasting troops.

sentences.zh: 以破欽等功，進封方城鄉侯，行安西將軍。

translations.literal: For merit against Qin he was advanced to township marquis of Fangcheng and acted as general who pacifies the west.
translations.idiomatic: Breaking Wen Qin earned township marquis of Fangcheng and acting general who pacifies the west.

sentences.zh: 解雍州刺史王經圍於狄道，姜維退駐鍾提，乃以艾為安西將軍，假節、領護東羌校尉。

translations.literal: He relieved Yongzhou Inspector Wang Jing's siege at Didao—Jiang Wei withdrew to Zhongti—thereupon Ai became general who pacifies the west with jie staff and concurrent protector-general of eastern Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: After lifting Wang Jing at Didao he became general who pacifies the west with jie authority over eastern Qiang.

sentences.zh: 議者多以為維力已竭，未能更出。

translations.literal: Critics mostly thought Jiang Wei's strength was spent and he could not strike again.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion wrote Jiang Wei off as exhausted.

sentences.zh: 艾曰：

translations.literal: Ai said:
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai said:

sentences.zh: 洮西之敗，非小失也；

translations.literal: The defeat west of the Tao was no small loss;
translations.idiomatic: The Tao river rout was no minor setback;

sentences.zh: 破軍殺將，倉廩空虛，百姓流離，幾於危亡​​。

translations.literal: armies broken, generals slain, granaries empty, commoners scattered—close to peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: armies shattered, stores bare, people fled—the realm tottered.

sentences.zh: 今以策言之，彼有乘勝之勢，我有虛弱之實，一也。

translations.literal: Judging by strategy, they hold victory's momentum while we show weakness—first point.
translations.idiomatic: They ride victory; we show weakness—that is one.

sentences.zh: 彼上下相習，五兵犀利，我將易兵新，器杖未復，二也。

translations.literal: They are practiced top to bottom and weapons keen; our commanders are new and weapons not replenished—second point.
translations.idiomatic: Their troops drill together with sharp arms; our officers rotate and gear unready—two.

sentences.zh: 彼以船行，吾以陸軍，勞逸不同，三也。

translations.literal: They move by boat while we march overland—ease differs—third point.
translations.idiomatic: They sail while we march—third.

sentences.zh: 狄道、隴西、南安、祁山，各當有守，彼專為一，我分為四，四也。

translations.literal: Didao, Longxi, Nan'an, and Qishan each need garrison—they strike as one while we split four ways—fourth point.
translations.idiomatic: We guard four sectors; they concentrate—four.

sentences.zh: 從南安、隴西，因食羌谷，若趣祁山，熟麥千頃，為之縣餌，五也。

translations.literal: From Nan'an and Longxi they can feed on Qiang grain; aiming at Qishan a thousand qing of ripe wheat hangs like bait—fifth point.
translations.idiomatic: They can live off Qiang grain toward Qishan—ripe wheat lures them—five.

sentences.zh: 賊有黠數，其來必矣。

translations.literal: The enemy is cunning and numerous—they will surely come.
translations.idiomatic: A clever foe in force will come.

sentences.zh: 頃之，維果向祁山，聞艾已有備，乃回從董亭趣南安，艾據武城山以相持。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Jiang Wei indeed marched toward Qishan; hearing Ai already had defenses, he doubled back from Dongting toward Nan'an; Ai held Wucheng Mountain and contested him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei headed for Qishan but veered toward Nan'an from Dong Pavilion when he found Deng Ai ready; they grappled for Wucheng Mountain.

sentences.zh: 維與艾爭險，不克，其夜，渡渭東行，緣山趣上邽，艾與戰於段谷，大破之。

translations.literal: Wei and Ai vied for narrows without success; that night he crossed east over the Wei and skirted mountains toward Shanggui—Ai fought him at Duangu Valley and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: That night Jiang Wei forded the Wei eastward; Deng Ai shattered him at Duangu.

sentences.zh: 甘露元年詔曰：「逆賊姜維連年狡黠，民夷騷動，西土不寧。

translations.literal: Ganlu first year edict stated: "The rebel Jiang Wei for years has been crafty—folk and barbarians stirred—the west unquiet.
translations.idiomatic: The Ganlu 260 edict condemned Jiang Wei's raids for unsettling the west.

sentences.zh: 艾籌畫有方，忠勇奮發，斬將十數，馘首千計；

translations.literal: Ai planned skillfully, loyal and brave—beheaded more than ten generals and counted heads by thousands;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai slew dozens of officers and thousands of soldiers.

sentences.zh: 國威震於巴、蜀，武聲揚於江、岷。

translations.literal: national awe shook Ba and Shu; martial fame rose along Jiang and Min.
translations.idiomatic: Wei prestige shook Shu and his fame echoed along the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 今以艾為鎮西將軍、都督隴右諸軍事，進封鄧侯。

translations.literal: Now appoint Ai general who guards the west and superintender of Longyou military affairs; advance enfeoffment to marquis of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: He became general who guards the west, commander of Longyou, and marquis of Deng.

sentences.zh: 分五百戶封子忠為亭侯。

translations.literal: Divide five hundred households to enfeoff son Zhong as village marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Son Deng Zhong received a village marquisate of 500 households.

sentences.zh: 」二年，拒姜維於長城，維退還。

translations.literal: Second year he resisted Jiang Wei at Changcheng—Wei withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he blocked Jiang Wei at Changcheng and Jiang Wei retreated.

sentences.zh: 遷征西將軍，前後增邑凡六千六百戶。

translations.literal: Promoted general who conquers the west; total added fief reached 6,600 households.
translations.idiomatic: As general who conquers the west his fief grew to 6,600 households.

sentences.zh: 景元三年，又破維於侯和，維卻保沓中。

translations.literal: Jingyuan third year he again defeated Wei at Hehou—Wei fell back to Tazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan 3: broken again at Hehou, Jiang Wei withdrew to Tazhong.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，詔諸軍征蜀，大將軍司馬文王皆指授節度，使艾與維相綴連；

translations.literal: Fourth year autumn edict ordered armies to conquer Shu; Grand General Sima Wenwang directed all movements—ordering Ai to tie Wei down;
translations.idiomatic: Autumn Jingyuan 4: Sima Zhao orchestrated the Shu invasion—Deng Ai was to fix Jiang Wei.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史諸葛緒要維，令不得歸。

translations.literal: Yongzhou Inspector Zhuge Xu blocked Wei so he could not return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Xu was to cut Jiang Wei's retreat.

sentences.zh: 艾遣天水太守王頎等直攻維營，隴西太守牽弘等邀其前，金城太守楊欣等詣甘松。

translations.literal: Ai sent Tianshui governor Wang Qi and others straight against Wei's camp; Longxi governor Qian Hong blocked his front; Jincheng governor Yang Xin went toward Gansong.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai attacked Jiang Wei's camp from three directions via Wang Qi, Qian Hong, and Yang Xin.

sentences.zh: 維聞鍾會諸軍已入漢中，引退還。

translations.literal: Wei heard Zhong Hui's armies had entered Hanzhong and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Zhong Hui had penetrated Hanzhong, Jiang Wei pulled back.

sentences.zh: 欣等追躡於強川口，大戰，維敗走。

translations.literal: Xin and others pursued through Qiangchuankou—great battle—Wei fled defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xin overtook him at Qiangchuankou and broke him.

sentences.zh: 聞雍州已塞道屯橋頭，從孔函谷入北道，欲出雍州後。

translations.literal: Hearing Yongzhou had sealed the road at Bridgehead, he entered the northern road through Konghan Valley to emerge behind Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Bridgehead blocked, he slipped through Konghan Valley to flank Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 諸葛緒聞之，卻還三十里。

translations.literal: Zhuge Xu heard and withdrew thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Xu fell back thirty li.

sentences.zh: 維入北道三十餘里，聞緒軍卻，尋還，從橋頭過，緒趣截維，較一日不及。

translations.literal: Wei penetrated the northern route thirty-some li—hearing Xu's army withdrew he hurried back, crossed Bridgehead—Xu raced to intercept Wei—missed by one day.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei doubled back for Bridgehead but Zhuge Xu missed him by a day.

sentences.zh: 維遂東引，還守劍閣。

translations.literal: Wei therefore marched east and defended Jiange.
translations.idiomatic: He raced east to hold Jiange.

sentences.zh: 鍾會攻維未能克。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui attacked Wei but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui stalled against Jiang Wei.

sentences.zh: 艾上言：「今賊摧折，宜遂乘之，從陰平由邪徑經漢德陽亭趣涪，出劍閣西百里，去成都三百餘里，奇兵衝其腹心。

translations.literal: Ai memorialized: "Now the foe is broken—we ought strike—from Yinping by hidden trail past Han's Deyang pavilion toward Fu—west of Jiange a hundred li—three hundred odd li from Chengdu—strike the belly with surprise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai urged the Yinping shortcut past Deyang to Fu—behind Jiange—to stab Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 劍閣之守必還赴涪，則會方軌而進；

translations.literal: Jiange's defenders must hurry back to Fu—then Hui advances on parallel tracks;
translations.idiomatic: Jiange's garrison would rush to Fu—freeing Zhong Hui to advance.

sentences.zh: 劍閣之軍不還，則應涪之兵寡矣。

translations.literal: if Jiange's army does not return, Fu's defenders will be few.
translations.idiomatic: If not, Fu falls lightly guarded.

sentences.zh: 軍誌有之曰：『攻其無備，出其不意。

translations.literal: The military canon says: strike unwatched—strike unanticipated.
translations.idiomatic: Sunzi: strike where unwary.

sentences.zh: 』今掩其空虛，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: Now mask their emptiness—shattering them is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Hit the hollow—a sure win."

sentences.zh: 冬十月，艾自陰平道行無人之地七百餘里，鑿山通道，造作橋閣。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month Ai went seven hundred li through uninhabited Yinping terrain—cut roads through mountains—built bridges on cliffs.
translations.idiomatic: In winter Deng Ai carved seven hundred li through Yinping.

sentences.zh: 山高谷深，至為艱險，又糧運將匱，頻於危殆。

translations.literal: Mountains high valleys deep—extremely perilous—grain convoys nearly exhausted—often at mortal risk.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies failed on deadly cliffs.

sentences.zh: 艾以氈自裹，推轉而下。

translations.literal: Ai wrapped himself in felt and rolled downhill.
translations.idiomatic: He rolled down slopes wrapped in felt.

sentences.zh: 將士皆攀木緣崖，魚貫而進。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers all climbed trees hugged cliffs—fish-strung advance.
translations.idiomatic: Men scaled cliffs in single file.

sentences.zh: 先登至江由，蜀守將馬邈降。

translations.literal: Van reached Jiangyou—Shu defender Ma Miao surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Miao surrendered Jiangyou.

sentences.zh: 蜀衛將軍諸葛瞻自涪還綿竹，列陳待艾。

translations.literal: Shu guard-general Zhuge Zhan returned from Fu to Mianzhu and drew up ranks awaiting Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Zhan barred Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 艾遣子惠唐亭侯忠等出其右，司馬師纂等出其左。

translations.literal: Ai sent son Zhong of Tang village marquisate and others against his right wing—Major Shi Zuan against his left.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Zhong and Shi Zuan attacked both flanks.

sentences.zh: 忠、纂戰不利，並退還，曰：「賊未可擊。

translations.literal: Zhong and Zuan fought poorly and withdrew saying "the bandits cannot be struck."
translations.idiomatic: They fell back claiming the enemy too strong.

sentences.zh: 」艾怒曰：「存亡之分，在此一舉，何不可之有？

translations.literal: Ai raged: "Survival hangs on this stroke—how can it be impossible?
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai thundered that victory rode on one clash.

sentences.zh: 」乃叱忠、纂等，將斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he berated Zhong and Zuan—prepared to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: He nearly beheaded his son and Shi Zuan.

sentences.zh: 忠、纂馳還更戰，大破之，斬瞻及尚書張遵等首，進軍到雒。

translations.literal: Zhong and Zuan galloped back and renewed battle—greatly defeated them—beheaded Zhan and secretary Zhang Zun and others—advanced to Luo.
translations.idiomatic: They rallied, smashed Zhuge Zhan, took heads to Luo.

sentences.zh: 劉禪遣使奉皇帝璽綬，為箋詣艾請降。

translations.literal: Liu Shan dispatched envoys bearing imperial seals—submitting memorial begging Ai accept surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan sent seals and surrender plea.

sentences.zh: 艾至成都，禪率太子諸王及群臣六十餘人面縛輿櫬詣軍門，艾執節解縛焚櫬，受而宥之。

translations.literal: Ai reached Chengdu—Shan led crown prince, kings, and sixty-odd ministers bound with coffins to camp gate—Ai holding insignia loosed bonds burned coffins accepted and spared them.
translations.idiomatic: At Chengdu Liu Shan came bound with a bier; Deng Ai freed him per ritual.

sentences.zh: 檢禦將士，無所虜略，綏納降附，使復舊業，蜀人稱焉。

translations.literal: He restrained troops from plunder—pacified surrenderers—restored old occupations—Shu people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: No looting—people restored—Shu praised him.

sentences.zh: 輒依鄧禹故事，承制拜禪行驃騎將軍，太子奉車、諸王駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Following Deng Yu precedent he by imperial warrant named Shan acting flying-cavalry general—crown prince carriage attendant—kings horse attendant chief.
translations.idiomatic: Like Deng Yu he breveted Liu Shan and sons.

sentences.zh: 蜀群司各隨高下拜為王官，或領艾官屬。

translations.literal: Shu officials each appointed Wei offices according rank—or attached to Ai's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Shu bureaucracy folded into Wei appointments.

sentences.zh: 以師纂領益州刺史，隴西太守牽弘等領蜀中諸郡。

translations.literal: Ordered Shi Zuan acting Inspector of Yi—Qian Hong and others held Shu commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zuan governed Yi; Hong held counties.

sentences.zh: 使於綿竹築臺以為京觀，用彰戰功。

translations.literal: Built mound platform at Mianzhu as corpse mound—displaying martial merit.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a victory mound at Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 士卒死事者，皆與蜀兵同共埋藏。

translations.literal: Soldiers who died in battle were buried together with Shu dead.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Shu dead were buried together.

sentences.zh: 艾深自矜伐，謂蜀士大夫曰：「諸君賴遭某，故得有今日耳。

translations.literal: Ai deeply boasted to Shu gentry: "You gentlemen owe your survival today to me.
translations.idiomatic: He boasted that Shu elite owed him survival.

sentences.zh: 若遇吳漢之徒，已殄滅矣。

translations.literal: Had you met Wu Han's sort—you would already be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Han would have exterminated you."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「姜維自一時雄兒也，與某相值，故窮耳。

translations.literal: He also said: "Jiang Wei was a mere champion of an hour—matched against me—thus ruined.
translations.idiomatic: He mocked Jiang Wei as beaten by him."

sentences.zh: 」有識者笑之。

translations.literal: Men of insight laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Knowledged Shu smiled.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔曰：「艾曜威奮武，深入虜庭，斬將搴旗，梟其鯨鯢，使僭號之主，稽首系頸，歷世逋誅，一朝而平。

translations.literal: Twelfth month edict: "Ai displayed might—deep struck barbarian court—beheaded generals tore banners—beheaded leviathans—made pretender ruler bind throat bow—generations evaded execution—leveled in one morn.
translations.idiomatic: Winter edict hailed Deng Ai's Shu conquest.

sentences.zh: 兵不逾時，戰不終日，雲徹席捲，盪定巴蜀。

translations.literal: Weapons crossed not whole seasons—battles lasted not whole days—clouds rolled swept clean—Ba-Shu pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Swift victory cleared Shu.

sentences.zh: 雖白起破強楚，韓信克勁趙，吳漢禽子陽，亞夫滅七國，計功論美，不足比勳也。

translations.literal: Though Bai Qi broke mighty Chu, Han Xin subdued fierce Zhao, Wu Han seized Ziyang, Zhou Yafu extinguished seven kingdoms—measuring merit and praise—not enough to compare his merit.
translations.idiomatic: His feat rivaled Bai Qi, Han Xin, Wu Han, Zhou Yafu.

sentences.zh: 其以艾為太尉，增邑二萬戶，封子二人亭侯，各食邑千戶。」

translations.literal: Let Ai be grand commandant—increase fief twenty thousand households—enfeoff two sons village marquis—each thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: Grand commandant, +20,000 households, two sons ennobled."

sentences.zh: 〈袁子曰：諸葛亮，重人也，而驟用蜀兵，此知小國弱民難以久存也。

translations.literal: Master Yuan states: Zhuge Liang was prudent yet pressed Shu troops—knowing small states weak peoples cannot long endure.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhun notes Zhuge Liang drafted Shu relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 今國家一舉而滅蜀，自征伐之功，未有如此之速者也。

translations.literal: Now the state extinguished Shu in one blow—since punitive wars none so swift.
translations.idiomatic: No campaign matched its speed.

sentences.zh: 方鄧艾以萬人入江由之危險，鍾會以二十萬眾留劍閣而不得進，三軍之士已飢，艾雖戰勝克將，使劉禪數日不降，則二將之軍難以反矣。

translations.literal: When Deng Ai led ten thousand through Jiangyou's peril while Zhong Hui's two hundred thousand stalled at Jiange—three armies already starving—though Ai conquered generals had Liu Shan delayed surrender days—both generals' armies could hardly return.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan warns one slip would have trapped Deng Ai and Zhong Hui.

sentences.zh: 故功業如此之難也。

translations.literal: Thus merit so hard-earned.
translations.idiomatic: Victory hung by a thread.

sentences.zh: 國家前有壽春之役，後有滅蜀之勞，百姓貧而倉禀虛，故小國之慮，在於時立功以自存，大國之慮，在於既勝而力竭，成功之後，戒懼之時也。〉

translations.literal: State earlier had Shouchun campaign later Shu pacification—people poor granaries empty—thus small state's worry is timely merit to survive—great state's worry is exhaustion after victory—after success comes hour of vigilance."
translations.idiomatic: Small states must seize moments; great states guard against exhaustion after triumph."

sentences.zh: 艾言司馬文王曰：

translations.literal: Ai addressed Sima Wenwang:
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai wrote Sima Zhao:

sentences.zh: 兵有先聲而後實者，今因平蜀之勢以乘吳，吳人震恐，席捲之時也。

translations.literal: War has reputation before substance—now ride Shu pacification to strike Wu—Wu terrified—time to sweep.
translations.idiomatic: Strike Wu while fear spreads.

sentences.zh: 然大舉之後，將士疲勞，不可便用，且徐緩之；

translations.literal: Yet after great effort troops weary—cannot use at once—rather temporize slowly;
translations.idiomatic: Rest the army first.

sentences.zh: 留隴右兵二萬人，蜀兵二萬人，煮鹽興冶，為軍農要用，並作舟船，豫順流之事，然後發使告以利害，吳必歸化，可不征而定也。

translations.literal: Leave twenty thousand Longyou troops twenty thousand Shu troops—boil salt forge iron for army-agriculture essentials—build boats—prepare downstream matters—then dispatch envoys stating profit and harm—Wu must submit—may pacify without campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison 40,000, build industry and fleet, then diplomatic surrender.

sentences.zh: 今宜厚劉禪以致孫休，安士民以來遠人，若便送禪於京都，吳以為流徙，則於向化之心不勸。

translations.literal: Now ought treat Liu Shan generously to attract Sun Xiu—pacify people to draw distant folk—if hastily send Shan to capital Wu will think exile—discouraging hearts turning.
translations.idiomatic: Keep Liu Shan local to entice Wu.

sentences.zh: 宜權停留，須來年秋冬，比爾吳亦足平。

translations.literal: Ought temporarily detain until next autumn winter—by then Wu enough pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until next cool season.

sentences.zh: 以為可封禪為扶風王，錫其資財，供其左右。

translations.literal: Deemed possible enfeoff Shan as king of Fufeng—grant wealth supply attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Ennoble Liu Shan as king of Fufeng with subsidy.

sentences.zh: 郡有董卓塢，為之宮舍。

translations.literal: Commandery has Dong Zhuo's bastion—make palace lodging.
translations.idiomatic: House him in Dong Zhuo's old fort.

sentences.zh: 爵其子為公侯，食郡內縣，以顯歸命之寵。

translations.literal: Ennoble sons dukes—feed from counties within commandery—display grace of submission.
translations.idiomatic: His sons get noble ranks in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 開廣陵、城陽以待吳人，則畏威懷德，望風而從矣。

translations.literal: Open Guangling Chengyang to await Wu people—then awe virtue blend—they yield at rumor.
translations.idiomatic: Prepare coastal havens for Wu defectors.

sentences.zh: 文王使監軍衛瓘喻艾：「事當須報，不宜輒行。

translations.literal: Wenwang ordered army supervisor Wei Guan instruct Ai: "Affairs must be reported—ought not act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao told Wei Guan to rein Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 」艾重言曰：「銜命征行，奉指授之策，元惡既服；

translations.literal: Ai emphasized: "Bearing orders on campaign following commander-in-chief's plan—chief evil already submitted;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai cited acting authority.

sentences.zh: 至於承制拜假，以安初附，謂合權宜。

translations.literal: As for imperial warrant appointments to pacify new adherents—deemed fitting expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Brevet appointments stabilized Shu.

sentences.zh: 今蜀舉眾歸命，地盡南海，東接吳會，宜早鎮定若待國命，往復道途，延引日月。

translations.literal: Now Shu masses submit—land reaches south sea—east joins Wu-Yue—ought pacify early—if await court orders—round-trip roads delay months.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang round-trip wastes time.

sentences.zh: 春秋之義，大夫出疆，有可以安社稷，利國家，專之可也。

translations.literal: Spring and Autumn meaning—great ministers abroad—what can secure altars benefit state—may decide alone.
translations.idiomatic: Classics allow initiative abroad.

sentences.zh: 今吳未賓；

translations.literal: Now Wu not yet guest;
translations.idiomatic: Wu still independent.

sentences.zh: 勢與蜀連，不可拘常以失事機。

translations.literal: situation connects Shu—cannot cling routine lose opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Cannot miss timing.

sentences.zh: 兵法，進不求名，退不避罪，艾雖無古人之節，終不自嫌以損於國也。

translations.literal: Military law—advance not seeking fame—retreat not avoiding guilt—Ai though lacks ancient integrity—finally will not suspect self harming state.
translations.idiomatic: Art of War: duty over fame—Deng Ai claims loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」鍾會、胡烈、師纂等皆白艾所作悖逆，變釁以結。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui Hu Lie Shi Zuan and others all reported Ai acted rebelliously—changed banners forming conspiracy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui accused Deng Ai of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 詔書檻車徵艾。

translations.literal: Edict summoned Ai in cage cart.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial order arrested Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：艾仰天歎曰：「艾忠臣也，一至此乎！

translations.literal: Annals of Wei relates Ai sighed skyward: "Ai is loyal minister—reached this!
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai cried foul.

sentences.zh: 白起之酷，復見於今日矣。」〉

translations.literal: Bai Qi's cruelty—seen again today."
translations.idiomatic: Like Bai Qi's fate."

sentences.zh: 艾父子既囚，鍾會至成都，先送艾，然後作亂。

translations.literal: Ai father and son imprisoned—Zhong Hui reached Chengdu—first sent Ai—then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui shipped Deng Ai off then mutinied.

sentences.zh: 會已死，艾本營將士追出艾檻車，迎還。

translations.literal: After Hui died Ai original camp soldiers chased out cage cart—welcomed return.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai's troops freed him.

sentences.zh: 瓘遣田續等討艾，遇於綿竹西，斬之。

translations.literal: Guan sent Tian Xu and others campaign Ai—met west of Mianzhu—executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan's Tian Xu killed Deng Ai west of Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 子忠與艾俱死，餘子在洛陽者悉誅，徙艾妻子及孫於西域。

translations.literal: Son Zhong died with Ai—remaining sons at Luoyang all executed—relocated Ai's wife children grandchildren to western regions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong died with father; rest executed; family exiled west.

sentences.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：初艾之下江由也，以續不進，欲斬，既而捨之。

translations.literal: Han-Jin Spring and Autumn relates initially when Ai descended Jiangyou—because Xu did not advance wished execute—later spared.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai had spared Tian Xu at Jiangyou.

sentences.zh: 及瓘遣續，謂曰：「可以報江由之辱矣。

translations.literal: When Guan dispatched Xu said: "Can repay Jiangyou insult.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan told Xu to settle scores.

sentences.zh: 」杜預言於眾曰：「伯玉其不免乎！

translations.literal: Du Yu declared to crowd: "Boyu surely cannot escape!
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu predicted Wei Guan's doom.

sentences.zh: 身為名士，位望已高，既無德音，又不御下以正，是小人而乘君子之器，將何以堪其責乎？

translations.literal: Body famed gentleman rank outlook already high—without virtuous reputation nor ruling subordinates upright—small man riding gentleman's vessel—how bear responsibility?
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu criticized Wei Guan's character.

sentences.zh: 」瓘聞之，不俟駕而謝。

translations.literal: Guan hearing—did not await carriage—went apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan rushed to apologize.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：師纂亦與艾俱死。

translations.literal: Sayings of Age relates Shi Zuan also died with Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zuan died with Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 纂性急少恩，死之日體無完皮。〉

translations.literal: Zuan nature urgent little kindness—day died body lacked intact skin."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zuan's corpse was mutilated."

sentences.zh: 初，艾當伐蜀，夢坐山上而有流水，以問殄虜護軍爰邵。

translations.literal: Earlier when Ai about to conquer Shu dreamed sitting mountain with flowing water—asked protector-general Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Before Shu campaign Deng Ai dreamed mountain stream—asked Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 邵曰：「按易卦，山上有水曰蹇。

translations.literal: Shao said: "According to Changes hexagram water atop mountain is Obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao cited hexagram Jian.

sentences.zh: 蹇繇曰：『蹇利西南，不利東北。

translations.literal: Obstruction commentary says: Obstruction profits southwest—not northeast.
translations.idiomatic: Judgment favors southwest.

sentences.zh: 』孔子曰：『蹇利西南，往有功也；

translations.literal: Confucius says: Obstruction profits southwest—going has merit;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: southwest wins merit.

sentences.zh: 不利東北，其道窮也。

translations.literal: Not profitable northeast—its way exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast path ends.

sentences.zh: 』往必克蜀，殆不還乎！

translations.literal: Going certainly conquers Shu—perhaps not return!
translations.idiomatic: Victory in Shu—no return home.

sentences.zh: 」艾憮然不樂。

translations.literal: Ai sorrowful unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai grew gloomy.

sentences.zh: 〈荀綽《冀州記》曰：邵起自幹吏，位至衛尉。

translations.literal: Xun Chuo's Ji Prefecture Record relates Shao rose from clerk to commandant of guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao rose clerk to commandant.

sentences.zh: 長子翰，河東太守。

translations.literal: Eldest son Han—governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Son Han governed Hedong.

sentences.zh: 中子敞，大司農。

translations.literal: Middle son Chang—minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Son Chang became minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 少子倩，字君幼，寬厚有器局，勤於當世，歷位冀州刺史、太子右衛率。

translations.literal: The youngest son Qian, courtesy name Junyou, was generous in bearing and diligent in his age—served as Inspector of Ji, right guard rate of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Youngest son Qian, styled Junyou, served as inspector of Ji and right guard of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 翰子俞，字世都，清貞貴素，辯於論議，採公孫龍之辭以談微理。

translations.literal: Han's son Yu, courtesy name Shidu, chaste, noble, plain, skilled in disputation—borrowed Gongsun Long's sophistry to discuss subtle principles.
translations.idiomatic: Han's son Yu, styled Shidu, was a debater in the Gongsun Long manner.

sentences.zh: 少有能名，辟太尉府，稍歷顯位，至侍中中書令，遷為監。

translations.literal: In youth he had a capable name; summoned to grand commandant's office; gradually rose to prominent rank—reached palace attendant and palace secretary—promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the commandant's office to palace secretary and director.

sentences.zh: 臣松之按：蹇彖辭云「蹇利西南，往得中也」，不云「有功」；

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes: the Obstruction tuan commentary says 'Obstruction profits southwest—going attains center'—it does not say 'has merit'.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi: the Tuan line reads 'attains center' not 'merit'.

sentences.zh: 下云「利見大人，往有功也」。〉

translations.literal: Below it says 'Profitable to see the great man—going has merit'.
translations.idiomatic: The next line adds 'merit' with the great man.

sentences.zh: 艾心懷至忠而荷反逆之名，平定巴蜀而受夷滅之誅，臣竊悼之。

translations.literal: Ai cherished utmost loyalty yet bore the name of rebel—pacified Ba-Shu yet suffered extermination execution—your servant privately grieves.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zhuo (memorial) says Deng Ai was loyal yet called traitor—grieved his fate.

sentences.zh: 惜哉，言艾之反也！

translations.literal: Alas, speaking of Ai's rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: The claim of rebellion is false!

sentences.zh: 艾性剛急，輕犯雅俗，不能協同朋類，故莫肯理之。

translations.literal: Ai's nature was harsh and hasty—lightly offended refined custom—could not harmonize with peers—therefore none willing to straighten matters.
translations.idiomatic: His blunt pride left him few defenders.

sentences.zh: 臣敢言艾不反之狀。

translations.literal: Your servant dares state the signs Ai did not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: I prove he never rebelled.

sentences.zh: 昔姜維有斷隴右之志，艾脩治備守，積穀強兵。

translations.literal: Formerly Jiang Wei had ambition to sever Longyou—Ai repaired defenses—stored grain strengthened troops.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Longyou against Jiang Wei.

sentences.zh: 值歲凶旱，艾為區種，身被烏衣，手執耒耜，以率將士。

translations.literal: Meeting years of famine drought Ai practiced pit farming—wore black coats himself—held plow handles—to lead officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In drought he led by doing pit farming in black laborer's coat.

sentences.zh: 上下相感，莫不盡力。

translations.literal: Superiors and inferiors mutually moved—none failed to exert strength.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men gave their all.

sentences.zh: 艾持節守邊，所統萬數，而不難僕虜之勞，士民之役，非執節忠勤，孰能若此？

translations.literal: Ai holding insignia guarded frontier—commanded tens of thousands—yet did not shun labor of servants or service of soldiers and commoners—without integrity and diligence holding insignia—who could match this?
translations.idiomatic: A commander who labored like a private showed rare devotion.

sentences.zh: 故落門、段谷之戰，以少擊多，摧破強賊。

translations.literal: Thus at Luomen and Duangu battles—with few struck many—smashed strong bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He routed superior forces at Luomen and Duangu.

sentences.zh: 先帝知其可任，委艾廟勝，授以長策。

translations.literal: Late emperor knew him trustworthy—entrusted Ai temple victory—granted long stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted him with strategic command.

sentences.zh: 艾受命忘身，束馬縣車，自投死地，勇氣陵雲士眾乘勢，使劉禪君臣面縛，叉手屈膝。

translations.literal: Ai receiving orders forgot self—bound horses suspended carts—threw self into dead ground—courage overtopped clouds—soldiers rode momentum—made Liu Shan ruler and ministers bind faces fold hands kneel.
translations.idiomatic: He took Yinping at mortal risk and forced Liu Shan's surrender.

sentences.zh: 艾功名以成，當書之竹帛，傳祚萬世。

translations.literal: Ai's merit and fame accomplished—ought be written on bamboo silk—transmit blessing myriad generations.
translations.idiomatic: His deeds deserved chronicle for ages.

sentences.zh: 七十老公，反欲何求！

translations.literal: A seventy-year-old man—what further does he seek!
translations.idiomatic: What could a septuagenarian gain by rebellion?

sentences.zh: 艾誠恃養育之恩，心不自疑，矯命承制，權安社稷；

translations.literal: Ai truly relied on nurturing grace—heart did not self-doubt—counterfeit orders imperial warrant—expediently pacified altars.
translations.idiomatic: He stretched authority to stabilize Shu out of duty.

sentences.zh: 雖違常科，有合古義，原心定罪，本在可論。

translations.literal: Though violated routine statutes—accorded ancient meaning—investigate heart fix guilt—originally discussable.
translations.idiomatic: Intent matters—his acts were defensible.

sentences.zh: 鍾會忌艾威名，構成其事。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui envied Ai's martial fame—fabricated this affair.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui framed him.

sentences.zh: 忠而受誅，信而見疑，頭縣馬巿，諸子並斬，見之者垂泣，聞之者嘆息。

translations.literal: Loyal yet executed—trusted yet suspected—head hung market—sons all beheaded—those who saw wept—those who heard sighed.
translations.idiomatic: A tragedy that moved the realm.

sentences.zh: 陛下龍興，闡弘大度，釋諸嫌忌，受誅之家，不拘敘用。

translations.literal: Your Majesty dragon rising—expanding great tolerance—releasing various suspicions—families executed not restricted from employment.
translations.idiomatic: Your reign welcomes even sons of the condemned.

sentences.zh: 昔秦民憐白起之無罪，吳人傷子胥之冤酷，皆為立祠。

translations.literal: Formerly Qin people pitied Bai Qi guiltless—Wu people mourned Zixu's cruel wrong—both established shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Qin mourned Bai Qi; Wu mourned Wu Zixu.

sentences.zh: 今天下民人為艾悼心痛恨，亦猶是也。

translations.literal: Now realm's people for Ai mourn heartache hatred—also likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The people grieve Deng Ai the same way.

sentences.zh: 臣以為艾身首分離，捐棄草土，宜收屍喪，還其田宅。

translations.literal: Your servant judges Ai body head separated—cast aside grass earth—ought collect corpse mourning—return his fields houses.
translations.idiomatic: Recover his body and lands.

sentences.zh: 以平蜀之功，紹封其孫，使闔棺定諡，死無餘恨。

translations.literal: By virtue of pacifying Shu merit—continue enfeoff his grandson—make coffin closed fix posthumous title—die without leftover regret.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors for his heir would right the wrong.

sentences.zh: 赦冤魂於黃泉，收信義於後世，葬一人而天下慕其行，埋一魂而天下歸其義，所為者寡而悅者眾矣。

translations.literal: Pardon wronged ghost in yellow springs—gather faith righteousness posterity—bury one man realm admires his conduct—inter one soul realm returns to his righteousness—actions few yet pleased many.
translations.idiomatic: One burial could win the world's heart.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔曰：「艾有功勳，受罪不逃刑，而子孫為民隸，朕常愍之。

translations.literal: Ninth year edict stated: "Ai had merit—received punishment did not flee punishment—yet descendants became common bondsmen—I constantly pity them.
translations.idiomatic: Later edict pitied Deng Ai's enslaved descendants.

sentences.zh: 其以嫡孫朗為郎中。」

translations.literal: Let eldest grandson Lang be gentleman consultant."
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Lang became gentleman consultant."

sentences.zh: 艾在西時，修治障塞，築起城塢。

translations.literal: When Ai was west he repaired barrier passes—raised fort bastions.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai built western fortifications.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，羌虜大叛，頻殺刺史，涼州道斷。

translations.literal: Taishi era Qiang rebels greatly rebelled—repeatedly killed inspectors—Liangzhou road cut.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi: Liangzhou fell to Qiang raids.

sentences.zh: 吏民安全者，皆保艾所築塢焉。

translations.literal: Clerks and commoners who survived safe—all protected by Ai's built bastions.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors sheltered in Deng Ai's forts.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：咸寧中，積射將軍樊震為西戎牙門，得見辭，武帝問震所由進，震自陳曾為鄧艾伐蜀時帳下將，帝遂尋問艾，震具申艾之忠，言之流涕。

translations.literal: Sayings of Age relates: Xianning era stacked-shoots general Fan Zhen was western barbarian gate guard—audience farewell—Emperor Wu asked Zhen's advancement—Zhen stated self had been Deng Ai Shu campaign tent officer—emperor pursued asking Ai—Zhen fully declared Ai's loyalty—speaking wept.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen told Emperor Wu of Deng Ai's loyalty in tears.

sentences.zh: 先是以艾孫朗為丹水令，由此遷為定陵令。

translations.literal: Earlier because Ai's grandson Lang was Danshui magistrate—thereby promoted Dingling magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Lang rose from Danshui to Dingling.

sentences.zh: 次孫千秋有時望，光祿大夫王戎辟為掾。

translations.literal: Second grandson Qianqiu had contemporary reputation—minister of works Wang Rong summoned as aide.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Qianqiu served Wang Rong.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，朗為新都太守，未之官，在襄陽失火，朗及母妻子舉室燒死，惟子韜子行得免。

translations.literal: Yongjia era Lang was Xindu prefect—before reaching office—fire at Xiangyang—Lang with mother wife children whole household burned dead—only sons Tao Xing escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia fire killed Lang's household except two sons.

sentences.zh: 千秋先卒，二子亦燒死。〉

translations.literal: Qianqiu died earlier—two sons also burned dead."
translations.idiomatic: Qianqiu and his sons perished in the same fire."

sentences.zh: 鍾會字士季，潁川長社人，太傅繇小子也。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui, courtesy name Shiji, native of Changshe in Yingchuan—youngest son of Grand Tutor You.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui, styled Shiji, from Changshe—Zhong You's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 少敏惠夙成。

translations.literal: In youth clever and quick—matured early.
translations.idiomatic: A precocious child.

sentences.zh: 〈會為其母傳曰：「夫人張氏，字昌蒲，太原茲氏人，太傅定陵成侯之命婦也。

translations.literal: Hui wrote his mother's biography stating: "Lady Zhang, courtesy name Changpu, native of Zishi in Taiyuan—wife by ritual of Grand Tutor Order-to-Dingling accomplished marquis."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui's mother biography opens with Lady Zhang Changpu of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 世長吏二千石。

translations.literal: Generations served as officials two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Her line held 2,000-picul posts.

sentences.zh: 夫人少喪父母，充成侯家，修身正行，非禮不動，為上下所稱述。

translations.literal: Lady young lost parents—entered accomplished marquis household—cultivated self upright conduct—did not move except by ritual—praised by high and low.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned, she married Zhong Yao with perfect deportment.

sentences.zh: 貴妾孫氏，攝嫡專家，心害其賢，數讒毀無所不至。

translations.literal: Honored concubine Lady Sun—acting mistress monopolized household—heart envied her worth—repeatedly slandered without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Concubine Sun schemed against her.

sentences.zh: 孫氏辨博有智巧，言足以飾非成過，然竟不能傷也。

translations.literal: Lady Sun was eloquent clever—speech enough to whitewash wrongs forge faults—yet ultimately could not harm her.
translations.idiomatic: Sun's wit failed to displace Lady Zhang.

sentences.zh: 及妊娠，愈更嫉妒，乃置藥食中，夫人中食，覺而吐之，瞑眩者數日。

translations.literal: When pregnant—jealousy grew worse—then placed poison in food—lady ate mid-meal—felt and vomited—dizzy several days.
translations.idiomatic: Sun poisoned her food during pregnancy.

sentences.zh: 或曰：『何不向公言之？

translations.literal: Someone said: 'Why not tell lord?'
translations.idiomatic: Asked why she stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 』答曰：『嫡庶相害，破家危國，古今以為鑑誡。

translations.literal: She answered: 'Primary and secondary harming each other ruins house endangers state—ancients took this as mirror.
translations.idiomatic: She cited the peril of concubine rivalries.

sentences.zh: 假如公信我，眾誰能明其事？

translations.literal: Suppose lord trusts me—who among crowd can clarify matter?
translations.idiomatic: Who would believe her over Sun?

sentences.zh: 彼以心度我，謂我必言，固將先我；

translations.literal: She measures my heart—reckons I must speak—will strike before me;
translations.idiomatic: Sun would preempt her complaint.

sentences.zh: 事由彼發，顧不快耶！

translations.literal: Affair begun by her—would not that be satisfying!'
translations.idiomatic: Let Sun expose herself.

sentences.zh: 』遂稱疾不見。

translations.literal: Thereupon claimed illness did not appear.
translations.idiomatic: She feigned illness.

sentences.zh: 孫氏果謂成侯曰：『妾欲其得男，故飲以得男之藥，反謂毒之！

translations.literal: Lady Sun indeed told accomplished marquis: 'Concubine wished him obtain boy—therefore drank boy medicine—she instead calls it poison!'
translations.idiomatic: Sun claimed boy-sexing medicine was poison.

sentences.zh: 』成侯曰：『得男藥佳事，闇於食中與人，非人情也。

translations.literal: Accomplished marquis said: 'Boy medicine good affair—secretly in food give person—not human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao saw through Sun.

sentences.zh: 』遂訊侍者俱服，孫氏由是得罪出。

translations.literal: Thereupon interrogated attendants—all confessed—Lady Sun thereby convicted expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Servants confessed; Sun was expelled.

sentences.zh: 成侯問夫人何能不言，夫人言其故，成侯大驚，益以此賢之。

translations.literal: Accomplished marquis asked lady how could not speak—lady stated reason—accomplished marquis greatly amazed—increasingly deemed her worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao admired her restraint.

sentences.zh: 黃初六年，生會，恩寵愈隆。

translations.literal: Huangchu sixth year bore Hui—favor grew greater.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Zhong Hui in Huangchu 6.

sentences.zh: 成侯既出孫氏，更納正嫡賈氏。

translations.literal: After accomplished marquis expelled Lady Sun—again took proper wife Lady Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao then married Lady Jia as principal wife.

sentences.zh: 」臣松之按：鍾繇於時老矣，而方納正室。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes: Zhong You at that time was old—yet took proper chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Pei doubts Zhong Yao marrying a new principal wife so late.

sentences.zh: 蓋禮所云「宗子雖七十，無無主婦」之義也。

translations.literal: Probably ritual saying 'Heir son though seventy—cannot lack mistress of house' meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Rite allowed a wife for the heir line.

sentences.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：會母見寵於繇，繇為之出其夫人。

translations.literal: Annals of Wei states: Hui's mother favored by You—You for her expelled his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Alternative: Lady Zhang displaced the principal wife.

sentences.zh: 卞太后以為言，文帝詔繇復之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Bian spoke—Emperor Wen ordered You restore her.
translations.idiomatic: Bian spoke; Emperor Wen ordered restoration.

sentences.zh: 繇恚憤，將引鴆，弗獲，餐椒致噤，帝乃止。〉

translations.literal: You angry resentful—wished drink hemlock—did not obtain—ate peppers till mute—emperor then stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao tried suicide and went mute until Wen relented."

sentences.zh: 中護軍蔣濟著論，謂「觀其眸子，足以知人。

translations.literal: Central protector Jiang Ji wrote treatise stating 'Observing their pupils enough to know persons.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji: eyes reveal character.

sentences.zh: 」會年五歲，繇遣見濟，濟甚異之，曰：「非常人也。

translations.literal: Hui age five—You sent see Ji—Ji greatly marveled—said 'Not ordinary person.
translations.idiomatic: At five Jiang Ji called him extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 」及壯，有才數技藝，而博學精練名理，以夜續晝，由是獲聲譽。

translations.literal: When grown—had talent several arts—broadly learned refined principles—continued day into night—thereby gained reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Adult Zhong Hui was polymath scholar.

sentences.zh: 正始中，以為秘書郎，遷尚書中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhengshi era—made secretary gentleman—promoted secretary-attendant of masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengshi: secretary then masters of writing attendant.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：司馬景王命中書令虞松作表，再呈輒不可意，命松更定。

translations.literal: Sayings of Age states: Sima Jingwang ordered palace secretary Yu Song compose memorial—twice presented still not satisfactory—ordered Song revise.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Song could not please Sima Shi.

sentences.zh: 以經時，松思竭不能改，心苦之，形於顏色。

translations.literal: After long time Song thought exhausted could not revise—heart bitter—shown on face.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Song despaired.

sentences.zh: 會察其有憂，問松，松以實答。

translations.literal: Hui observed his worry—asked Song—Song answered truth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui noticed and learned why.

sentences.zh: 會取視，為定五字。

translations.literal: Hui took view—fixed five characters.
translations.idiomatic: He rewrote five characters.

sentences.zh: 松悅服，以呈景王，王曰：「不當爾邪，誰所定也？

translations.literal: Song pleased submitted—presented Jingwang—king said 'Should it not be thus—who fixed it?
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi approved.

sentences.zh: 」松曰：「鍾會。

translations.literal: Song said 'Zhong Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Song credited Zhong Hui.

sentences.zh: 向亦欲啟之，會公見問，不敢饕其能。

translations.literal: Earlier also wished report—meeting lord asked—dared not steal his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Song had modestly withheld credit.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「如此，可大用，可令來。

translations.literal: King said 'Thus—can greatly employ—order come.
