translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi summoned Zhong Hui.

sentences.zh: 」會問松王所能，松曰：「博學明識，無所不貫。

translations.literal: Hui asked Song king's abilities—Song said 'Broad learning clear knowledge—nothing not penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Song praised Sima Shi.

sentences.zh: 」會乃絕賓客，精思十日，平旦入見，至鼓二乃出。

translations.literal: Hui then cut off guests—precision thought ten days—dawn entered audience—to second drum then exited.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui studied ten days then impressed Sima Shi.

sentences.zh: 出後，王獨拊手嘆息曰：「此真王佐材也！

translations.literal: After exiting king alone clapped hands sighed saying 'This truly king's assistant talent!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi named him statecraft material.

sentences.zh: 」松字叔茂，陳留人，九江太守邊讓外孫。

translations.literal: Song courtesy name Shumao—Chenliu person—grandson without of Jiujiang prefect Bian Rang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Song was Bian Rang's descendant.

sentences.zh: 松弱冠有才，從司馬宣王征遼東，宣王命作檄，及破賊，作露布。

translations.literal: Song weak crown had talent—followed Sima Yi campaign Liaodong—Yi ordered compose proclamation—when bandits broken compose victory bulletin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Song wrote Xi campaign prose.

sentences.zh: 松從還，宣王辟為掾，時年二十四，遷中書郎，遂至太守。

translations.literal: Song followed return—Yi summoned aide—then age twenty-four—promoted palace secretary—reached prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Song rose to prefect.

sentences.zh: 松子濬，字顯弘，晉廷尉。

translations.literal: Song's son Jun—courtesy name Xianhong—Jin minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Song's son Jun became minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以為鍾會名公之子，聲譽夙著，弱冠登朝，已歷顯位，景王為相，何容不悉，而方於定虞松表然後乃蒙接引乎？

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi judges Zhong Hui famous lord's son—reputation long prominent—weak crown ascended court—already passed prominent ranks—when Jingwang was minister—how tolerate not know—only after fixing Yu Song memorial then received summons?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi doubts the anecdote—Hui was already famous.

sentences.zh: 設使先不相識，但見五字而便知可大用，雖聖人其猶病諸，而況景王哉？〉

translations.literal: Suppose first not acquainted—only seeing five characters then knew greatly employable—even sage still troubled—moreover Jingwang?
translations.idiomatic: Pei finds five-character miracle implausible."

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公即尊位，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Duke Gaoguixiang assumed throne—granted noble rank within passes.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoguixiang's accession brought noble rank.

sentences.zh: 初，吳大將全琮，孫權之婚親重臣也，琮子懌、孫靜、從子端、翩、緝等，皆將兵來救誕。

translations.literal: Earlier Wu great general Quan Zong—Sun Quan's marriage-relative heavy minister—Zong's sons Yi Jing nephew sons Duan Pian Ji each led troops came rescue Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Quan clan rescued Zhuge Dan.

sentences.zh: 懌兄子輝、儀留建業，與其家內爭訟，攜其母，將部曲數十家渡江，自歸文王。

translations.literal: Yi's brother's sons Hui Yi stayed Jianye—with household internal lawsuit—carried mother led dozens of households retainers crossed river—self-submitted Wenwang.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Hui and Yi defected to Sima Zhao.

sentences.zh: 會建策，密為輝、儀作書，使輝、儀所親信齎入城告懌等，說吳中怒懌等不能拔壽春，欲盡誅諸將家，故逃來歸命。

translations.literal: Hui devised stratagem—secretly for Hui Yi composed letter—made Hui Yi trusted intimate carry into city tell Yi and company—stating Wu central angry Yi company could not lift Shouchun—wished execute all generals' families—therefore fled come submit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui forged letters about Wu executing families.

sentences.zh: 懌等恐懼，遂將所領開東城門出降，皆蒙封寵，城中由是乖離。

translations.literal: Yi company fearful—thereupon led command opened east gate surrendered—all received enfeoff favor—inside city thereby split apart.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi surrendered from fear.

sentences.zh: 壽春之破，會謀居多，親待日隆，時人謂之子房。

translations.literal: Shouchun's breaking—Hui stratagem mostly—intimate treatment daily grew—people of age called him Zifang.
translations.idiomatic: His Shouchun stratagem earned comparisons to Zhang Liang.

sentences.zh: 軍還，遷為太僕，固辭不就。

translations.literal: Army returned—promoted grand coach—firmly declined not assume.
translations.idiomatic: He refused grand coach.

sentences.zh: 以中郎在大將軍府管記室事，為腹心之任。

translations.literal: As gentleman of the palace in grand general office managed secretary chamber affairs—trusted intimate duty.
translations.idiomatic: He ran Sima Zhao's secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以討諸葛誕功，進爵陳侯，屢讓不受。

translations.literal: By merit against Zhuge Dan—advanced noble Chen marquis—repeatedly declined not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the Chen marquisate.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「會典綜軍事，參同計策，料敵制勝，有謀謨之勳，而推寵固讓，辭指款實，前後累重，志不可奪。

translations.literal: Edict stated: 'Hui manages comprehensive military affairs—joins same planning—measures enemy controls victory—has stratagem merit—yet pushes favor firmly declines—words sincere—before after accumulated weight—intent cannot be seized.
translations.idiomatic: The edict praised Zhong Hui for overseeing military affairs, joining in planning, reading the enemy and winning battles, and earning true merit in counsel—yet he steadfastly declined honors with sincere words time and again, and could not be moved from his resolve.

sentences.zh: 夫成功不處，古人所重，其聽會所執，以成其美。

translations.literal: Now success not occupying—ancients valued—listen Hui's insistence—to complete his beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Court respected his refusal.

sentences.zh: 」遷司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Promoted metropolitan commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He became metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 雖在外司，時政損益，當世與奪，無不綜典。

translations.literal: Though outside court—current policy gains losses—age's grants seizures—none not comprehensively managed.
translations.idiomatic: He dominated policy despite nominal role.

sentences.zh: 嵇康等見誅，皆會謀也。

translations.literal: Ji Kang and others executed—all Hui's plotting.
translations.idiomatic: He engineered Ji Kang's death.

sentences.zh: 文王以蜀大將姜維屢擾邊陲，料蜀國小民疲，資力單竭，欲大舉圖蜀。

translations.literal: Wenwang because Shu great general Jiang Wei repeatedly disturbed frontier—judged Shu state small people weary—resources strength singly exhausted—wished great undertaking map Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao planned Shu because of Jiang Wei.

sentences.zh: 惟會亦以為蜀可取，豫共籌度地形，考論事勢。

translations.literal: Only Hui also judged Shu could take—together beforehand planned terrain—examined discussed situation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui agreed and mapped the campaign.

sentences.zh: 景元三年冬，以會為鎮西將軍、假節都督關中諸軍事。

translations.literal: Jingyuan third year winter Hui was appointed general who guards the west with jie staff commanding Guanzhong military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In winter Jingyuan 3 Zhong Hui became general who guards the west with authority over the Guanzhong armies.

sentences.zh: 文王敕青、徐、兗、豫、荊、揚諸州，並使作船，又令唐咨作浮海大船，外為將伐吳者。

translations.literal: Wenwang ordered Qing, Xu, Yan, Yu, Jing, Yang provinces each to build ships—also ordered Tang Zi build ocean-going vessels—outwardly as preparing to attack Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao mobilized shipbuilding across the eastern provinces and had Tang Zi build sea transports as cover for a Wu campaign.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，乃下詔使鄧艾、諸葛緒各統諸軍三萬餘人，艾趣甘松、沓中連綴維，緒趣武街、橋頭絕維歸路。

translations.literal: Fourth year autumn edict ordered Deng Ai and Zhuge Xu each lead over thirty thousand—Ai toward Gansong and Tazhong to pin Jiang Wei—Xu toward Wujie and Bridgehead to cut Wei's retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn Jingyuan 4: Deng Ai struck Gansong-Tazhong while Zhuge Xu sealed Bridgehead.

sentences.zh: 會統十餘萬眾，分從斜谷、駱谷入。

translations.literal: Hui commanded over one hundred thousand divided from Xie Valley and Luo Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui took more than 100,000 men through Xie and Luo passes.

sentences.zh: 先命牙門將許儀在前治道，會在後行，而橋穿，馬足陷，於是斬儀。

translations.literal: First ordered gate general Xu Yi repair the road ahead—Hui followed—the bridge broke and a horse sank—thereupon Yi was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Xu Yi when the pioneer bridge collapsed.

sentences.zh: 儀者，許褚之子，有功王室，猶不原貸。

translations.literal: Yi was Xu Chu's son—meritorious to the dynasty—yet received no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Even Xu Chu's son earned no mercy.

sentences.zh: 諸軍聞之，莫不震竦。

translations.literal: The armies hearing this none failed to tremble.
translations.idiomatic: The hosts trembled at such severity.

sentences.zh: 蜀令諸圍皆不得戰，退還漢、樂二城守。

translations.literal: Shu ordered every cordon not to fight—withdraw to defend Han and Le cities.
translations.idiomatic: Shu pulled back to Han and Le fortresses.

sentences.zh: 魏興太守劉欽趣子午谷，諸軍數道平行，至漢中。

translations.literal: Weixing prefect Liu Qin pushed toward Ziwu Valley—the armies advanced in parallel columns to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Columns converged on Hanzhong via Ziwu.

sentences.zh: 蜀監軍王含守樂城，護軍蔣斌守漢城，兵各五千。

translations.literal: Shu army supervisor Wang Han held Lecheng—protector Jiang Bin held Hancheng—five thousand men each.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han and Jiang Bin held 5,000 each at Le and Han.

sentences.zh: 會使護軍荀愷、前將軍李輔各統萬人，愷圍漢城，輔圍樂城。

translations.literal: Hui ordered protectors Xun Kai and former general Li Fu each ten thousand—Kai besieged Hancheng—Fu besieged Lecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Kai and Li Fu invested the twin fortresses.

sentences.zh: 會徑過，西出陽安口，遣人祭諸葛亮之墓。

translations.literal: Hui passed through—exited west Yangankou—sent men to sacrifice at Zhuge Liang's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui offered sacrifice at Zhuge Liang's grave.

sentences.zh: 使護軍胡烈等行前，攻破關城，得庫藏積穀。

translations.literal: Ordered protector Hu Lie forward—broke Guancheng—seized stored grain.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Lie took Guancheng and its granaries.

sentences.zh: 姜維自沓中還，至陰平，合集士眾，欲赴關城。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei returned from Tazhong to Yinping—gathered troops—meant to relieve Guancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei raced from Tazhong toward Guancheng.

sentences.zh: 未到，聞其已破，退趣白水，與蜀將張翼、廖化等合守劍閣拒會。

translations.literal: Before arriving heard it had fallen—withdrew toward Bailong—joined Zhang Yi Liao Hua to hold Jiange against Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Too late he fell back to Jiange with Zhang Yi and Liao Hua.

sentences.zh: 會移檄蜀將吏士民曰：

translations.literal: Hui issued proclamation to Shu officers soldiers and people stating:
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui's open letter to Shu began:

sentences.zh: 往者漢祚衰微，率土分崩，生民之命，幾於泯滅。

translations.literal: Formerly Han mandate decayed—realm split apart—common people's lives nearly extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: When Han fell the land shattered and lives hung by a thread.

sentences.zh: 太祖武皇帝神武聖哲，撥亂反正，拯其將墜，造我區夏。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu divine martial and sage quelled chaos restored order—saved the tottering—founded our realm.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao restored order from chaos.

sentences.zh: 高祖文皇帝應天順民，受命踐阼。

translations.literal: Gaozu Wen Emperor answered Heaven and followed the people—received mandate and ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen took the Wei throne.

sentences.zh: 烈祖明皇帝奕世重光，恢拓洪業。

translations.literal: Liezu Ming Emperor successive reigns renewed light—expanded the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming extended Wei power.

sentences.zh: 然江山之外，異政殊俗，率土齊民未蒙王化，此三祖所以顧懷遺恨也。

translations.literal: Yet beyond rivers and mountains foreign governments and customs—the realm's people did not receive royal transformation—this is why the three ancestors cherished lingering regret.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Yangzi and Bashu lay peoples Wei had not yet transformed.

sentences.zh: 今主上聖德欽明，紹隆前緒，宰輔忠肅明允，劬勞王室，布政垂惠而萬邦協和，施德百蠻而肅慎致貢。

translations.literal: Now our lord's sagely virtue is admirable—he continues the former thread—the chief ministers are loyal solemn and wise—they labor for the royal house—spread policy and extend favor so myriad states harmonize—extend virtue to hundred barbarians until Sushen sends tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sima Zhao governance reaches everywhere—even distant Sushen pays tribute.

sentences.zh: 悼彼巴蜀，獨為匪民，愍此百姓，勞役未已。

translations.literal: We grieve that Ba-Shu alone remain beyond our people—we pity these folk worn by endless levies.
translations.idiomatic: Shu still levied its people without end.

sentences.zh: 是以命授六師，龔行天罰，征西、雍州、鎮西諸軍，五道並進。

translations.literal: Therefore we ordered six armies respectfully to execute Heaven's punishment—the west expedition Yongzhou and west-guard hosts advance together on five roads.
translations.idiomatic: Wei struck Shu on five axes.

sentences.zh: 古之行軍，以仁為本，以義治之；

translations.literal: Ancient armies took benevolence as root and righteousness as rule;
translations.idiomatic: Classical warfare rests on humanity and duty.

sentences.zh: 王者之師，有征無戰；

translations.literal: a king's army campaigns without fighting;
translations.idiomatic: A kingly host goes forth on campaign, and the foe yields without a fight.

sentences.zh: 故虞舜舞干戚而服有苗，周武有散財、發廩、表閭之義。

translations.literal: thus Shun danced shield and axe and You Miao submitted—King Wu of Zhou scattered wealth opened granaries and honored gates.
translations.idiomatic: Shun and Wu Wang won without slaughter.

sentences.zh: 今鎮西奉辭銜命，攝統戎重，庶弘文告之訓，以濟元元之命，非欲窮武極戰，以快一朝之政，故略陳安危之要，其敬聽話言。

translations.literal: Now the west-guard receives charge—commands military weight—hopes to extend civil instruction's teaching and rescue common lives—not to exhaust arms for one morning's pleasure—briefly stated essentials of peril and safety—listen carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui promised humane conquest.

sentences.zh: 益州先主以命世英才，興兵朔野，困躓冀、徐之郊，制命紹、布之手，太祖拯而濟之，與隆大好。

translations.literal: Yizhou's Founder with generation-spanning genius raised troops on northern frontier—stumbled at Ji and Xu borders—life fell into Yuan Shao and Lü Bu's hands—Taizu rescued and aided him—made great friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei failed against Yuan Shao and Lü Bu until Cao Cao aided him.

sentences.zh: 中更背違，棄同即異，諸葛孔明仍規秦川，姜伯約屢出隴右，勞動我邊境，侵擾我氐、羌，方國家多故，未遑修九伐之征也。

translations.literal: Middle period betrayed alliance—abandoned sameness sought difference—Zhuge Liang still plotted Qin river lands—Jiang Boyue repeatedly exited Longyou—laboring our borderlands—disturbing our Di and Qiang—while state had many troubles—had no leisure for nine punitive expeditions.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shu betrayed Wei—Zhuge Liang and Jiang Wei raided Longyou—Wei had too many crises to strike back.

sentences.zh: 今邊境乂清，方內無事，畜力待時，并兵一向，而巴蜀一州之眾，分張守備，難以御天下之師。

translations.literal: Now borders quiet—inside without affairs—stored strength awaits opportunity—combine armies one direction—yet Ba-Shu one province's hosts divide defense—hard to resist realm's armies.
translations.idiomatic: Peace on northern borders lets Wei concentrate—Shu's scattered garrisons cannot hold.

sentences.zh: 段谷、侯和沮傷之氣，難以敵堂堂之陳。

translations.literal: Duangu and Hehou defeats have slack morale—hard to oppose mighty formation.
translations.idiomatic: Morale still weak from Duangu and Hehou.

sentences.zh: 比年以來，曾無寧歲，征夫勤瘁，難以當子來之民。

translations.literal: Recent years without peaceful year—campaign laborers weary—hard to match willing populace.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's levies exhaust the people.

sentences.zh: 此皆諸賢所親見也。

translations.literal: These all worthy gentlemen personally witnessed.
translations.idiomatic: You have seen this yourselves.

sentences.zh: 蜀相壯見禽於秦，公孫述授首於漢，九州之險，是非一姓。

translations.literal: Shu minister Zhuang was captured by Qin—Gongsun Shu lost head to Han—nine provinces' peril belongs not one surname.
translations.idiomatic: History shows Bashu falls—Shu Long was taken; Gongsun Shu died.

sentences.zh: 此皆諸賢所備聞也。

translations.literal: These all worthy gentlemen fully heard.
translations.idiomatic: You know the precedents.

sentences.zh: 明者見危於無形，智者規禍於未萌，是以微子去商，長為周賓，陳平背項，立功於漢。

translations.literal: Bright ones see peril without form—wise ones plot calamity before sprouting—thus Weizi left Shang—long served Zhou guest—Chen Ping betrayed Xiang—meritorious to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Wise men flee doomed regimes like Weizi and Chen Ping.

sentences.zh: 豈晏安酖毒，懷祿而不變哉？

translations.literal: How swallow ease and poisoned cup—embrace stipend without changing?
translations.idiomatic: Will you cling to salary till doom?

sentences.zh: 今國朝隆天覆之恩，宰輔弘寬恕之德，先惠後誅，好生惡殺。

translations.literal: Now court extends Heaven-covering grace—chief ministers expand forgiving virtue—favor first punish later—love life hate killing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei offers mercy before the sword.

sentences.zh: 往者吳將孫壹舉眾內附，位為上司，寵秩殊異。

translations.literal: Formerly Wu general Sun Yi led masses inward submission—ranked upper commander—favor salary exceptionally different.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yi defected to wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 文欽、唐咨為國大害，叛主仇賊，還為戎首。

translations.literal: Wen Qin Tang Zi were state's great harm—betrayed lord enemy bandits—yet became campaign leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Even rebels Wen Qin and Tang Zi became leaders.

sentences.zh: 咨困逼禽獲，欽二子還降，皆將軍、封侯；

translations.literal: Zi trapped captured—Qin's two sons returned surrender—all generals enfeoffed marquises;
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zi captured—Wen Qin's sons surrendered—as generals and marquises.

sentences.zh: 咨與聞國事。

translations.literal: Zi participates hear state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zi joined court councils.

sentences.zh: 壹等窮踧歸命，猶加盛寵，況巴蜀賢知見機而作者哉！

translations.literal: Yi and others cornered submitted—still received lavish favor—moreover Ba-Shu worthy wise who seize opportunity act!
translations.idiomatic: Cornered defectors flourished—how much more worthies who yield now!

sentences.zh: 誠能深鑑成敗，邈然高蹈，投跡微子之踪，錯身陳平之軌，則福同古人，慶流來裔，百姓士民，安堵舊業，農不易畝，巿不回肆，去累卵之危，就永安之福，豈不美與！

translations.literal: If truly deeply mirror success failure—loftily tread high—cast footprints Weizi's traces—shift body Chen Ping's track—then fortune matches ancients—blessing flows posterity—commoners and soldiers peaceably keep old tasks—farmers change not furrows—markets shift not stalls—leave piled-egg peril—approach eternal peace blessing—is this not beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Defect now for fortune like Weizi or Chen Ping.

sentences.zh: 若偷安旦夕，迷而不反，大兵一發，玉石皆碎，雖欲悔之，亦無及已。

translations.literal: If steal ease morning evening—lost not returning—great army once launched—jade and stone both shattered—though wish regret—also cannot catch up.
translations.idiomatic: Delay until Wei armies crush all.

sentences.zh: 其詳擇利害，自求多福，各具宣布，咸使聞知。

translations.literal: Their detailed choose profit harm—self seek much blessing—each spread declare—all hear know.
translations.idiomatic: Choose wisely—spread this word everywhere.

sentences.zh: 鄧艾追姜維到陰平，簡選精銳，欲從漢德陽入江由、左儋道詣綿竹，趣成都，與諸葛緒共行。

translations.literal: Deng Ai pursued Jiang Wei to Yinping—picked crack troops—wished from Han Deyang enter Jiangyou and Zuodan road to Mianzhu toward Chengdu—together with Zhuge Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai aimed through Deyang toward Jiangyou and Chengdu with Zhuge Xu.

sentences.zh: 緒以本受節度邀姜維，西行非本詔，遂進軍前向白水，與會合。

translations.literal: Xu originally received orders to intercept Jiang Wei—westward march was not original edict—thereupon advanced forward toward Bailong—joined Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Xu advanced to Bailong to link with Hui—ignoring the flanking order.

sentences.zh: 會遣將軍田章等從劍閣西，徑出江由。

translations.literal: Hui sent generals Tian Zhang and others from west of Jiange—straight to Jiangyou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui sent Tian Zhang west of Jiange toward Jiangyou.

sentences.zh: 未至百里，章先破蜀伏兵三校，艾使章先登。

translations.literal: Not yet hundred li—Zhang first broke Shu ambush three regiments—Ai made Zhang vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zhang cleared Shu ambush a hundred li out.

sentences.zh: 遂長驅而前。

translations.literal: Thereupon long drive forward.
translations.idiomatic: They drove deep.

sentences.zh: 會與緒軍向劍閣，會欲專軍勢，密白緒畏懦不進，檻車徵還。

translations.literal: Hui and Xu's army toward Jiange—Hui wished monopolize military power—secretly reported Xu timid did not advance—cage cart summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui framed Zhuge Xu as coward and recalled him.

sentences.zh: 軍悉屬會，

translations.literal: Army wholly belonged Hui,
translations.idiomatic: All troops fell to Zhong Hui.

sentences.zh: 〈按《百官名》：緒入晉為太常崇禮衛尉。

translations.literal: Checking Officials Directory states Xu entered Jin as minister of rituals reverence guard commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Directory notes Zhuge Xu's Jin offices.

sentences.zh: 子衝，廷尉。

translations.literal: Son Chong—minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Son Chong became minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 荀綽《兗州記》曰：衝子詮，字德林，玫字仁林，並知名顯達。

translations.literal: Xun Chuo's Yanzhou Record states Chong's son Quan courtesy Deilin Mei courtesy Renlin—both famous distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's sons Quan and Mei were notable.

sentences.zh: 詮，兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Quan—Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quan governed Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 玫，侍中御史中丞。〉

translations.literal: Mei—palace attendant censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Mei reached attendant and censor chief."

sentences.zh: 進攻劍閣，不克，引退，蜀軍保險拒守。

translations.literal: Attacked Jiange—could not prevail—withdrew—Shu army held narrows defended.
translations.idiomatic: Jiange held against Zhong Hui.

sentences.zh: 艾遂至綿竹，大戰，斬諸葛瞻。

translations.literal: Ai reached Mianzhu—great battle—beheaded Zhuge Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai crushed Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 維等聞瞻巳破，率其眾東入於巴。

translations.literal: Wei and others hearing Zhan already defeated—led host east into Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei fled east into Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 會乃進軍至涪，遣胡烈、田續、龐會等追維。

translations.literal: Hui therefore advanced army to Fu—sent Hu Lie Tian Xu Pang Hui pursue Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui pushed to Fu and chased Jiang Wei.

sentences.zh: 艾進軍向成都，劉禪詣艾降，遣使敕維等令降於會。

translations.literal: Ai advanced army toward Chengdu—Liu Shan went surrender Ai—sent messenger order Wei and others surrender Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan surrendered to Deng Ai while ordering Jiang Wei to yield to Zhong Hui.

sentences.zh: 維至廣漢郪縣，令兵悉放器仗，送節傳於胡烈，便從東道詣會降。

translations.literal: Wei reached Quxian of Guanghan—ordered troops lay down weapons—sent insignia to Hu Lie—then east road went surrender Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei disarmed at Quxian and surrendered to Zhong Hui.

sentences.zh: 會上言曰：

translations.literal: Hui memorialized stating:
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui reported:

sentences.zh: 賊姜維、張翼、廖化、董厥等逃死遁走，欲趣成都。

translations.literal: Bandits Jiang Wei Zhang Yi Liao Hua Dong Jue etc fled death escaped—wished hurry Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei and officers raced toward Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 臣輒遣司馬夏侯咸、護軍胡烈等，經從劍閣，出新都、大渡截其前，參軍爰青彡、將軍句安等躡其後，參軍皇甫闓、將軍王買等從涪南出衝其腹，臣據涪縣為東西勢援。

translations.literal: Your servant dispatched Major Xiahou Xian, Protector Hu Lie, and others along Jiange, emerging at Xindu and Dadu to block their front; Adjutant Yuan Pang and General Gou An pressed their rear; Adjutant Huangfu Kai and General Wang Mai struck from south of Fu toward their flank; your servant held Fu county to lend east-west support.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui claimed he had sent Xiahou Xian and Hu Lie through Jiange and out toward Xindu and Dadu to bar the way ahead, while Yuan Pang and Gou An closed from behind, Huangfu Kai and Wang Mai hit from south of Fu, and he himself anchored Fu to tie the wings together.

sentences.zh: 維等所統步騎四五萬人，擐甲厲兵，塞川填谷，數百里中首尾相繼，憑恃其眾，方軌而西。

translations.literal: Wei and others commanded infantry cavalry forty fifty thousand—don armor sharpen weapons—fill valleys block rivers—several hundred li head tail linked—relying on multitude—parallel tracks westward.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei's army marched west in force.

sentences.zh: 臣敕咸、闓等令分兵據勢，廣張羅罔，南杜走吳之道，西塞成都之路，北絕越逸之徑，四面雲集，首尾並進，蹊路斷絕，走伏無地。

translations.literal: Your servant ordered Xian Kai etc divide troops seize terrain—spread wide nets—south block road flee Wu—west seal Chengdu road—north cut escape routes—four sides cloud gather—head tail advance together—paths cut off—nowhere flee hide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui described trapping Jiang Wei on every road.

sentences.zh: 臣又手書申喻，開示生路，群寇困逼，知命窮數盡，解甲投戈，面縛委質，印綬萬數，資器山積。

translations.literal: Your servant also hand wrote explain—open survival road—mass bandits cornered pressed—know fate exhausted numbers ended—remove armor cast weapons—bind faces submit credentials—seals cords myriad count—goods piled mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Shu stacked surrendered seals before him.

sentences.zh: 昔舜舞干戚，有苗自服；

translations.literal: Formerly Shun danced shield axe—You Miao self-submitted;
translations.idiomatic: Like Shun winning without fighting.

sentences.zh: 牧野之師，商旅倒戈：有征無戰，帝王之盛業。

translations.literal: Muye army merchants inverted weapons—campaign without battle—emperor-king's flourishing enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Like Zhou's bloodless victory.

sentences.zh: 全國為上，破國次之；

translations.literal: Spare whole state highest—break state second;
translations.idiomatic: Sunzi: preserve the whole state first.

sentences.zh: 全軍為上，破軍次之：用兵之令典。

translations.literal: Spare whole army highest—break army second—this is military canon.
translations.idiomatic: Preserve armies when possible.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖德，侔踪前代，翼輔忠明，齊軌公旦，仁育羣生，義征不譓，殊俗向化，無思不服，師不逾時，兵不血刃，萬里同風，九州共貫。

translations.literal: Your Majesty sagely virtue traces former generations—wing assistants loyal bright parallel Duke Zhou Duke Dan—benevolence nurtures living beings—righteous campaigns punish rebels—foreign customs turn toward transformation—none think not submit—armies cross not whole seasons—blades touch not blood—ten thousand li same wind—nine provinces threaded.
translations.idiomatic: Edict praised Sima Zhao like Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 臣輒奉宣詔命，導揚恩化，復其社稷，安其閭伍，捨其賦調，弛其徵役，訓之德禮以移其風，示之軌儀以易其俗，百姓欣欣，人懷逸豫，後來其蘇，義無以過。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully proclaimed edict—guided spread gracious transformation—restored altars—pacified neighborhoods—remitted taxes levies—relaxed corvee labor—trained virtue ritual to shift customs—displayed standards rites to change habits—common folk rejoicing—each harbored ease later they revive—righteousness none surpass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui claimed benevolent occupation of Shu.

sentences.zh: 會於是禁檢士眾不得鈔略，虛己誘納，以接蜀之群司，與維情好歡甚。

translations.literal: Hui thereupon forbade inspecting soldiers people must not plunder—emptied self lure accept—to receive Shu crowd of officials—with Wei intimate friendship extremely joyful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui banned looting and courted Shu officials—charmed Jiang Wei.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：夏侯霸奔蜀，蜀朝問「司馬公如何德」？

translations.literal: Sayings of Age states when Xiahou Ba fled Shu Shu court asked how Lord Sima's virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Shu asked Xiahou Ba about Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 霸曰：「自當作家門。

translations.literal: Ba said 'Certainly will establish household.
translations.idiomatic: Ba said Sima Yi would consolidate power.

sentences.zh: 」「京師俊士」？

translations.literal: 'Capital elite'?
translations.idiomatic: Asked about Luoyang talent.

sentences.zh: 曰：「有鍾士季，其人管朝政，吳、蜀之憂也。

translations.literal: Said 'There is Zhong Shiji—that person will manage court politics—Wu and Shu's worry.
translations.idiomatic: Ba named Zhong Hui as future threat.

sentences.zh: 」《漢晉春秋》曰：初，夏侯霸降蜀，姜維問之曰：「司馬懿既得彼政，當復有征伐之志不？

translations.literal: Han-Jin Spring and Autumn states initially when Xiahou Ba surrendered Shu Jiang Wei asked 'Sima Yi having seized government—will again have campaign ambition?'
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei asked Ba whether Sima Yi would attack.

sentences.zh: 」霸曰：「彼方營立家門，未遑外事。

translations.literal: Ba said 'That side establishing household gate—not leisure foreign affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ba said Sima Yi focused inward.

sentences.zh: 有鍾士季者，其人雖少，終為吳、蜀之憂，然非非常之人亦不能用也。

translations.literal: There is Zhong Shiji—that person though young finally Wu Shu's worry—yet not extraordinary person also cannot employ.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ba warned Zhong Hui would threaten Wu-Shu.

sentences.zh: 」後十五年而會果滅蜀。

translations.literal: Later fifteen years Hui indeed extinguished Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years later Zhong Hui destroyed Shu.

sentences.zh: 按習鑿齒此言，非出他書，故採用《世語》而附益也。〉

translations.literal: Checking Xi Chao's words—not from other book—therefore adopt Sayings of Age and attach supplement.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi merged Xi Chao with Shishuo.

sentences.zh: 十二月詔曰：「會所向摧弊，前無強敵，緘制眾城，罔羅迸逸。

translations.literal: Twelfth month edict stated 'Hui wherever directed smashed decline—before no strong enemy—silenced mass cities—netted fleeing fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Winter edict praised Zhong Hui's victories.

sentences.zh: 蜀之豪帥，面縛歸命，謀無遺策，舉無廢功。

translations.literal: Shu's heroic leaders bound faces submitted fate—planning left no strategy—raising arms wasted no merit.
translations.idiomatic: Shu commanders surrendered.

sentences.zh: 凡所降誅，動以萬計，全勝獨克，有征無戰。

translations.literal: All surrendered executed moved by myriad measure—complete victory sole conquest—campaign without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Bloodless surrender of masses.

sentences.zh: 拓平西夏，方隅清晏。

translations.literal: Expanded pacified western Xia—regions corners clear calm.
translations.idiomatic: West pacified.

sentences.zh: 其以會為司徒，進封縣侯，增邑萬戶。

translations.literal: Let Hui be minister of education—advance enfeoff county marquis—increase fief ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui became minister of education with vast fief.

sentences.zh: 封子二人亭侯，邑各千戶。」

translations.literal: Enfeoff two sons village marquis—each thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: His sons received village marquises."

sentences.zh: 會內有異志，因鄧艾承制專事，密白艾有反狀，

translations.literal: Hui inner harbored different ambition—because Deng Ai carried orders monopolized affairs—secretly reported Ai had rebellion signs,
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui coveted power and framed Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：會善效人書，於劍閣要艾章表白事，皆易其言，令辭指悖傲，多自矜伐。

translations.literal: Sayings of Age states Hui skilled imitating handwriting—at Jiange intercepted Ai's memorial reports—changed all wording—made rhetoric arrogant boastful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui forged Deng Ai's memorials.

sentences.zh: 又毀文王報書，手作以疑之也。〉

translations.literal: Also destroyed Wenwang reply letter—hand wrote to doubt him.
translations.idiomatic: He forged Sima Zhao's replies too."

sentences.zh: 於是詔書檻車徵艾。

translations.literal: Thereupon edict cage cart summoned Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Court ordered Deng Ai arrested.

sentences.zh: 司馬文王懼艾或不從命，敕會並進軍成都，監軍衛瓘在會前行，以文王手筆令宣喻艾軍，艾軍皆釋仗，遂收艾入檻車。

translations.literal: Sima Wenwang feared Ai might not obey command—ordered Hui together advance Chengdu—army supervisor Wei Guan ahead of Hui—with Wenwang handwritten order proclaim Ai's army—Ai army all laid weapons—thereupon seized Ai into cage cart.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao sent Wei Guan to disarm Deng Ai safely.

sentences.zh: 會所憚惟艾，艾既禽而會尋至，獨統大眾，威震西土。

translations.literal: What Hui feared only Ai—Ai already captured and Hui soon arrived—alone commanded great host—awe shook western lands.
translations.idiomatic: With Deng Ai gone Zhong Hui commanded alone.

sentences.zh: 自謂功名蓋世，不可復為人下，加猛將銳卒皆在己手，遂謀反。

translations.literal: Self-judged merit fame covered generation—could not again be under others—added fierce generals crack troops all in own hand—thereupon plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui deemed himself peerless and plotted revolt.

sentences.zh: 欲使姜維等皆將蜀兵出斜谷，會自將大眾隨其後。

translations.literal: He wished to have Jiang Wei and the others all lead Shu troops out through Xie Valley, while he himself would command the main host and follow behind them.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to send Jiang Wei and company leading Shu forces through Xie Valley while he followed with the main army.

sentences.zh: 既至長安，令騎士從陸道，步兵從水道順流浮渭入河，以為五日可到孟津，與騎會洛陽，一旦天下可定也。

translations.literal: Once they reached Chang'an, he would order the cavalry by the land route and the infantry by water, floating down the Wei into the Yellow River; he reckoned that in five days they could reach Mengjin, join the cavalry at Luoyang, and in one stroke settle the realm.
translations.idiomatic: From Chang'an, cavalry would go overland and infantry downstream on the Wei into the river; he figured five days to Mengjin, a rendezvous with the horse at Luoyang, and the realm settled at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 會得文王書云：「恐鄧艾或不就徵，今遣中護軍賈充將步騎萬人徑入斜谷，屯樂城，吾自將十萬屯長安，相見在近。

translations.literal: Hui received a letter from King Wen stating: "I fear Deng Ai may not comply with the summons. I now dispatch the Central Protector of the Army Jia Chong to lead ten thousand foot and horse straight into Xie Valley and encamp at Lecheng; I myself will lead one hundred thousand and encamp at Chang'an. We shall meet soon.
translations.idiomatic: Word came from Sima Zhao: if Deng Ai might refuse the summons, Jia Chong would take ten thousand into Xie Valley to Lecheng while Zhao himself camped at Chang'an with a hundred thousand—“we shall meet shortly.”

sentences.zh: 」會得書，驚呼所親語之曰：「但取鄧艾，相國知我能獨辦之；

translations.literal: " When Hui received the letter, he cried out in alarm to his intimates and said to them: "If it were only to take Deng Ai, the Chancellor knows I could manage it alone;
translations.idiomatic: Reading it, he told his confidants in alarm: “If it were only Deng Ai, the Chancellor knows I could handle that myself;

sentences.zh: 今來大重，必覺我異矣，便當速發。

translations.literal: now that such a great force is coming, he must already suspect my intentions; I must act at once.
translations.idiomatic: this massive deployment means he has seen through me—I must move immediately.”

sentences.zh: 事成，可得天下；

translations.literal: If the affair succeeds, I can gain the realm;
translations.idiomatic: If I succeed, I take the realm;

sentences.zh: 不成，退保蜀漢，不失作劉備也。

translations.literal: if it fails, I can fall back and hold Hanzhong and Shu—no worse than Liu Bei did."
translations.idiomatic: if not, I pull back and hold Hanzhong and Shu—no worse than Liu Bei.”

sentences.zh: 我自淮南以來，畫無遣策，四海所共知也。

translations.literal: From Huainan onward I have never once mislaid a stratagem; all within the Four Seas know it.
translations.idiomatic: Since Huainan I have never dropped a plan—the whole world knows it.

sentences.zh: 我欲持此安歸乎！

translations.literal: Am I to take this reputation and go quietly home!"
translations.idiomatic: Am I supposed to walk away with this and go home in peace!”

sentences.zh: 」會以五年正月十五日至，其明日，悉請護軍、郡守、牙門騎督以上及蜀之故官，為太后發喪於蜀朝堂。

translations.literal: Hui arrived on the fifteenth day of the first month of the fifth year of Xiandi's reign; the next day he summoned all Protectors of the Army, commandery governors, commandants of the gates and cavalry supervisors and above, together with former Shu officials, and held mourning for the Empress Dowager in the Shu court hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth of the first month in the fifth year he arrived; the next day he called every Protector of the Army, governor, gate commandant and cavalry inspector upward, plus former Shu officials, and staged mourning for the empress dowager in the Shu court hall.

sentences.zh: 矯太后遺詔，使會起兵廢文王，皆班示坐上人，使下議訖，書版署置，更使所親信代領諸軍。

translations.literal: He forged the Empress Dowager's final edict, ordering himself to raise troops and depose King Wen; he displayed it to all seated there, had them debate below and finish, sign the tablets and appointments, and then had his trusted men replace command of the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: He forged her testament ordering himself to revolt and depose Sima Zhao, showed it to the assembly, made them debate and sign wooden slips of appointment, then put his own men in command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 所請群官，悉閉著益州諸曹屋中，城門宮門皆閉，嚴兵圍守。

translations.literal: All the officials he had summoned he shut inside the various bureau chambers of Yizhou; city gates and palace gates were closed, and troops strictly ringed the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Every summoned official was locked in the Yizhou bureau buildings; city and palace gates were shut and soldiers sealed the compound.

sentences.zh: 會帳下督丘建本屬胡烈，烈薦之文王，會請以自隨，任愛之。

translations.literal: Qiu Jian, supervisor under Hui's command, had originally belonged to Hu Lie; Lie had recommended him to King Wen, and Hui had asked to keep him with him and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Jian, Zhong Hui's camp supervisor, had served under Hu Lie, whom Lie had recommended to Sima Zhao; Hui had asked to keep him and favored him.

sentences.zh: 建愍烈獨坐，啟會，使聽內一親兵出取飲食，諸牙門隨例各內一人。

translations.literal: Jian pitied Lie sitting alone, reported to Hui, and had him allow one personal soldier from each camp to go out for food and drink; following precedent, each gate commandant admitted one man inside.
translations.idiomatic: Jian pitied Lie isolated inside and persuaded Hui to let each camp send one orderly out for food; by custom each gate commandant was allowed one man in.

sentences.zh: 烈紿語親兵及疏與其子曰：「丘建密說消息，會已作大坑，白棓

translations.literal: Lie deceived his personal soldier and wrote secretly to his son, saying: "Qiu Jian secretly brought word: Hui has already dug a great pit and white clubs
translations.idiomatic: Lie lied to his orderly and slipped a note to his son: “Jian’s secret word—Hui has dug pits and prepared white clubs

sentences.zh: 〈棓與棒同。〉

translations.literal: (The commentary gloss states that the graph here is equivalent to the word meaning "club.")
translations.idiomatic: (Commentary gloss: same word as "club.")

sentences.zh: 數千，欲悉呼外兵入，人賜白㡊

translations.literal: There are thousands of them; he intends to call all the outer troops inside and give each a white kerchief
translations.idiomatic: They number in the thousands; he plans to bring every outer unit inside and give each man a white kerchief

sentences.zh: 〈苦洽反。〉

translations.literal: (Phonetic gloss: the commentary gives the fanqie spelling for reading this character.)
translations.idiomatic: (Phonetic gloss: fanqie spelling supplied in the commentary.)

sentences.zh: ，拜為散將，以次棓殺坑中。

translations.literal: , appoint them as miscellaneous officers, then beat them to death in the pits in order."
translations.idiomatic: , promote them to miscellaneous officers, then club them into the pits in order.”

sentences.zh: 」諸牙門親兵亦咸說此語，一夜傳相告，皆遍。

translations.literal: The gate commandants' personal soldiers all repeated this too; in one night the news spread everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: The gate guards’ orderlies repeated it too; within one night everyone knew.

sentences.zh: 或謂會：「可盡殺牙門騎督以上。

translations.literal: Someone said to Hui: "You could kill all the gate commandants and cavalry supervisors and above."
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Hui: “Kill every gate commandant and cavalry inspector and above.”

sentences.zh: 」會猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Hui hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Hui wavered and did not act.

sentences.zh: 十八日日中，烈軍兵與烈兒雷鼓出門，諸軍兵不期皆鼓譟出，曾無督促之者，而爭先赴城。

translations.literal: At noon on the eighteenth day, Lie's soldiers and Lie's son beat drums and rushed out the gates; the troops of the various camps, without prior arrangement, all thundered out—none had urged them—yet they raced to the city.
translations.idiomatic: At noon on the eighteenth, Lie’s troops and his son beat drums and burst from the gates; every camp roared out though no one had ordered it, all rushing for the city.

sentences.zh: 時方給與姜維鎧杖，白外有匈匈聲，似失火，有頃，白兵走向城。

translations.literal: At that moment they were just issuing armor and weapons to Jiang Wei; a report came that outside there was a hubbub like a fire; presently word came that soldiers were moving toward the city.
translations.idiomatic: They were still handing Jiang Wei armor and arms when word came of a din outside like a fire; soon reports said soldiers were heading for the walls.

sentences.zh: 會驚，謂維曰：「兵來似欲作惡，當云何？

translations.literal: Hui was alarmed and said to Jiang Wei: "The troops seem bent on mischief; what should we do?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui started and asked Jiang Wei: “The men sound ready to turn on us—what now?”

sentences.zh: 」維曰：「但當擊之耳。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei said: "We have only to strike them."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei said: “We strike them.”

sentences.zh: 」會遣兵悉殺所閉諸牙門郡守，內人共舉機以柱門，兵斫門，不能破。

translations.literal: Hui sent troops to kill all the shut-in gate commandants and governors; those inside together raised weaving frames to prop the doors; the soldiers hacked at the doors but could not break through.
translations.idiomatic: Hui sent men to slaughter the penned gate commandants and governors; those inside jammed looms against the doors so the attackers could not break in.

sentences.zh: 斯須，門外倚梯登城，或燒城屋，蟻附亂進，矢下如雨，牙門、郡守各緣屋出，與其卒兵相得。

translations.literal: In a moment, outside they leaned ladders against the wall and climbed, or set fire to buildings in the city; men swarmed up like ants in disorder; arrows fell like rain; each gate commandant and governor climbed out along the roofs and rejoined his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later ladders rose outside; buildings burned; men swarmed the walls like ants; arrows fell like rain; commandants and governors climbed from the roofs to their men.

sentences.zh: 姜維率會左右戰，手殺五六人，眾既格斬維，爭赴殺會。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei led Hui's attendants in fighting and personally killed five or six men; once the crowd had cut Jiang Wei down, they rushed to kill Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei fought beside Hui’s guards and killed five or six himself; when he fell the mob turned on Zhong Hui.

sentences.zh: 會時年四十，將士死者數百人。

translations.literal: Hui was forty sui at the time; several hundred officers and soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui was forty; hundreds of soldiers died.

sentences.zh: 〈《晉諸公贊》曰：胡烈兒名淵，字世元，遵之孫也。

translations.literal: The Jin Zhugong Zan states: Hu Lie's son was named Yuan, courtesy name Shiyuan, and was the grandson of Zun.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Zhugong Zan says Hu Lie’s son Yuan (courtesy Shiyuan) was grandson of Zun.

sentences.zh: 遵，安定人，以才兼文武，累居籓鎮，至車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Zun was a native of Anding; talented in both civil and military affairs, he successively held frontier posts, rising to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Zun of Anding combined civil and military talent, served repeatedly on the frontier, and rose to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 子奮，字玄威，亦歷方任。

translations.literal: His son Fen, courtesy name Xuanwei, also served in regional commands.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fen (courtesy Xuanwei) also held regional posts.

sentences.zh: 女為晉武帝貴人，有寵。

translations.literal: His daughter became an honored consort of Emperor Wu of Jin and was favored.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was a favored honored consort of Emperor Wu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 太康中，以奮為尚書僕射，加鎮軍大將軍、開府。

translations.literal: In the Taikang era, Fen was appointed Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and added General Who Guards the Army and opening of a separate establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taikang, Fen became Supervisor of the Masters of Writing with supernumerary General Who Guards the Army and an independent command.

sentences.zh: 弟廣，字宣祖，少府。

translations.literal: His younger brother Guang, courtesy name Xuanzu, was Minister of the Lesser Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Guang (courtesy Xuanzu) was Minister of the Lesser Treasury.

sentences.zh: 次烈，字玄武，秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Next Lie, courtesy name Xuanwu, was Inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Next, Lie (courtesy Xuanwu) was Inspector of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 次岐，宇玄嶷，并州刺史。

translations.literal: Next Qi, courtesy name Xuanyi, was Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Next, Qi (courtesy Xuanyi) was Inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣子喜，涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Guang's son Xi was Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guang’s son Xi was Inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 淵小字鷂鴟，時年十八，既殺會救父，名震遠近。

translations.literal: Yuan's childhood name was Yaochi; he was eighteen sui at the time; having killed Hui to rescue his father, his fame shook near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan’s boyhood name was Yaochi; at eighteen he killed Zhong Hui to free his father and his name rang far and wide.

sentences.zh: 後趙王倫篡位，三王興義，倫使淵與張泓將兵禦齊王，屢破齊軍。

translations.literal: Later, when Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne and the Three Princes raised the righteous cause, Lun sent Yuan with Zhang Hong to lead troops against the Prince of Qi, and they repeatedly defeated Qi's army.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Prince Zhao Lun seized the throne and the Three Princes rose against him, Lun sent Yuan with Zhang Hong against the Prince of Qi and they repeatedly broke Qi’s forces.

sentences.zh: 會成都戰克，淵乃歸降伏法。〉

translations.literal: When Chengdu fell in battle, Yuan then surrendered and submitted to the law."
translations.idiomatic: When Chengdu fell, Yuan surrendered and accepted judgment.”

sentences.zh: 初，文王欲遣會伐蜀，西曹屬邵悌求見曰：「今遣鍾會率十餘萬眾伐蜀，愚謂會單身無重任，不若使餘人行。

translations.literal: Earlier, when King Wen wished to dispatch Hui to attack Shu, the Western Bureau clerk Shao Ti requested an audience and said: "You now send Zhong Hui at the head of over a hundred thousand to attack Shu; I humbly think Hui, alone and without heavy responsibility on him, is less fit than having someone else go."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Sima Zhao meant to send Zhong Hui against Shu, Western Bureau clerk Shao Ti sought audience: “You give Hui more than a hundred thousand men—yet he bears no grave office alone; better send someone else.”

sentences.zh: 」文王笑曰：

translations.literal: King Wen smiled and said:
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao smiled:

sentences.zh: 我寧當復不知此耶？

translations.literal: "Do you suppose I truly do not know this?
translations.idiomatic: “Do you think I do not know that?

sentences.zh: 蜀為天下作患，使民不得安息，我今伐之如指掌耳，而眾人皆言蜀不可伐。

translations.literal: Shu plagues the realm and keeps the people from resting; I now destroy it as easily as turning my palm—yet everyone says Shu cannot be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Shu harms the empire and denies the people peace; I will crush it like turning my hand—yet everyone says Shu cannot be taken.

sentences.zh: 夫人心豫怯則智勇並竭，智勇並竭而強使之，適為敵禽耳。

translations.literal: When men's hearts are anxious and timid beforehand, wisdom and courage fail together; when wisdom and courage have failed and you force them anyway, you merely deliver them into the enemy's hands.
translations.idiomatic: When hearts start afraid, wit and daring fail together; force such troops and you only feed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 惟鍾會與人意同，今遣會伐蜀，必可滅蜀。

translations.literal: Only Zhong Hui shares my intent; if I send Hui to attack Shu, Shu can certainly be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhong Hui agrees with me—send him and Shu will fall.

sentences.zh: 滅蜀之後，就如卿所慮，當何所能一辦耶？

translations.literal: After Shu is destroyed, even if what you fear comes to pass—what could anyone accomplish all at once?
translations.idiomatic: After Shu falls, even if your fears come true—what could anyone do in one stroke?

sentences.zh: 凡敗軍之將不可以語勇，亡國之大夫不可與圖存，心膽以破故也。

translations.literal: In general one does not speak of courage to a defeated general, nor plan survival with ministers of a ruined state—their hearts and gall are broken.
translations.idiomatic: You do not talk bravery with a beaten general or survival with ministers of a fallen state—their nerve is gone.

sentences.zh: 若蜀以破，遺民震恐，不足與圖事；

translations.literal: If Shu is already broken, the surviving people will be terrified and unfit for plotting;
translations.idiomatic: Once Shu is crushed, the remnant population will be too terrified to plot;

sentences.zh: 中國將士各自思歸，不肯與同也。

translations.literal: the officers and soldiers of the Central Plain will each think of returning home and will not join him.
translations.idiomatic: Central Plain troops will each think of home and refuse to follow him.

sentences.zh: 若作惡，祗自滅族耳。

translations.literal: If he turns to evil, he will only destroy his own clan.
translations.idiomatic: If he rebels, he only wipes out his own kin.

sentences.zh: 卿不須憂此，慎莫使人聞也。

translations.literal: You need not worry over this; only be careful that no one hears."
translations.idiomatic: You need not fret—just keep this between us.”

sentences.zh: 會嘗論易無互體、才性同異。

translations.literal: Hui once discussed whether the Changes lacked overlapping trigrams and whether talent and nature were identical or different.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui once debated “no overlapping trigrams” in the Changes and whether talent and nature were the same or different.

sentences.zh: 及會死後，於會家得書二十篇，名曰《道論》，而實刑名家也，其文似會。

translations.literal: After Hui died, twenty scrolls of writings were found in his house, entitled Daolun, though in substance they were Legalist; the style resembled Hui's.
translations.idiomatic: After his death twenty chapters titled Daolun were found at his house—Legalist in substance, in Hui’s voice.

sentences.zh: 初，會弱冠與山陽王弼竝知名。

translations.literal: Earlier, at his capping Hui was already famous together with Wang Bi of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was already celebrated alongside Wang Bi of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 弼好論儒道，辭才逸辯，注《易》及《老子》，為尚書郎，年二十餘卒。

translations.literal: Bi loved to discourse on Confucianism and Daoism; his rhetoric was swift and fluent; he annotated the Changes and the Laozi, served as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and died in his twenties.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bi loved debating Ru and Dao, wrote with brilliance, annotated the Changes and Laozi, became Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and died in his twenties.

sentences.zh: 〈弼字輔嗣。

translations.literal: (Bi's courtesy name was Fusi.)
translations.idiomatic: (His courtesy name was Fusi.)

sentences.zh: 何劭為其傳曰：弼幼而察慧，年十餘，好老氏，通辯能言。

translations.literal: He Shao wrote his biography: Bi was perceptive and clever from youth; at over ten he loved the Old Master and was eloquent.
translations.idiomatic: He Shao’s biography says Wang Bi was keen from boyhood; past ten he studied Laozi and argued fluently.

sentences.zh: 父業，為尚書郎。

translations.literal: His father Ye was Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ye was Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時裴徽為吏部郎，弼未弱冠，往造焉。

translations.literal: At the time Pei Hui was Director of the Bureau of Appointments; Bi had not yet reached his capping and went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Hui headed the Bureau of Appointments; Bi, still uncapped, called on him.

sentences.zh: 徽一見而異之，問弼曰：「夫無者誠萬物之所資也，然聖人莫肯致言，而老子申之無已者何？

translations.literal: Hui marveled at him at first sight and asked Bi: "Non-being is truly what the myriad things rely on—yet the sage never speaks of it, while the Old Master expounds non-being without end; why?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui was struck on first meeting and asked: “Non-being grounds all things—yet the sage never names it while Laozi never stops—why?”

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「聖人體無，無又不可以訓，故不說也。

translations.literal: Bi said: "The sage embodies non-being; non-being cannot be taught in words, therefore he does not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Bi answered: “The sage embodies non-being; it cannot be put into doctrine, so he is silent.

sentences.zh: 老子是有者也，故恆言無所不足。

translations.literal: The Old Master deals with being; therefore he always speaks of where non-being falls short."
translations.idiomatic: Laozi speaks from being, so he always shows where non-being is not enough.”

sentences.zh: 」尋亦為傅嘏所知。

translations.literal: Soon he was also recognized by Fu Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gu soon noticed him too.

sentences.zh: 於時何晏為吏部尚書，甚奇弼，嘆之曰：「仲尼稱後生可畏，若斯人者，可與言天人之際乎！

translations.literal: At that time He Yan was Minister of the Bureau of Appointments and thought Bi extraordinary; he sighed: "Confucius called the young awe-inspiring—men like this one may discuss the interface of Heaven and man!"
translations.idiomatic: He Yan was Minister of Appointments and marveled: “Confucius called youth formidable—this man may speak of Heaven and man!”

sentences.zh: 」正始中，黃門侍郎累缺。

translations.literal: During Zhengshi, posts of Palace Attendant were repeatedly vacant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi years Palace Attendant seats stood empty again and again.

sentences.zh: 晏既用賈充、裴秀、朱整，又議用弼。

translations.literal: Yan had already appointed Jia Chong, Pei Xiu, and Zhu Zheng, and also proposed Wang Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had placed Jia Chong, Pei Xiu, and Zhu Zheng and now moved to add Wang Bi.

sentences.zh: 時丁謐與晏爭衡，致高邑王黎於曹爽，爽用黎。

translations.literal: At that time Ding Mi vied with Yan for influence and advanced Wang Li of Gaoyi to Cao Shuang; Shuang employed Li.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Mi rivaled Yan and pushed Wang Li of Gaoyi on Cao Shuang; Shuang took Li.

sentences.zh: 於是以弼補臺郎。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bi was assigned as a clerk of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: So Wang Bi became a clerk at the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 初除，覲爽，請間，爽為屏左右，而弼與論道，移時無所他及，爽以此嗤之。

translations.literal: On his first appointment he had audience with Shuang, requested a private word, and Shuang screened his attendants; yet Bi discussed the Way with him for a long time without touching on anything else, and Shuang mocked him for it.
translations.idiomatic: On first taking office he asked Cao Shuang for a private audience; Shuang cleared the room, but Bi talked only abstruse doctrine for hours—Shuang laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 時爽專朝政，黨與共相進用，弼通俊不治名高。

translations.literal: At the time Shuang monopolized court government; his faction advanced one another; Bi was broadly talented and did not pursue reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang ran the court; his clique promoted each other; Bi had breadth of talent and chased no fame.

sentences.zh: 尋黎無幾時病亡，爽用王沈代黎，弼遂不得在門下，晏為之嘆恨。

translations.literal: Before long Li died of illness after a short time; Shuang replaced Li with Wang Shen, and Bi therefore never entered the inner bureau—Yan lamented it bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Li soon died; Shuang replaced him with Wang Shen, so Bi never reached the inner offices—He Yan rued it.

sentences.zh: 弼在臺既淺，事功亦雅非所長，益不留意焉。

translations.literal: Bi's tenure at the Masters of Writing was shallow, and practical affairs were never his strength; he cared even less.
translations.idiomatic: His time there was brief; administration was not his gift and he cared little.

sentences.zh: 淮南人劉陶善論縱橫，為當時所推。

translations.literal: Liu Tao of Huainan was skilled in Vertical-Horizontal rhetoric and was esteemed in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tao of Huainan mastered coalition rhetoric and was admired.

sentences.zh: 每與弼語，常屈弼。

translations.literal: Whenever he debated with Bi, he regularly got the better of Bi.
translations.idiomatic: In debate he usually got the better of Wang Bi.

sentences.zh: 弼天才卓出，當其所得，莫能奪也。

translations.literal: Bi's natural genius stood supreme; in what he grasped, none could take it from him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Bi’s genius was unmatched—what he saw, no one could wrest away.

sentences.zh: 性和理，樂遊宴，解音律，善投壺。

translations.literal: His nature was harmonious and reasonable; he enjoyed outings and feasts, understood music, and was skilled at pitch-pot.
translations.idiomatic: He was even-tempered, loved feasts and outings, knew music, and excelled at pitch-pot.

sentences.zh: 其論道傅會文辭，不如何晏，自然有所拔得，多晏也，頗以所長笑人，故時為士君子所疾。

translations.literal: In discoursing on the Way he forced terms and phrasing—unlike He Yan—yet in natural insight he surpassed Yan more often than not; he somewhat mocked others with his strengths, so gentlemen of the time resented him.
translations.idiomatic: His philosophy pinned words together—not He Yan’s polish—but he often saw deeper and laughed at others’ weakness, which grated on contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 弼與鍾會善，會論議以校練為家，然每服弼之高致。

translations.literal: Bi was on good terms with Zhong Hui; Hui's discussions took refinement as his hallmark, yet he always acknowledged Bi's lofty reach.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Zhong Hui, whose style was tight logic—yet Hui bowed to Wang Bi’s heights.

sentences.zh: 何晏以為聖人無喜怒哀樂，其論甚精，鍾會等述之。

translations.literal: He Yan held that the sage lacked joy, anger, grief, or pleasure; his argument was very subtle, and Zhong Hui and others repeated it.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan argued sages had no emotions—the thesis was subtle; Zhong Hui echoed it.

sentences.zh: 弼與不同，以為聖人茂於人者神明也，同於人者五情也，神明茂故能體沖和以通無，五情同故不能無哀樂以應物，然則聖人之情，應物而無累於物者也。

translations.literal: Bi disagreed: he held that where the sage surpasses others lies in spirit-like clarity; what he shares with others is the five emotions; spirit-like clarity is abundant, therefore he can embody the harmonious void and penetrate non-being; the five emotions are the same, therefore he cannot be without joy and grief in responding to things—thus the sage's emotions respond to things yet are not tethered to things.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bi disagreed: the sage exceeds common men in luminous spirit but shares the five emotions; that luminosity lets him embody emptiness and touch non-being, yet the shared emotions mean joy and sorrow still answer the world—only his responses leave no entanglement.

sentences.zh: 今以其無累，便謂不復應物，失之多矣。

translations.literal: Now because he is not tethered, you suppose he no longer responds to things—how far you miss the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Because he is untangled you imagine he does not respond—you err deeply.

sentences.zh: 弼注易，潁川人荀融難弼大衍義。

translations.literal: Bi annotated the Changes; Xun Rong of Yingchuan challenged Wang Bi's meaning of the Great Expansion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bi annotated the Changes; Xun Rong of Yingchuan attacked his Great Expansion gloss.

sentences.zh: 弼答其意，白書以戲之曰：「夫明足以尋極幽微，而不能去自然之性。

translations.literal: Bi answered his intent and wrote in jest: "Insight enough to plumb the subtle cannot remove innate nature.
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied playfully: “Vision enough to sound the depths cannot erase innate nature.

sentences.zh: 顏子之量，孔父之所預在，然遇之不能無樂，喪之不能無哀。

translations.literal: Yan Hui's capacity was within what Confucius foresaw—yet meeting him he could not but rejoice, losing him he could not but grieve.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Hui’s measure lay within Confucius’s ken—yet Confucius could not meet him without joy or lose him without grief.

sentences.zh: 又常狹斯人，以為未能以情從理者也，而今乃知自然之不可革。

translations.literal: I used to fault such men as unable to let emotion follow principle—now I know nature cannot be altered.
translations.idiomatic: I once faulted such men for failing to let feeling follow principle—I see now nature cannot be revised.

sentences.zh: 足下之量，雖已定乎胸懷之內，然而隔逾旬朔，何其相思之多乎？

translations.literal: Though your measure is already fixed within your breast, more than ten days apart—why this flood of longing?"
translations.idiomatic: Your mind may be settled—yet ten days apart, why such longing?”

sentences.zh: 故知尼父之於顏子，可以無大過矣。

translations.literal: Thus one knows Confucius toward Yan Hui could be largely without fault.
translations.idiomatic: So Confucius toward Yan Hui was nearly blameless.

sentences.zh: 」弼注《老子》，為之指略，致有理統。

translations.literal: He annotated the Laozi, composing a summary outline that achieved coherent structure.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated the Laozi with a pointed outline, coherent in structure.

sentences.zh: 著道略論，注《易》，往往有高麗言。

translations.literal: He wrote Daolüelun and annotated the Changes, often with lofty, refined formulations.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Daolüelun and glossed the Changes in often sublime language.

sentences.zh: 太原王濟好談，病老、莊，常云：「見弼《易》注，所悟者多。

translations.literal: Wang Ji of Taiyuan loved disputation and faulted Laozi and Zhuangzi, often saying: "Reading Wang Bi's commentary on the Changes, how much I have understood."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji of Taiyuan loved debate and criticized Laozi and Zhuangzi, yet said: “Wang Bi’s Changes commentary opens many doors.”

sentences.zh: 」然弼為人淺而不識物情，初與王黎、荀融善，黎奪其黃門郎，於是恨黎，與融亦不終。

translations.literal: Yet Bi was shallow and did not read human feeling; at first he was friendly with Wang Li and Xun Rong—Li seized his post as Palace Attendant, so he resented Li, and his ties with Rong did not last.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Bi misread people: he befriended Wang Li and Xun Rong until Li took his Palace Attendant post—he hated Li and fell out with Rong.

sentences.zh: 正始十年，曹爽廢，以公事免。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhengshi, Cao Shuang was cast aside; Bi was dismissed on official grounds.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi 10 Cao Shuang fell and Bi lost office on public grounds.

sentences.zh: 其秋遇癘疾亡，時年二十四，無子絕嗣。

translations.literal: That autumn he died of epidemic illness; he was twenty-four sui, without a son, his line ending.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn plague took him at twenty-four, childless—his line ended.

sentences.zh: 弼之卒也，晉景王聞之，嗟嘆者累日，其為高識所惜如此。

translations.literal: When Bi died, Prince Jing of Jin heard of it and lamented for days on end; such was how men of insight mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Sima Shi grieved for days—such high minds prized him.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：易之為書，窮神知化，非天下之至精，其孰能與於此？

translations.literal: Sun Sheng said: As a book, the Changes exhausts spirit and knows transformation—unless one is supremely refined in the realm, who can partake in this?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng said: the Changes plumbs spirit and transformation—who but the finest mind can join it?

sentences.zh: 世之註解，殆皆妄也。

translations.literal: Commentaries of the age are almost all mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly every commentary of the age misses the mark.

sentences.zh: 況弼以傅會之辨而欲籠統玄旨者乎？

translations.literal: How much the more when Bi, with patched-together sophistry, hoped to encompass the arcane purport?
translations.idiomatic: How much less Wang Bi, spinning clever dialectic to bottle the subtle teaching?

sentences.zh: 故其敘浮義則麗辭溢目，造陰陽則妙頤無聞，至於六爻變化，群象所效，日時歲月，五氣相推，弼皆擯落，多所不關。

translations.literal: Thus when he sets forth superficial doctrines, ornate phrases dazzle the eye; when he constructs yin and yang, subtle subtleties go unheard; as for the transformations of the six lines, what the cluster of images models, days and hours, years and months, the five vapors advancing one another—Bi casts them all aside and largely leaves them unconnected.
translations.idiomatic: His airy glosses overflow with ornament; his yin-yang moves are too clever by half; yet the hexagram lines’ turns, the images they mirror, the calendar and the five phases—he tosses them aside and barely touches them.

sentences.zh: 雖有可觀者焉，恐將泥夫大道。

translations.literal: Though there may be something worth viewing in it, I fear it will bog down the great Way.
translations.idiomatic: Parts shine, yet the whole risks clogging the great Way.

sentences.zh: 《博物記》曰：初，王粲與族兄凱俱避地荊州，劉表欲以女妻粲，而嫌其形陋而用率，以凱有風貌，乃以妻凱。

translations.literal: The Bowuzhi states: At first Wang Can and his elder male cousin Kai both took refuge in Jingzhou; Liu Biao wished to give his daughter to Can as wife, but disliked Can's ugly looks and blunt manner; since Kai had bearing and presence, he gave her to Kai instead.
translations.idiomatic: Bowuzhi records that Wang Can and cousin Kai fled to Jingzhou; Liu Biao meant to marry his daughter to Can but found him homely and blunt, while Kai looked the part—so the daughter went to Kai.

sentences.zh: 凱生業，業即劉表外孫也。

translations.literal: Kai begat Ye; Ye was Liu Biao's grandson by his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Kai fathered Ye, Liu Biao’s grandson through his daughter.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕有書近萬卷，末年載數車與粲，粲亡後，相國掾魏諷謀反，粲子與焉，既被誅，邕所與書悉入業。

translations.literal: Cai Yong owned nearly ten thousand scrolls of books; in his final years he loaded several carts for Can; after Can died, the Chancellor's clerk Wei Feng plotted rebellion—Can's son was implicated—and after they were executed, all the books Yong had given passed into Ye's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong’s library—nearly ten thousand scrolls—went by wagon to Wang Can; after Can’s death his son died in Wei Feng’s coup, and the entire legacy landed with Ye.

sentences.zh: 業字長緒，位至謁者僕射。

translations.literal: Ye, courtesy Changxu, rose to Supervisor of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Ye (courtesy Changxu) reached Supervisor of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 子宏字正宗，司隸校尉。

translations.literal: His son Hong, courtesy Zhengzong, was Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong (courtesy Zhengzong) served as Colonel Director of Retainers.

sentences.zh: 宏，弼之兄也。

translations.literal: Hong was Wang Bi's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was Wang Bi’s elder brother.

sentences.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：文帝既誅粲二子，以業嗣粲。〉

translations.literal: The Wei shi Chunqiu states: After Emperor Wen executed Can's two sons, he established Ye as Can's heir.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shi Chunqiu adds that after Wen executed Can’s sons, he made Ye heir to Can.

translations.literal: [Appraisal]
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：王凌風節格尚，毌丘儉才識拔幹，諸葛誕嚴毅威重，鍾會精練策數，咸以顯名，致茲榮任，而皆心大志迂，不慮禍難，變如發機，宗族塗地，豈不謬惑邪！

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Wang Ling's integrity was lofty in manner; Guanqiu Jian's talent and insight stood out; Zhuge Dan was stern, resolute, and august; Zhong Hui was adept at stratagem—all rose to fame and attained such honored posts, yet each harbored vast ambition and impractical schemes, gave no thought to calamity; disaster sprang like releasing a crossbow trigger—whole clans were ground into the earth—were they not deluded!
translations.idiomatic: The historian judges: Wang Ling’s bearing was high; Guanqiu Jian’s talent sharp; Zhuge Dan stern and weighty; Zhong Hui a master of schemes—all rose to glory, yet grand schemes blinded them to ruin; revolt snapped like a bow—clans extinguished—a madness.

sentences.zh: 鄧艾矯然強壯，立功立事，然闇於防患，咎敗旋至，豈遠知乎諸葛恪而不能近自見，此蓋古人所謂目論者也。

translations.literal: Deng Ai was ruggedly robust and accomplished deeds and enterprises, yet was obtuse about guarding against peril—blame and defeat arrived at once; could he perceive Zhuge Ke from afar yet fail to see himself close at hand? This is what the ancients called judging with the eyes alone.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai was tough and accomplished much yet saw no danger coming—disgrace followed fast; he could read Zhuge Ke from a distance but not his own feet—what ancients mocked as “eye-only” judgment.

sentences.zh: 〈《史記》曰：越王無疆與中國爭強，當楚威王時，越北伐齊，齊威王使人說越王，越王不納。

translations.literal: The Records states: King Wujiang of Yue strove with the Central Plain for supremacy; in the time of King Wei of Chu, Yue attacked Qi to the north; King Wei of Qi sent someone to persuade the king of Yue, and the king of Yue would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Records tells how King Wujiang of Yue rivaled the central states; under King Wei of Chu, Yue struck north at Qi; Qi’s king sent an envoy to dissuade Yue, who refused.

sentences.zh: 齊使者曰：「幸也，越之不亡也。

translations.literal: The envoy of Qi said: "How fortunate it is that Yue has not perished."
translations.idiomatic: The Qi envoy answered: “Fortunate indeed—Yue still stands.”

sentences.zh: 吾不貴其用智之如目，目見毫毛而不自見其睫也。

translations.literal: I do not admire using wisdom like eyes—eyes see the tip of an eyelash yet cannot see their own lashes.
translations.idiomatic: “I do not prize wit that works like eyes—eyes see every eyelash yet never their own lashes.”

sentences.zh: 今王知晉之失計，不自知越之過，是目論也。」〉

translations.literal: Now the king knows Jin's mistaken plan yet does not know Yue's fault—that is judging with the eyes alone.
translations.idiomatic: “Today the king sees Jin’s misstep but not Yue’s—that is the blindness of eye-only judgment.”
